# Decision Record

Append-only log of every non-trivial decision made while building Flux, D1 first (2026-07-31)
through D409 (latest). This is the "why" record — what current state looks like and what's next
lives in [roadmap.md](roadmap.md); what each subsystem does lives in the per-topic docs it links
to below. Every `D<N>` reference anywhere in this codebase (READMEs, docstrings, other docs)
points to a heading in this file — the numbering is load-bearing and never reused or reordered,
even when an entry is superseded by a later one.

## Index

_Generated from the `## D<N>.` headings — regenerate it (a one-line script over this file's
own headings) rather than hand-editing. It previously carried a hand-curated Topic column
that stopped being updated at D37 and was 74 entries stale by D111; a column that cannot be
kept true is worse than no column, and each entry names its own topics in its text._

## D1. Target domain: full SoC-level DSE, not DNN-accelerator-only

**Decision.** Flux targets design-space exploration and PPA evaluation for whole SoCs — memory
hierarchy, compute (including but not limited to DNN/NPU compute), interconnect/NoC — not only the
DNN-inference-accelerator niche that ZigZag/Timeloop/Stream occupy. This is broader than either of
the "edge vs datacentre" options [01 §9](landscape.md) originally posed.

**Why.** Stated directly: "design and evaluate and do DSE on EDA projects around SystemOnChip
(memory, architecture, interconnect, compute...) with DSE, PPA and other evaluation and improvement
methods."

**Implications.**
- The **Workload IR** ([04 §3.1](architecture.md)) cannot stay DNN/einsum-only. The affine/einsum core
  remains the flagship, best-supported case — it's what ZigZag/Timeloop/Stream actually give us for
  free — but it now needs a generic "compute kernel" escape hatch alongside the existing
  `data_dependent` one, for non-tensor workloads (protocol engines, control logic, general RTL
  blocks).
- The **Architecture IR** ([04 §3.2](architecture.md)) was already fairly general (memory/compute/interconnect
  component classes) and needs less change.
- **G6 (system-level effects: NoC, chiplets, thermal, off-chip memory)** — [03](gap-analysis.md) had this at
  tier 2, "high value, high cost, phase it." It is now closer to core scope, since NoC/interconnect
  and memory-hierarchy DSE are named explicitly, not an afterthought.
- **Sequencing, not scope-cutting.** Existing validated cost models and calibration data
  (Eyeriss, ENVISION, Gemmini RTL, Stream's three accelerators) are all DNN-accelerator-specific —
  that's where the field's ground truth lives. Recommend still building the Phase 1 spine
  (roadmap.md's Phase 1) against the DNN-accelerator corpus first (fastest path to a working,
  cross-validated contract), then generalising the corpus and cost models outward to general
  compute/interconnect as Phase 5 coverage work already anticipated. The IR should be designed as
  the general-SoC superset from day one so this generalisation is additive, not a rewrite.

---

## D2. Full hardware-generation closure is in scope

**Decision.** v1's closure goal is full generation (Voyager/Gemmini-generator-style: candidate →
generated RTL), not just conformance-checking of supplied RTL.

**Why.** Explicit: "Full HW generation in scope."

**Implications — this supersedes specific lines in [04](architecture.md) and [05](roadmap.md):**
- [04 §11](architecture.md) currently states v1 "does not generate RTL. It *checks conformance* of RTL you
  supply against the model." That line is superseded — generation is in scope.
- [05 §1](roadmap.md)'s build-vs-reuse table lists "RTL generation → **Defer** — Voyager/Gemmini
  territory." Change to **Build/adapt**: adapt existing generators (Gemmini's own generator, CIRCT/
  Chisel-based flows CHIA already wraps) before writing a generator from scratch; add an
  LLM-agent-driven generation strategy once the spine below it is trustworthy.
- **Sequencing matters more here than anywhere else.** Generation must sit *behind* the calibration/
  uncertainty layer (Phase 2) and the independent validity checker (Phase 4, G14), not in front of
  them. CHIA's own documented failure mode — AlphaEvolve exploiting an unenforced assertion to fake
  a speedup — is exactly what happens if an agent is allowed to generate RTL against a cost function
  it can already game. Recommend a new phase, **Phase 3.5 "Generation"**, gated on: (a) Phase 2's
  calibration/escalation machinery live, (b) Phase 4's independent validity checker and holdout
  corpus live for the workload classes being generated. The existing G7 conformance-checking
  machinery becomes the acceptance gate for *every* generated design, not a separate deferred
  feature — generation and conformance-checking are now the same workstream, not sequential ones.
- Add a KPI to [05 §4](roadmap.md): **% of generated designs passing independent validity + RTL
  conformance checking**, target ≥90% before a generation strategy is considered production-usable
  (mirrors the calibrated-CI-coverage KPI already in that table).
- Update the repository layout ([04 §10](architecture.md)): add a top-level `generation/` directory (see
  repo scaffold below).

---

## D3. Domain knowledge as agent context, not ML training

**Decision.** "Training" from [01 §9](landscape.md)'s open question is reinterpreted. DNN training
workloads (forward+backward+optimiser state, PULP-TrainLib territory) **stay out of v1 scope**,
unchanged from the existing docs. What's newly in scope is different: a knowledge/context layer —
specs, standards, protocols (AMBA/AXI, JEDEC memory timing, DDR/HBM, RISC-V ISA manual, PCIe, etc.)
made available to agents as retrievable context, to improve DSE and generation quality.

**Why.** Verbatim: "providing the model with some base knowledge (spec, standards, protocols...)
can improve performance and accuracy, but I would expect this to be more a 'context' thing" — not a
request for the DNN-training cost models [01](landscape.md)/[04](architecture.md) already scope out.

**Implications.**
- No change to the DNN-training exclusion already stated in [01 §9](landscape.md) and [04 §11](architecture.md).
- New component, not previously in [04](architecture.md)'s layering: a **Knowledge/Context layer**. It sits
  alongside L6 Flows rather than inside the evaluator stack proper — it doesn't produce metrics, it
  gives agents (and the generation strategy from D2) grounded context before they propose a
  candidate. Scope: ingest specs/standards/protocol documents, index them for retrieval (RAG-style),
  and expose retrieval the same three-surfaces way as everything else in
  [04 §7.2](architecture.md) (typed function / CHIA node / MCP tool), so a generation or search agent can call
  `knowledge_lookup(query, standard_id)` exactly like it calls `evaluate_design`.
- This is genuinely new work relative to [04](architecture.md)/[05](roadmap.md) — recommend scoping it to start
  alongside Phase 1 (agents will lean on it from the first generation experiment in Phase 3.5
  onward, so it shouldn't be a late add-on), but keep the first corpus small and hand-picked (e.g.
  AMBA AXI4, JEDEC DDR/LPDDR basics, RISC-V unprivileged ISA) rather than attempting broad coverage
  immediately.
- Update the repository layout ([04 §10](architecture.md)): add a top-level `knowledge/` directory (see repo
  scaffold below).

---

## D4. Next step taken now

Scaffold the `flux/` repository skeleton per [04 §10](architecture.md), extended with the `generation/` and
`knowledge/` directories from D2/D3. Directory structure only — no implementation logic. See the
repo root for the result.

---

## D5. CHIA moves to the front, a mixed-grain simulation rung is added, P&R joins the loop

**Decision.** Three changes, after further discussion:

1. **CHIA is now the primary tool, not a Phase 4 afterthought.** Real integration starts
   immediately rather than waiting for the roadmap's original Phase 4 — Flux evaluators become
   actual CHIA library nodes now.
2. **A mixed-grain simulation path**: coarse-grain SystemC for fast functional-correctness and a
   timing pre-check, escalating to the existing cycle-accurate SystemVerilog/Verilator rung for
   authoritative numbers. A new position in [04 §5](architecture.md)'s fidelity ladder, not a replacement
   for anything in it.
3. **P&R (place-and-route) joins the iteration loop**, not just RTL simulation — the escalation
   ladder's synthesis rung (`evaluators/hammer/`) becomes an active target, not a someday one.

The underlying motivation: design + P&R iterations are slow, and the highest-leverage response is
an AI-assisted loop — generate code (with tests and a spec), run it, iterate — with CHIA doing
the orchestration and Flux's evaluator contract supplying every rung of that loop, from fast
coarse-grain checks up through synthesis.

**Why.** Architecture exploration is the focus now, and the actual bottleneck in that loop is
wall-clock: full RTL sign-off and P&R are too slow to iterate against directly, so a fast
correctness pre-check (coarse-grain sim) and an agent-driven codegen loop (CHIA-orchestrated) are
both needed to make iteration fast without giving up the accurate rungs underneath.

**What was verified before deciding this was buildable, not just desirable:**
- **CHIA is real and runs here.** `github.com/ucb-bar/chia` (BSD-3) installs from
  `git+https://github.com/ucb-bar/chia.git` (not on PyPI — that name belongs to an unrelated
  project) and its `@ChiaFunction()` dispatches genuine Ray tasks against a local Ray instance —
  proven by actually running one, not read off its README. `flows/chia_nodes/` now has a real
  `flux_evaluate` node wrapping the same evaluator registry `flux eval` uses, verified against a
  real ZigZag evaluation dispatched through Ray (`tests/integration/test_chia_flux_evaluate_live.py`).
- **CHIA already wraps Hammer** (`chia.vlsi.hammer.HammerNode`) — [05 §1](roadmap.md)'s "already a
  CHIA library node" claim checked out. `evaluators/hammer/` should be a thin adapter over it,
  not a from-scratch subprocess wrapper — but an actual run needs `hammer-shell` (part of the
  full `github.com/ucb-bar/hammer` checkout, not the `hammer-vlsi` PyPI package alone, which also
  conflicts with CHIA's own `pydantic` pin) plus a real PDK, neither available here. Documented in
  `evaluators/hammer/README.md`; still blocked on tooling, not on design.
- **SystemC is real and runs here too** (`libsystemc-dev` 2.3.4, already installed) —
  `evaluators/systemc/` compiles and runs a genuine coarse-grain SystemC model of the same
  `mac_array` design `evaluators/rtl` simulates cycle-accurately, self-checked against the same
  golden reference, and cross-validated to agree *exactly* with real Verilator measurements across
  three array widths (`tests/integration/test_systemc_adapter_live.py`) — the design's schedule is
  fully static, so an exact closed-form cycle count was provable, not merely approximated.
- **Architecture-space DSE, not just mapping search, is real** — `search/architecture/` sweeps
  array width (the axis this decision actually asked to focus on), screens with a real evaluator,
  and escalates the winner through the fidelity ladder (analytic → coarse-grain SystemC →
  cycle-accurate RTL). Verified against real ZigZag/SystemC/RTL for `mlp-gemm0.yaml`: the winner
  selection is correct at every rung, but the analytic screening's absolute number is ~2.9x off
  from real hardware — a further real data point in this repo's own documented ZigZag-
  overestimation finding (`docs/calibration-report.md`), not a defect in the DSE loop, and exactly
  the reason an escalation cascade exists at all. `flows/chia_nodes.ChiaParallelEvaluator` gives
  this same sweep genuine Ray-parallel dispatch with no change to the search logic itself —
  proven concurrent (not sequential-in-disguise) by comparing real wall-clock time against a real
  sequential baseline, not asserted.

**Implications.**
- [04 §5](architecture.md)'s escalation diagram gains a rung between analytic estimates and RTL-sim:
  coarse-grain SystemC. Update the diagram and its surrounding text.
- agent-surface.md's "Flux ships CHIA library nodes" is no longer purely aspirational — one of
  the four named nodes (`flux_evaluate`) exists and is tested; `flux_search`, `flux_calibrate`,
  `flux_conformance_check` do not yet.
- roadmap.md's Phase 4 ("Agentic integration") is partially pulled forward: CHIA-node wiring
  for `flux_evaluate` is done now, ahead of the original phase order. This does **not** change
  D2's generation gate — Phase 3.5 (RTL generation) still waits on Phase 2's calibration/
  escalation machinery (live) and Phase 4's independent validity checker (not yet built). Moving
  `flux_evaluate` earlier doesn't relax that gate; the reward-hacking risk D2 named doesn't shrink
  just because CHIA integration started sooner.
- [05 §1](roadmap.md)'s build-vs-reuse table's Hammer row ("already a CHIA library node") is now
  verified, not just asserted from CHIA's own docs — no change to the row itself, but
  `evaluators/hammer/README.md` records what was actually checked.

---

## D6. Real NoC simulation, 2D and 3D, via Booksim2

**Decision.** Build `evaluators/booksim`, a real Evaluator ABI adapter over
[Booksim2](https://github.com/booksim/booksim2) (Stanford, BSD-3-Clause), covering the k-ary
n-cube network family — 2D mesh/torus and, by adding one more dimension, real 3D NoC topology
simulation. Extend Architecture IR's already-anticipated (but previously unstructured)
`interconnect.noc` placeholder with the fields this needs (`dimensions`, `routing_function`,
`num_vcs`, `vc_buf_size`, `traffic`, `injection_rate`, `packet_size`), additively — no existing
example breaks.

**Why.** D5's pivot named "3D NoC" as an explicit DSE target, but nothing in this repo modelled
NoC topology at all, and neither of the two tools discussed for the job actually does: ZigZag is
domain-locked to regular PE-array + memory-hierarchy cost modeling and doesn't generalise to
packet-routed networks (no notion of a router, contention, or topology graph — confirmed by
re-reading its own translation code, not assumed); CHIA orchestrates and exposes tools as agent-
callable surfaces but models nothing itself. Both are the wrong layer for "what does the NoC
actually do" — that requires a real NoC simulator underneath, which is what this decision adds.

**What was verified before deciding this was buildable, not just desirable:**
- **The first attempt hit a real, unprivileged-environment blocker, and nix fixed it.**
  Booksim2 built almost completely with plain `g++` (every router/allocator/network file) — only
  its config lexer/parser needed `flex`/`bison`, which weren't installed and needed `sudo`
  (password-protected, unavailable). `nix shell nixpkgs#flex nixpkgs#bison` (and, separately,
  `nixpkgs#cmake`/`nixpkgs#libyaml-cpp` for the GPL alternative, Noxim, considered but not used)
  fetched both with no elevated privileges at all — now wired into `flake.nix`'s `.#default`
  shell permanently, not just used ad hoc.
- **3D is a first-class Booksim2 capability, not a hack**: its `KNCube` network reads `n`
  (dimension count) and `k` (radix) straight from config. A real 4x4x4 3D mesh (64 nodes) was
  run alongside a real 8x8 2D mesh (also 64 nodes) — same node count, different dimensionality —
  and gave 4.72 average hops / 54.4-cycle average latency vs. the 2D mesh's 6.20 hops / 61.0
  cycles: the physically correct direction (higher dimensionality shortens network diameter for
  equal node count), not an assumed or hand-picked result
  (`tests/integration/test_booksim_adapter_live.py`).
- **The schema change is additive, checked, not assumed.** Two pre-existing examples
  (`my-npu-v3.yaml`'s `topology: mesh_4x4`, `generic-riscv-soc-v1.yaml`'s `topology: crossbar`)
  use a purely descriptive `noc` block with no `dimensions` — both still validate against the
  extended schema; `evaluators/booksim` raises `NotExpressibleError` for them in Python, not a
  schema-level rejection, matching every other translator's narrow-validation-in-the-adapter
  convention.

**Implications.**
- [04 §10](architecture.md)'s repository layout gains `evaluators/booksim/` alongside the other backends.
- [05 §5's coverage list](roadmap.md) ("NoC model... ongoing") is now partially real: topology and
  routing simulation exist. TSV placement, inter-die vs. in-die link characteristics, and thermal
  — 3D stacking's actual dominant real-world constraint — are still entirely unmodelled; that
  needs 3D-ICE integration layered on top of this, not a change to this adapter.
- Traffic (`traffic`/`injection_rate`/`packet_size`) lives on the *architecture's* `noc` block in
  v0.1, not the workload — Flux's Workload IR has no representation for a statistical packet-
  injection process, only data-dependent tensor computation. A real workload-driven NoC
  evaluator (from an actual multi-tile compute+communication trace) is future work, named
  honestly as a gap in `evaluators/booksim/README.md`, not silently assumed away.

**D6 addendum — actually connecting NoC DSE into CHIA, not just building it standalone.**
Building `evaluators/booksim` did not, on its own, make it reachable through `flux_evaluate`/
`flux_search`: two real gaps had to be closed, found by checking, not assumed fixed by the
adapter existing.
1. `"booksim"` had never been added to `flux_cli.registry`'s backend map — the thing both CHIA
   nodes resolve backend name strings through. Without it, `flux_evaluate("booksim", ...)` would
   raise `ValueError: unknown backend`, regardless of how correct the adapter itself is.
2. `search/architecture`'s DSE engine (`run_architecture_dse`) was hardcoded to
   `generate_width_candidates` — a compute-array-specific generator with no path to NoC topology
   at all. Fixed by generalising the engine's parameter from `widths: list[int]` to
   `candidates: list[...]` (it only ever read `.arch` off each candidate internally, confirmed by
   inspection before refactoring, not assumed) — the exact same engine now drives both a width
   sweep and a NoC topology sweep (`noc_candidates.generate_noc_topology_candidates`), a real
   architectural unification, not a NoC-specific copy of the compute path. `flows/chia_nodes.
   flux_search` gained a `search_kind` parameter selecting which generator builds the candidate
   list before handing it to the same engine.

Verified end to end, not just wired: `tests/integration/test_chia_flux_search_live.py`'s
`test_noc_topology_search_kind_connects_the_real_3d_noc_dse_into_chia` dispatches a real 2D-vs-
3D NoC comparison, screened by real Booksim2 via `ChiaParallelEvaluator("booksim")`, through the
real `flux_search` CHIA node, and gets the physically correct winner (the 3D topology).

## D7. `flows/mcp/`: the third surface, real, over a real MCP client

**Decision.** Build `flows/mcp/`'s `FluxTool`, a real `chia.base.tools.ChiaTool` subclass
exposing `flux_evaluate`/`flux_search` as MCP tools — the last of [04 §7.2](architecture.md)'s "one
definition, three surfaces" (typed Python function, `@ChiaFunction` node, MCP tool) that wasn't
built yet.

**Why.** `flows/chia_nodes/`'s own docstrings already named this as the deliberately-deferred
piece ("The MCP-tool surface is a separate, not-yet-built piece — see `flows/mcp/README.md`" —
written before that README existed). Without it, nothing outside a Python process that already
imports `flux_chia_nodes` can call these nodes — in particular, an LLM agent talking MCP (Claude
Code's `--mcp-config`, or any other MCP client) has no way to reach them at all.

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **Modeled on CHIA's own real examples, not guessed at from docs.** `chia.base.tools.ChiaTool`'s
  actual source (`__init_subclass__`, `setup()`, `__post_init__`) and two of CHIA's own working
  subclasses (`BashTool`, `ChiaToolTemplate`) were read directly from a fresh clone before writing
  `FluxTool` — same `setup()`-registers-tools-via-`self.mcp.add_tool(...)` shape, same
  auto-generated `__init__`.
- **`ArchitectureDSEReport`/`ArchitectureCandidate`/`NocTopologyCandidate` needed `.to_dict()`
  methods that didn't exist before this decision** — an MCP tool's return value must be JSON-safe,
  and neither type was (nested dataclasses, a `Method` enum, a `winner` field whose concrete type
  varies by which candidate generator produced it). Added following the exact convention every
  Evaluator ABI type (`Result`, `Estimate`, `Validity`, ...) already uses, not a one-off shape.
- **A real MCP client, not a local Python call in a trench coat.** `tests/integration/
  test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py` starts a genuine `ray.init()` instance, instantiates
  `FluxTool("flux")` (a real Ray-actor-backed uvicorn server on a real bound port), connects with
  `mcp.ClientSession` + `mcp.client.streamable_http.streamable_http_client` — the exact
  client-side pattern CHIA's own `chia/base/tools/test/test_tool.py` uses against `BashTool` —
  and calls both tools over the real wire protocol (JSON-RPC over streamable HTTP) against a real
  ZigZag backend. One real gotcha found this way and not assumed: FastMCP puts a tool's returned
  `dict` directly in `CallToolResult.structuredContent` with no wrapper key — an initial version
  of the test assumed a `{"result": ...}` wrapper and failed with a `KeyError` until checked by
  actually printing the raw response.
- **`tool.stop()` is checked to actually tear the server down**, not just assumed idempotent from
  reading `ChiaTool.stop()`'s source — a second client call after `stop()` is asserted to raise.

**Implications.**
- [04 §7.2](architecture.md) is updated: the illustrative `@flux_tool` decorator is still unbuilt (no
  code-generation layer exists — each surface is hand-written), but all three surfaces now exist
  for real for `flux_evaluate`/`flux_search`.
- **Scoping limit, stated honestly.** No LLM API credentials are available in this sandbox, so
  this cannot yet be verified with a live `ClaudeCodeLLM.prompt(..., tools=[...])` round trip —
  only with a raw MCP client speaking the real protocol. Any MCP-speaking agent reaches the exact
  same server the same way; the missing piece is credentials to run that specific client, not
  anything in `flows/mcp/` itself.
- `flux_calibrate`/`flux_conformance_check` still don't exist as CHIA nodes, so there is nothing
  yet for a future `FluxTool` extension to wrap for those two.

---

## D8. `flux_calibrate`/`flux_conformance_check`: the last two CHIA nodes, real

**Decision.** Build the remaining two of agent-surface.md's four named CHIA library nodes:
`flux_calibrate` (evaluate, then widen confidence intervals from real calibration residual data
and recompute the escalation recommendation) and `flux_conformance_check` (check whether a fast
declared model's *calibrated* CI actually contains a slower reference evaluator's measurement).
Both are thin `@ChiaFunction()` wrappers, matching every other node here's "adapters, not forks"
convention: `flux_calibrate` composes `flux_calibration.calibrate_result`/
`apply_escalation_policy` (already real, from Phase 3) around the same `flux_cli.registry.
make_evaluator` every other node uses; `flux_conformance_check` calls `flux_calibrate` for the
declared side and a second evaluator for the reference side, then a new
`flux_calibration.check_conformance`. Both are also wired into `flows/mcp/`'s `FluxTool` (D7) as
`{name}_calibrate`/`{name}_conformance_check` MCP tools, completing the four-tool set.

**Why.** These were the two explicitly-named gaps left open by D5 (`flux_evaluate`/`flux_search`)
and D7 (the MCP surface) — docs/agent-surface.md has said "`flux_calibrate` and `flux_conformance_check`
don't exist yet" since D5, and docs/roadmap.md Phase 3.5's exit criterion ("passes RTL conformance
against its declared model within the calibrated uncertainty band") named exactly the check
`flux_conformance_check` now makes real and callable, rather than just aspirational prose.

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **`check_conformance` is new logic, not a rename of something existing.** Searched the repo for
  "conformance" first: the only prior hits were `tests/conformance/`'s cross-*backend*
  IR-interpretation suite (a different meaning — ZigZag vs. Timeloop agreement on the same IR, not
  a declared-vs-reference-evaluator CI check) and `ArchitectureDSEReport.
  escalation_agrees_with_screening` (an absolute-tolerance comparison inside one DSE run, not a
  calibration-CI-based one usable standalone). Neither was reusable as-is; `check_conformance` was
  written new, in `flux_calibration/conformance.py` (the natural home — it's calibration's own "is
  the CI honest" question, not new-strategy or new-CHIA-node logic), with a `ConformanceReport`/
  `MetricConformance` pair of frozen dataclasses following the same `.to_dict()` convention as
  every other ABI-adjacent type (added specifically so `flows/mcp/` can return it as JSON).
- **Real numbers, not synthetic ones, prove the whole chain.** `mlp-gemm0.yaml` through
  `simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml`'s real ZigZag estimate (1554 cycles) vs. its real Verilator RTL
  measurement (529 cycles) is this repo's own pre-existing, already-documented ZigZag-
  overestimation finding (docs/phase1-exit-criterion-report.md) — reused here, not invented, as
  the fixture proving both directions: `flux_conformance_check` correctly reports `ok=False` with
  an empty calibration store (a bare point-estimate CI cannot honestly contain a value 3x away),
  and correctly reports `ok=True` once that exact residual is seeded into the store first (the CI
  widens enough to contain it) — verified by actually running both scenarios against real ZigZag
  and real Verilator, not asserted from the math alone.
  (`tests/integration/test_chia_flux_calibrate_and_conformance_live.py`)
- **A real, if transient, Ray-startup flake was hit and correctly not treated as a bug**: one run
  failed with "node timed out during startup" (a Ray/GCS startup race, not code) and passed clean
  on immediate re-run — noted rather than papered over with a retry-loop in the test itself.

**Implications.**
- agent-surface.md's "two of the four are real" is now "all four are real."
- `flows/mcp/`'s `FluxTool` now exposes all four nodes as MCP tools — see its README for the
  updated tool list.
- **Still open, stated honestly**: `flux_calibrate`/`flux_conformance_check` default
  `calibration_db_path="flux_calibration.db"` (a relative path) rather than resolving a shared,
  well-known store location — same "no default store location convention" gap the CalibrationStore
  itself has always had; a caller must pass an explicit path to actually accumulate records across
  calls. `reference_backend="rtl"` needs `evaluators/rtl`'s Verilator dependency installed and on
  PATH — same v0.1 scope limit (single two-operand `einsum` op, single-spatial-dim architecture)
  every RTL-adjacent adapter here already has.

## D9. The agentic DSE loop, reworked: the credential blocker is not real, but two other gaps are

**Decision.** Reject the standing assumption (repeated across `search/agentic/README.md`,
`flux/README.md`, and this session's own prior turns) that building `search/agentic/` is blocked
on LLM API credentials. It isn't: this sandbox already runs a local **Ollama** server with three
pulled models (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`, `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b`, `gemma4:e2b`), and CHIA ships
`chia.models.ollama.OllamaLLM` specifically for this case — a thin preset over
`OpenAICompatLLM` pointed at `http://localhost:11434/v1`, needing zero API keys (Ollama's own
docstring: *"requires no credentials... we default `api_key` to the conventional dummy value
`'ollama'`"*). Confirmed working end to end with a real `curl` call against `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b`
before relying on it for anything. Reprioritise: build the safety-critical gaps (independent
validity, agent tool access to knowledge/history) *before* the agentic loop itself, then build the
loop for real against Ollama — not defer everything behind an absent credential indefinitely.

**Why.** Every prior mention of `search/agentic/` in this repo cites "no LLM API credentials" as
the reason it's unbuilt. That was true for the paid/gated backends (`claude.py`, `codex.py`,
`bedrock.py`, `vertex.py`, `openai_compat.py` pointed at a real OpenAI endpoint, `antigravity.py`,
`copilot.py`, `opencode.py` — all confirmed to need an account, subscription, or API key by
reading their source) but was never checked against CHIA's own local-inference presets
(`ollama.py`, `vllm.py`), which exist in CHIA precisely so agentic loops can be built and tested
without a paid credential. `chia.base.llm_call.LLMCallBase.prompt(user_message, tools) ->
QueryResult` is the one interface every backend implements — swapping `OllamaLLM` for
`ClaudeCodeLLM` later, if/when real credentials exist, requires no change to calling code, so
building against Ollama now is not throwaway work.

Separately, a full internal gap survey (prompted by re-reading this session's own "agentic DSE"
framing against what's actually built) found the credential question was masking two more
concrete, more important gaps for a *safe* agentic loop:

1. **No independent validity checker exists.** Every evaluator adapter self-reports
   `Validity(ok=True, checker_version="none-v0.1")` — e.g.
   `evaluators/zigzag/src/flux_evaluator_zigzag/adapter.py:251-254`'s own comment: *"No
   independent validity checker exists yet... `ok=True` is a v0.1 placeholder, not a real
   guarantee."* docs/gap-analysis.md G14's anti-reward-hacking principle requires validity computed
   independently of the cost model; today the evaluator grades its own homework. Handing an LLM
   agent a search loop over an ungated cost model is exactly CHIA's own documented AlphaEvolve
   reward-hacking failure mode, reproduced on purpose, if this ships first.
2. **The agent has no tool access to either `knowledge_lookup` or `flux_store`.** Both are real,
   working Python functions (`knowledge/src/flux_knowledge/retrieval.py`,
   `stores/src/flux_store/`), but neither is wired into `flows/chia_nodes/` or `flows/mcp/` —
   confirmed by grep, zero references in either directory. An agentic proposer with no way to
   look up a spec passage or query prior results/holdout status is missing two of the concrete
   capabilities this whole project's framing (docs/agent-surface.md, "AI assisted flow... run some
   stuff and keep iterating") assumes it has.

CHIA's own reference loops (`examples/timing_opt/improve_timing.py`,
`examples/gem5_align/gem5_align_loop.py` — both read in full) confirm the right *shape* for
`search/agentic/`: sample/restore a parent state → **propose** (LLM call with tools) → **evaluate**
(rebuild + simulate) → **observe** (parse results, compare vs. parent) → persist → iterate from a
newly sampled parent. Both hardcode `ClaudeCodeLLM`, so there is no upstream example to copy for
the Ollama substitution specifically, but the interface guarantees it's a drop-in swap.

Also checked and ruled out as reusable: `chia/chipyard/circt.py` is toolchain-wrapping (CIRCT
lowering/build of Chisel a human or LLM already wrote via a bash tool), not spec-to-RTL
generation — confirms `generation/`'s realistic scope is "LLM edits/writes RTL/Chisel source with
a tool, gated by the fidelity ladder," not "generate RTL from a prose spec directly." No Gemmini
wrapper exists in CHIA (grep, zero matches) — docs' "adapt Gemmini's own generator" target would
need to be built from scratch, following the `chia/chipyard/`/`chia/esp/` `ColocatedNode` pattern.

**Reworked priority order:**

1. **Independent validity checker** (small, high-leverage, unblocks everything downstream
   honestly) — a real check computed via a code path that does not share logic with the evaluator
   being checked, not another self-report.
2. **Expose `knowledge_lookup` and a read-only slice of `flux_store`** (`get_result`,
   `find_results`, holdout-safe) as MCP tools — mechanical, follows the exact `FluxTool` pattern
   already built and verified.
3. **`search/agentic/` MVP**: an `OllamaLLM`-backed `Strategy` proposing candidates over an
   already-DSE'd axis (architecture width or NoC topology — both have working candidate
   generators and a proven DSE engine to compare against), calling `flux_evaluate`/`flux_search`/
   `flux_calibrate`/`flux_conformance_check` as its tools, verified against the *proven* optimum
   `search/exhaustive`/`search/annealing` already established (same discipline
   `search/annealing`'s own tests use) — not just "it ran and produced *a* number."
4. **`generation/`** (LLM edits real RTL/Chisel source, gated by 1+2+3 being live) — correctly
   stays gated per docs/roadmap.md's existing Phase 3.5 condition; this decision doesn't change that,
   it only clarifies the realistic shape once unblocked.
5. **Redaction policy, `evaluators/hammer`** — correctly stay deferred: no PDK exists in this
   sandbox to redact, and Hammer is blocked on external tooling (`hammer-shell` + a PDK), not on
   sequencing.

**Implications.**
- docs/roadmap.md's Phase 4 "agentic integration" and Phase 3.5 "generation" sections should read
  against this reordering: the credential line blocking `search/agentic/` is stale and should be
  corrected wherever it's repeated, not preserved as historical narrative (it was never actually
  checked against Ollama/vLLM until now).
- `flux/README.md`'s "genuinely blocked, not skipped by choice: an LLM-driven proposal step needs
  LLM API credentials this environment doesn't have" is now known to be wrong and needs
  correcting the next time `search/agentic/` work lands.
- Model choice for the MVP: `qwen2.5-coder:7b` (coder-tuned, better structured-output/parameter-
  proposal reliability than the general-purpose `gemma4:e2b`) as the primary target,
  `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b` for fast iteration during harness development — both already pulled, no
  additional setup needed.

---

## D10. A real independent validity checker (D9's priority 1), built

**Decision.** Build `validity/` (`flux-validity`): two checks computed from the Workload/
Architecture IR and a `Result`'s reported metrics, sharing no code with any evaluator adapter —
`check_declared_constraints` (Architecture IR's own `constraints` block — `area_mm2`/`tdp_w`/...
`max`/`min` bounds — against the matching reported metric) and `check_physical_validity` (a
first-principles roofline: no evaluator can report `latency_cycles` below
`total_macs / lanes`, computed purely from IR, not from any cost model). Wire both into a new
fifth CHIA node, `flux_check_validity` (`flows/chia_nodes/`), which evaluates through a named
backend and *merges* the evaluator's own self-reported `Validity` with the independent finding —
and into `flows/mcp/`'s `FluxTool` as a fifth MCP tool, `{name}_check_validity`.

**Why.** D9 identified this as priority 1, ahead of building `search/agentic/` itself: every
evaluator adapter has shipped `Validity(ok=True, checker_version="none-v0.1")` since Phase 1 — a
self-report, not docs/gap-analysis.md G14's "computed independently of the cost model" guarantee. Handing
an LLM agent (even a free local one, per D9) a search loop over an ungated cost model first would
be CHIA's own documented reward-hacking failure mode, reproduced on purpose. The Architecture IR
schema already had a slot for exactly this (`constraints`, docs/ir.md: "the validity checker
enforces them even when the cost model has no opinion") that nothing had evaluated until now.

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **The roofline bound is this repo's own already-verified arithmetic, not a new invention.**
  docs/phase1-exit-criterion-report.md had already computed "the theoretical compute-bound
  minimum for this workload on an 8-wide array is `4*32*32/8 = 512` cycles" by hand, to explain
  why Timeloop's mapper (512, exact) beat ZigZag's LOMA search (1554). `check_physical_validity`
  formalises exactly that calculation as a real, callable, tested function — and running it
  against all three real backends confirmed the same story empirically: ZigZag (1554) and real
  Verilator RTL (529) both clear the bound comfortably, and real Timeloop hits the bound *exactly*
  (512), confirming the check's `>=` boundary accepts an exact match rather than only strictly-
  above (`tests/integration/test_chia_flux_check_validity_live.py`).
- **The constraints check was proven against a real "nothing to check" case and a real "something
  to check" case, not just synthetic fixtures.** `simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml` declares `area_mm2 max=
  4.0`/`tdp_w max=2.0`; real ZigZag and real RTL neither compute `area_mm2` nor `power_w`, so the
  check honestly reports `checked=0/2` for both — not a silent pass pretending to have verified
  something it never looked at. Real Timeloop *does* compute `area_mm2` (0.0 for this reference
  architecture, itself a known gap — Timeloop's area model isn't meaningfully wired up for it),
  so the check reports `checked=1/2` — a real constraint genuinely evaluated, confirmed by
  actually running Timeloop via Docker, not assumed from reading the adapter's code.
- **The merge preserves, rather than discards, an evaluator's own real self-check.** `flux_check_
  validity("rtl", ...)`'s returned `Validity.checker_version` contains both
  `"rtl-testbench-self-check-v0.1"` (evaluators/rtl's own comparison against a Python golden
  reference — a real, if not fully independent, check) and the new `"roofline-v0.1"`/
  `"constraints-v0.1"` — `ok` is `False` if either side finds a problem, `violations` is the
  union. Deciding to merge rather than replace was a deliberate choice, checked against what
  would be lost by replacing: RTL/SystemC's internal self-check is genuinely informative and
  discarding it to make room for the new check would be a regression, not a fix.
- **17 unit tests + 6 live-backend integration tests + 2 MCP-tool tests, all passing**, including
  the `arch=None` case (neither check has an architecture to read — both must report
  "not applicable" honestly, confirmed `ok=True` in that case rather than defaulting to a
  meaningless pass or an unwarranted failure).

**Implications.**
- `flows/README.md`'s claim that flows/ "includes the independent validity checker... that gate
  generation/" is corrected: it now actually does, for the metrics/constraints this v0.1 scope
  covers.
- Still narrow, stated honestly: `check_physical_validity` only bounds `latency_cycles`, and only
  for the same single-two-operand-einsum-op / single-spatial-dim-architecture scope every other
  RTL-adjacent component in this repo already uses — not a new restriction, but real coverage,
  not universal coverage. `check_declared_constraints` never checks `"thermal"` constraints (no
  model exists) and compares against `Estimate.value` only, not `ci_high` (doesn't yet account
  for calibrated uncertainty at a boundary).
- D9's priority 2 (expose `knowledge_lookup`/`flux_store` as MCP tools) and priority 3
  (`search/agentic/` MVP against Ollama) remain the next steps in that reworked order.

---

## D11. `knowledge_lookup`/`flux_store` as agent-callable tools (D9's priority 2), built

**Decision.** Four more CHIA nodes, wrapping code that already existed but had no CHIA-node or
MCP-tool surface: `flux_knowledge_lookup` (wraps `flux_knowledge.knowledge_lookup`, real since
D3), `flux_get_result`/`flux_find_results` (wrap `flux_store.ResultStore`'s existing query
methods, real since Phase 1/2), and `flux_list_public_corpus` — which calls
`CorpusStore.public_entries()` **only**, and does not accept or forward an
`acknowledge_holdout_access` parameter at all, so an agent using this tool cannot reach the
holdout partition regardless of what it asks for. All four are wired into `flows/mcp/`'s
`FluxTool` as a fifth-through-ninth MCP tool.

**Why.** D9 named this gap directly: "an agentic proposer with no way to look up a spec passage
or query prior results/holdout status is missing two of the concrete capabilities this whole
project's framing... assumes it has." Both `knowledge_lookup` and `flux_store` were real,
tested, working Python since well before this decision — the gap was purely in the agent-facing
surface, confirmed by grep (zero references to either in `flows/chia_nodes/`/`flows/mcp/` before
this record).

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **`Chunk`/`RetrievedChunk` (knowledge) and `CorpusEntry` (stores) needed real `.to_dict()`
  methods that didn't exist before this decision** — same reasoning as D7/D8/D10: an MCP tool's
  return value must be JSON-safe, and none of these dataclasses were (`CorpusEntry.partition` is
  a `CorpusPartition` enum). Added following the same convention every other ABI-adjacent type
  uses. `ResultStore.get_result`/`find_results` already returned plain dicts — no change needed
  there, confirmed by reading the store's own docstring ("deliberately decoupled from any one
  evaluator's in-memory types") before assuming serialization work was required.
- **`flux_knowledge_lookup` was run against the real, live BM25 index over the real ingested
  RISC-V corpus, not a synthetic fixture** — `flux_knowledge_lookup("fence instruction memory
  ordering", "riscv-unpriv", k=3)` returns real chunks from `zicsr.adoc` with positive BM25
  scores. `flux_get_result`/`flux_find_results` were run against a real `ResultStore` populated
  by a real ZigZag evaluation (145.0 cycles, `mlp-gemm0.yaml` with no explicit architecture — the
  same pinned number `test_chia_flux_evaluate_live.py` already checks), round-tripped through a
  temp SQLite file.
- **`flux_list_public_corpus`'s holdout safety was checked structurally, not just
  behaviourally**: run against the real `corpus/` directory, it returns exactly the three public
  entries (`mlp-gemm0-simple-npu-1d-v{1,2,3}`) and never the real fourth, held-out entry
  (`...-v4`, docs/calibration-report.md's Finding 3). Beyond that behavioural check, `inspect.
  signature(flux_list_public_corpus)`'s parameters were asserted to equal exactly `{"corpus_
  root"}` — proving there is no `acknowledge_holdout_access`-shaped escape hatch reachable by an
  agent, not merely that the current implementation happens not to use one.
- **A found gotcha, not assumed away**: FastMCP wraps `list[...]`/`X | None`-returning tools in a
  `{"result": ...}` envelope in `structuredContent` — different from the no-wrapper-key behaviour
  D7 found for plain-`dict`-returning tools. Found by printing the raw response before writing
  test assertions, the same discipline D7 used for the first gotcha.
- **18 new unit/integration tests, all passing** (110 total across this record's affected test
  files run together), including a real MCP-client round trip for all four new tools.

**Implications.**
- All nine `flux_chia_nodes` functions now have all three of docs/agent-surface.md's surfaces.
- D9's priority 3 (`search/agentic/` MVP against a real local Ollama model) is the next step in
  the reworked order — it now has a full real tool surface to call: evaluate, search, calibrate,
  check conformance, check validity, look up specs, and query prior results/public corpus.
- Still open: no "put" tool exists for `flux_store` (storing a result is left to the search/
  generation loop that produced it, not exposed as something an agent calls directly) — a
  deliberate scope limit, not an oversight, matching this tool surface's "read-only agent access"
  framing.

---

## D12. `search/agentic/` MVP (D9's priority 3), built — and a real limitation found along the way

**Decision.** Build `search/agentic/`'s `AgenticMappingStrategy`: a third independent
implementation of docs/search.md's `Strategy` Protocol (`propose`/`observe`/`done`), over the
exact same flat-mapping space `search/exhaustive`/`search/annealing` already search, driven by
one real LLM call per round instead of enumeration or simulated-annealing perturbation. Stays
CHIA-agnostic (docs/architecture.md's L5/L6 layering): `LLMProposer` is a one-method Protocol
(`propose(prompt: str) -> str`); any real backend is adapted onto it by the caller, not imported
by the package. Verified with `chia.models.ollama.OllamaLLM` (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`, D9's real,
credential-free local model) against real ZigZag, validated against exhaustive search's *proven*
true optimum (1554 cycles for `mlp-gemm0.yaml` + `simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml`) the same way annealing
already is.

**Why.** D9 named this as priority 3, after the safety-critical validity checker (D10) and agent
tool access to knowledge/history (D11) were live. With those in place, the last named gap in the
reworked plan was the agentic loop itself.

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **Autonomous multi-turn tool-calling was tried first, and found not to work reliably in this
  sandbox — this is the one significant real limitation this record needs to state plainly.**
  `chia.models.ollama.OllamaLLM.prompt(user_message, tools=[flux_tool])` was tested against a
  real running `FluxTool` MCP server (the exact tool surface D7–D11 built). Both `qwen2.5-coder:7b`
  and `gemma4:e2b` report Ollama's `tools` capability (`ollama show`), but neither model actually
  populates a structured `tool_calls` field via Ollama's native `/api/chat` or its OpenAI-
  compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint (Ollama 0.20.4) — both echo a tool-call-shaped JSON
  blob as plain assistant *text* instead. Confirmed with a minimal textbook `get_weather`
  function-calling example (no Flux code involved at all) before concluding this was a real,
  reproducible environment limitation and not a fluke of one prompt or one tool schema. This is
  not a CHIA bug — `OpenAICompatLLM`'s tool-dispatch code is correct; the model/Ollama-version
  combination simply never emits the field that code depends on.
- **Given that, a harness-driven propose/observe loop was chosen deliberately, not by default** —
  the same shape `search/annealing` already uses (one LLM call, one evaluation, per round), which
  only requires the model to emit one JSON object per turn. Separately confirmed via a raw
  `curl` against Ollama's `/api/generate` with `format: "json"` forced (4/4 and 4/4 valid,
  schema-matching JSON across two models) that this narrower ask is one both models satisfy
  reliably — `CHIA`'s `OllamaLLM.prompt()` doesn't expose forced-JSON mode, so the real
  free-text behaviour was tested too (not assumed to match the forced-mode result), and two real
  failure modes surfaced: markdown code-fence wrapping, and — the more interesting one — a model
  dropping the dimension it chose as `spatial_dim` out of `temporal_order` entirely (producing a
  2-element list for a 3-dimension problem, since the spatial dim's own remainder still runs
  temporally too). Both are parsed/validated explicitly (`_parse_llm_proposal`, raising
  `InvalidLLMProposal` naming the exact reason) with a uniformly-random-unvisited fallback,
  recorded via `EvaluatedCandidate.used_fallback`/`fallback_reason` — never silently substituted.
- **The proven-optimum assertion is deterministic despite a real LLM in the loop, not flaky** —
  worth spelling out since it's a subtle point: the 18-combination space is small enough that the
  fallback-to-unvisited behaviour guarantees every combination gets visited exactly once within
  18 rounds, regardless of how many rounds the LLM itself contributes usefully. Running for
  exactly `max_iterations=18` therefore guarantees full coverage of the same space
  `test_search_exhaustive_live.py` covers, making "found 1554.0 cycles" a certainty, not a hope.
  What *is* a genuine, non-guaranteed test of the LLM's real contribution — and passed — is
  `fallback_count < 18`: proof the model produced at least one valid, useful, non-repeating
  proposal on its own, not that the deterministic fallback net did all 18 evaluations alone.
- **A second real number was corrected by actually running it, not assumed from memory**: the
  first version of the live test asserted `skipped_not_expressible == 0`; the real run reported 6.
  Checking `test_search_exhaustive_live.py`'s own already-established real result confirmed the
  correct number is 6 (the candidates that spatially split `B`, hitting the documented
  zigzag-dse==3.8.5 size-1-temporal-loop bug) — the assertion was fixed to match reality, the
  same discipline this whole record has used throughout (verify, don't guess, and when a guess is
  wrong, fix the guess, not the finding).
- **49 tests pass together in a fresh venv** (16 new unit tests against a scripted fake
  `LLMProposer`, 2 new live tests against real Ollama + real ZigZag, plus the pre-existing
  exhaustive/annealing suites over the same space, run side by side to confirm no regression).

**Implications.**
- All three `Strategy` Protocol implementations over the flat-mapping space
  (`search/exhaustive`, `search/annealing`, `search/agentic`) are now real, independently
  verified, and mutually cross-checked against the same proven optimum.
- `search/agentic/README.md` and `flows/mcp/README.md` are corrected: the credential blocker was
  already known to be false (D9); this decision adds the further, more specific finding that
  *autonomous tool-calling* specifically doesn't work yet in this sandbox, which a live-agent MCP
  round trip (still unbuilt) would run straight into if attempted with the current Ollama
  version/models. A future attempt should either wait for improved Ollama tool-call support, try
  a different local model, or use one of the gated cloud backends (Claude/OpenAI/etc.) that CHIA's
  own reference loops (`improve_timing.py`, `gem5_align_loop.py`) actually use for this reason.
- No CHIA node/MCP tool wraps `run_agentic_search` itself — an external driver (the live test) is
  enough for this MVP; wrapping the loop as a single dispatchable Ray task is future work if a
  real use case needs it.
- This strategy only covers the flat-mapping axis, the same one `search/exhaustive`/`annealing`
  already do — no LLM-driven architecture-width or NoC-topology search yet.

---

## D13. LLM-driven architecture-width search, extending D12's pattern to a second axis

**Decision.** Build `AgenticArchitectureWidthStrategy` (`search/agentic/architecture_strategy.py`):
a second axis for this package's agentic approach, alongside D12's flat-mapping one, over the
architecture-width axis `flux_search_architecture`'s `run_architecture_dse` engine already
unifies with the NoC-topology axis (docs/decisions.md D6 addendum). Reuses
`generate_width_candidates` directly (adapters, not forks) — this module only decides *which*
width to propose next and when to stop. Refactored `LLMProposer`/`InvalidLLMProposal` out of
`strategy.py` into a shared `llm.py` module so both axes' strategies use the identical interface
and parsing-failure vocabulary, rather than each redefining it.

**Why.** After D12 proved the harness-driven `LLMProposer` pattern works end to end for one axis
(flat mapping), the natural next question — asked directly, not assumed — was whether that same
pattern generalises to a structurally different search space, or whether it was accidentally
specific to the mapping representation. Reusing `generate_width_candidates` (a different existing
candidate generator, already proven inside `run_architecture_dse`) is the test of that.

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **The real landscape was checked first, and it changes the honest framing of what this
  demonstrates.** `test_architecture_dse_live.py` already established real ZigZag numbers for
  `mlp-gemm0.yaml` across widths {4, 8, 16, 32}: 3106 / 1554 / 778 / 263 cycles — strictly
  monotonic, "wider is always faster," confirmed by running it again for width=32 specifically
  (not previously tested) before designing around it. Unlike D12's mapping axis — whose
  (spatial_dim, temporal_order) landscape is genuinely non-obvious enough that it needed
  exhaustive search to establish the true optimum in the first place — there is no clever
  inversion for an LLM to discover here. This record says so plainly rather than overclaiming
  "the LLM found the best design": what's actually demonstrated is that the harness pattern
  (one JSON proposal per round, parsed/validated, fallback-on-failure) generalises cleanly to a
  different candidate representation and a different existing candidate generator, not that the
  model exhibited non-trivial judgement on this particular axis.
- **The same deterministic-despite-a-real-LLM argument D12 established still holds, checked
  freshly for this axis**: running for exactly `max_iterations=4` (the full candidate set)
  guarantees every width is tried regardless of the LLM's own contribution, via the same
  fallback-to-unvisited mechanism — making "found 263.0 cycles" a certainty. `fallback_count < 4`
  (verified true in the real run) is the one non-guaranteed, genuine signal that
  `qwen2.5-coder:7b` contributed real, valid, non-repeating proposals.
- **A real edge case caught and handled, not assumed away**: Python's `bool` is an `int` subclass,
  so a naive `isinstance(width, int)` check would silently accept `{"width": true}` as
  `width=1` — excluded explicitly (`isinstance(width, bool) or ...`) and covered by a unit test,
  found by thinking through the parser's actual type-checking logic before shipping it, not by
  hitting it in a real LLM response.
- **31 new unit tests + 2 new live tests, 86 total passing together** in a fresh venv alongside
  the pre-existing exhaustive/annealing/agentic-mapping suites, confirming the `llm.py` refactor
  didn't regress D12's mapping-axis strategy.

**Implications.**
- Both axes `flux_search_architecture` unifies (`architecture_width`, `noc_topology` — D6
  addendum) now have a real candidate-generator path; only `noc_topology` lacks an LLM-driven one
  so far (real Booksim2 is slower per-evaluation than ZigZag, making it a reasonable next
  extension but not done here).
- No CHIA node/MCP tool wraps either agentic strategy yet — same scope note D12 made, unchanged.
- The honest "no inversion to discover" framing above should guide expectations for any future
  agentic axis: check the real landscape first, and report what the LLM actually contributes
  (efficient coverage, representation-generalisation) rather than assuming every axis has a
  non-obvious optimum worth "discovering."

---

## D14. LLM-driven NoC-topology search — the third and last axis, and a real Booksim2 bug found

**Decision.** Build `AgenticNocTopologyStrategy` (`search/agentic/noc_strategy.py`): the third
axis for this package's agentic approach, closing out D13's own "only NoC-topology lacks an
LLM-driven one" note. Reuses `generate_noc_topology_candidates` directly. Candidate set
restricted to `topology="mesh"` at a fixed 64-node total, varying dimensionality: `[64]` (1D),
`[8,8]` (2D), `[4,4,4]` (3D), `[2,2,2,2,2,2]` (6D).

**Why `torus` is excluded, found while building this, not assumed away.** Real end-to-end testing
against `evaluators/booksim`'s real translator (which supports both `mesh` and `torus`) surfaced
a genuine, separate bug: a `torus` candidate fails inside Booksim2 itself with `"Invalid routing
function: dor_torus"` — the adapter's default `routing_function="dor"` has no valid torus-routing
mapping in the Booksim2 config it generates. This is an `evaluators/booksim` bug, out of scope
for an agentic-search module to fix; `valid_variants` here deliberately excludes `torus` rather
than silently swallowing the failure or scope-creeping into fixing an unrelated adapter. Logged
here so it isn't lost: `evaluators/booksim`'s `routing_function` handling needs a real fix before
`torus` candidates are usable anywhere in this repo.

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **The real landscape was measured first, including one point never previously tested.** `1D=
  [64]`, `2D=[8,8]`, and `3D=[4,4,4]` build on `evaluators/booksim`'s own already-established
  2D-vs-3D finding; `6D=[2,2,2,2,2,2]` was run for the first time while designing this module's
  candidate set. Real Booksim2 measurements: 203.433 / 60.9617 / 54.3862 / 51.8472 cycles —
  strictly decreasing with dimensionality (shorter network diameter at fixed node count, the same
  physical direction already established, now confirmed to continue past 3D). Same honest framing
  D13 established: this is a monotonic axis, no inversion to discover — what's demonstrated is
  the harness pattern's third generalisation, this time against a real, slower-per-evaluation
  simulator (Booksim2) rather than an analytic one.
- **Booksim2's determinism was checked directly, not assumed, before choosing an exact-value vs.
  margin-based assertion.** The same NoC config was evaluated three times in a row; all three
  returned exactly 60.9617 — `evaluators/booksim`'s adapter sets no explicit seed, but Booksim2's
  own default is fixed, so the live test asserts an exact known minimum (51.8472) rather than a
  loose margin, once that determinism was confirmed empirically.
- **The same deterministic-despite-a-real-LLM argument D12/D13 established still holds**: running
  for exactly `max_iterations=4` (the full candidate set) guarantees every variant is tried via
  the fallback-to-unvisited mechanism, making "found 51.8472 cycles" a certainty;
  `fallback_count < 4` (verified true in the real run) is the genuine, non-guaranteed signal that
  `qwen2.5-coder:7b` contributed real, valid, non-repeating proposals — this time against a
  three-field JSON schema (`topology` + `dimensions` list) rather than the simpler single-field
  schemas the other two axes use.
- **14 new unit tests (including one asserting a proposed `torus` variant correctly falls back,
  not silently accepted) + 2 new live tests against real Ollama and real Booksim2, 45 total
  passing together** across all three agentic strategies in a fresh venv.

**Implications.**
- All three axes this repo's DSE engines cover (flat-mapping via `search/exhaustive`'s
  representation; architecture-width and NoC-topology via `run_architecture_dse`'s unification,
  D6 addendum) now have a real, independently-verified LLM-driven candidate generator alongside
  their non-agentic ones.
- `evaluators/booksim`'s `torus`-routing bug is a real, open item this record surfaces but does
  not fix — worth a dedicated follow-up, not bundled into agentic-search work.
- No CHIA node/MCP tool wraps any of the three agentic strategies yet — same scope note D12/D13
  made, unchanged; a real use case would need one dispatched as a single Ray task.

---

## D15. `evaluators/booksim`'s torus-routing bug, fixed (the follow-up D14 flagged)

**Decision.** Fix the real bug D14 found and deliberately didn't fix: `architecture_translator.py`
defaulted `routing_function` to `"dor"`, which crashes Booksim2 itself for `topology="torus"`
(`"Invalid routing function: dor_torus"`). Changed the default to `"dim_order"` — a valid Booksim2
routing-function alias for *both* `mesh` and `torus` — and added an explicit, narrow check that
raises `NotExpressibleError` in Python for the one specific known-bad combination
(`routing_function="dor"` with `topology="torus"`), rather than letting it reach Booksim2 and
crash there. Updated the two real example fixtures (`noc-mesh-2d-v1.yaml`, `noc-mesh-3d-v1.yaml`)
from `dor` to `dim_order` — the exact path a torus variant generated from them (e.g. via
`generate_noc_topology_candidates`) would otherwise have inherited the broken value from.

**Why.** D14 explicitly logged this as a real, open item rather than bundling an unrelated fix
into agentic-search work. Once that work was done, this was the natural, well-scoped next step:
small, concrete, already root-caused, and it unblocks `torus` — a real capability
`_VALID_TOPOLOGIES` already claimed to support but never actually worked — for anything in this
repo that wants it (including a future extension of `search/agentic/`'s NoC-topology strategy).

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper:**
- **The actual root cause was found by reading Booksim2's own source, not guessed at.**
  `trafficmanager.cpp:100` builds the real routing-function lookup key as
  `config.GetStr("routing_function") + "_" + config.GetStr("topology")`. `routefunc.cpp`'s
  `gRoutingFunctionMap` registers both `"dor_mesh"` and `"dim_order_mesh"` as aliases for the same
  mesh dimension-order routing function, but only `"dim_order_torus"` (and `"dim_order_ni_torus"`,
  `"dim_order_bal_torus"`) for torus — no `"dor_torus"` alias exists at all. This is why `"dor"`
  had silently worked for every mesh candidate this repo had ever run (including D6's original
  2D-vs-3D mesh comparison) and only broke the moment a torus candidate was tried.
- **The fix was proven safe for the existing case before being applied**: the same real 8x8 mesh
  config was evaluated once with `routing_function="dor"` and once with `"dim_order"` — both gave
  the identical real latency, 60.9617 cycles — confirming `"dim_order"` is a true drop-in
  replacement for mesh, not a behavioural change, before changing the default or the example
  fixtures.
- **The fix was proven to actually unblock torus, not just stop crashing**: a real torus 8x8
  candidate with `routing_function="dim_order"` now evaluates successfully — 56.564 cycles,
  5.00662 average hops, genuinely fewer hops than the equivalent mesh (6.20265) — the physically
  correct direction (torus's wraparound links shorten paths relative to mesh at the same radix
  and dimension count), not merely "no longer crashes."
- **9 real live tests now pass against real Booksim2** (up from 6): three new ones — a torus
  candidate evaluating successfully via the fixed default, a real torus-vs-mesh hop-count
  comparison, and confirmation that the exact previously-crashing combination
  (`routing_function="dor"` + `topology="torus"`) now fails cleanly in Python with a clear message
  instead of crashing the simulator. Plus 3 new unit tests (14 total in that file) covering the
  new default, the new validation, and that `"dor"` remains valid for `mesh` (the fix is narrow,
  not a blanket rejection of `"dor"`).

**Implications.**
- `_VALID_TOPOLOGIES = ("mesh", "torus")` in `architecture_translator.py` is now honestly true for
  both entries — before this record, `torus` was accepted by the Python-level validation but
  unusable in practice.
- The "still open" list entry this bug had is now resolved; removed from that section.
- A future extension of `search/agentic/`'s NoC-topology strategy could now include `torus`
  candidates alongside `mesh` — not done here (D14's own scope was the strategy itself, not
  re-verifying it after an unrelated bugfix), but the blocker named in D14's README is gone.

---

## D16. `AgenticNocTopologyStrategy` extended to mesh+torus — and a genuinely non-monotonic axis found

**Decision.** Extend the NoC-topology candidate set D14 built to include `torus` now that D15
fixed the bug forcing its exclusion: a combined mesh+torus, four-dimensionality (1D/2D/3D/6D),
equal-64-node candidate set (8 candidates total). No code change to `AgenticNocTopologyStrategy`
itself was needed — `valid_variants` was always caller-supplied and topology-agnostic; this is a
docs/tests/live-test update, not a new mechanism.

**Why.** D15's own implications section named this as the natural next step, and D16 exists to
actually check what including `torus` does to the search problem rather than assume it's more of
the same.

**What was verified before deciding this was done, not just wired on paper — and the actual
finding, which reframes this whole axis:**
- **The combined 8-candidate space is genuinely non-monotonic — the first non-trivial optimum
  found on any agentic axis in this repo.** Real Booksim2 measurements: mesh gives 203.433 /
  60.9617 / 54.3862 / 51.8472 cycles across 1D/2D/3D/6D (D14's own already-established, strictly
  monotonic numbers); torus gives 187.093 / 56.564 / **49.5155** / 51.9412 across the same four
  dimensionalities. Torus's 3D point is the *global* minimum — lower than torus's own 6D point,
  even though 6D torus has marginally *fewer* average hops than 3D torus (4.03 vs 4.05, confirmed
  by reading `hops_average` directly, not inferred from latency alone). Neither "more dimensions
  is better" (D14's own finding, still true for mesh, but not for torus past 3D) nor "torus always
  beats mesh at equal dimensionality" (true for every dimensionality *except* this isn't why 3D
  wins — 3D torus beats 6D torus too) predicts the actual optimum alone. This is the first agentic
  axis in this repo where an LLM proposer has something genuinely non-obvious to find, unlike
  D13's architecture-width axis or D14's mesh-only NoC axis.
- **The new minimum was checked for determinism the same way D14's was**, before pinning an exact
  assertion: the same torus 3D config was evaluated three times in a row, all three gave
  49.5155 cycles.
- **The live test's "found the true optimum" assertion remains deterministic despite a real LLM
  in the loop**, via the same argument D12/D13/D14 established: running for exactly
  `max_iterations=8` (the full 8-candidate space) guarantees every variant is visited via the
  fallback-to-unvisited mechanism; `fallback_count < 8` (verified true in the real run) is the
  separate, genuine, non-guaranteed signal that `qwen2.5-coder:7b` contributed real, valid,
  non-repeating proposals — now over a larger, more genuinely interesting search space than any
  previous agentic axis.
- **2 new unit tests + the live test rewritten for the 8-candidate space, 46 total agentic unit
  tests passing together**, confirming the `torus`-specific rejection test from D14 (now
  generalised to "any variant outside the caller's valid set falls back," not
  "torus specifically") and a new test confirming a `torus` proposal is accepted directly, with no
  fallback, once it's actually in `valid_variants`.

**Implications.**
- `search/agentic/`'s NoC-topology strategy now searches the same real 8-candidate space
  `evaluators/booksim/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` describe, not a `mesh`-only subset.
- The "no non-obvious inversion to discover" honesty framing D13/D14 established for the width
  and NoC axes needs a caveat now: it was true for the *mesh-only* NoC axis specifically. Adding
  `torus` changes the shape of the problem — a reminder that "check the real landscape" (D13's own
  stated principle) has to be re-applied whenever a candidate set's scope actually changes, not
  assumed to carry over from a narrower version of the same axis.

---

## D17. `search/agentic/`'s three strategies wired as real CHIA nodes and MCP tools — closing the gap D12/D13/D14 each flagged

**Decision.** Build `flows/chia_nodes/src/flux_chia_nodes/agentic.py` with three
`@ChiaFunction()` nodes — `flux_agentic_mapping_search`, `flux_agentic_architecture_search`,
`flux_agentic_noc_search` — each a thin dispatch wrapper around the matching `run_agentic_*`
function from `search/agentic/`, backed by a real `chia.models.ollama.OllamaLLM` proposer
(`qwen2.5-coder:7b` by default, D9's zero-credential local Ollama). Then expose all three as real
MCP tools on `FluxTool` (`flows/mcp/src/flux_mcp/tool.py`), bringing the tool's total from nine to
twelve.

**Why.** D12, D13, and D14 each independently flagged the same gap in their own Implications
sections: "No CHIA node/MCP tool wraps [this strategy] yet." All three strategies were fully
built, verified against proven optima, and CHIA-agnostic by design (`LLMProposer` is a plain
Protocol) — the only missing piece was the dispatch surface itself, exactly like D6/D7 did for
`flux_evaluate`/`flux_search`/`flux_calibrate`/`flux_conformance_check`.

**What was verified before deciding this was done:**
- **In-process calls to all three new CHIA nodes**, against real Ollama + real ZigZag (mapping,
  architecture-width) and real Ollama + real Booksim2 (NoC), in a new
  `tests/integration/test_chia_flux_agentic_search_live.py` (4 tests). The architecture-width
  test reuses D13's proven optimum (width=32, 263.0 cycles) as a deterministic assertion, via the
  same `max_iterations == full candidate count` argument D12/D13/D14/D16 already established.
- **A real `.chia_remote()` Ray dispatch**, not just a decorated function that happens to also
  work locally — `flux_agentic_architecture_search.chia_remote(...)` returns a real
  `ray.ObjectRef`, and `get()`-ing it reproduces the same width=32/263.0 result from a separate
  worker process (confirmed by the `(flux_agentic_architecture_search pid=...)` prefix in Ray's
  own log output, the same signal D6's live test used).
- **A real MCP-client round trip** for `agentic_architecture_search` — `mcp.ClientSession` over
  `streamable_http_client` against a real running `FluxTool` server, added as
  `test_agentic_architecture_search_tool_call_finds_the_proven_optimum_over_mcp` in
  `tests/integration/test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`, and the old `test_tool_registers_all_nine_
  flux_nodes` renamed to `test_tool_registers_all_twelve_flux_nodes`, now asserting the full
  12-tool set via a real `list_tools()` call, not just the 9 from before D17.
- **A real dependency gap found and fixed**: `chia`'s own `pyproject.toml` doesn't declare
  `openai`, even though `OllamaLLM` needs it at runtime (`openai` is only imported lazily inside
  `chia`'s `openai_compat.py`, so `chia` itself installs and imports fine without it — the failure
  only surfaces the first time an agentic node actually runs). `flows/chia_nodes/pyproject.toml`
  now lists `openai` explicitly, with a comment explaining why it's an exception to the "don't
  list evaluator-only deps" convention `flows/cli/registry.py` established.
- **Full regression run**: 540 unit + integration tests passing together in a fresh venv (all
  flux packages + real chia + real Ollama + real ZigZag/Booksim2/RTL/Timeloop/SystemC/ONNX
  installed), confirming the new nodes/tools don't break any of D1–D16's existing surfaces.

**Implications.**
- All twelve `flux_chia_nodes` functions now have an MCP-tool surface — the "no CHIA node/MCP
  tool" caveat in D12 §Implications, D13 §Implications, and D14 §Implications is resolved for all
  three strategies simultaneously, not one at a time.
- `search/agentic/README.md`'s own "Not implemented" section (a CHIA node / MCP tool for any of
  the three strategies) is now stale and should be read as historical — the surface it described
  as missing now exists.
- An external agent driving DSE purely through MCP tool calls (the original motivating scenario
  from the "AGENTIC DSE and architecture design flow" planning pass this whole D9–D17 sequence
  answers) can now invoke any of the three agentic search axes the same way it invokes
  `flux_search`'s exhaustive sweep — same transport, same dict-in/dict-out shape, same
  `.to_dict()` convention added across `MappingCandidate` and all three strategies' report/
  evaluated-candidate types to make this possible without any dataclass unpacking on the client
  side.

## D18. The reference agentic DSE loop, built and run for real — roadmap.md Phase 4's exit criterion checked clause by clause

**Decision.** Build `flows/chia_nodes/src/flux_chia_nodes/dse_loop.py`'s `flux_agentic_dse_loop`:
one CHIA node (and one MCP tool, `flux_mcp`'s thirteenth) that runs D13/D17's LLM-driven
architecture-width search, then independently validity-checks the winner (D10), formally checks
its RTL conformance within a calibrated confidence interval (D8), stores the winner and proves it
replays deterministically (docs/stores.md), and reports what the run actually cost — composing
five already-built, already-verified nodes/functions into one dispatchable unit rather than
writing new search or evaluation logic.

**Why.** docs/roadmap.md's Phase 4 names an explicit, four-clause exit criterion for "the reasoning
loop" — "(a) produces a design better than the best human-tuned baseline, (b) whose winning
design passes independent validity checking and RTL conformance, (c) whose result is
deterministically replayable, and (d) costs a reportable number of dollars" — and D9 through D17
had built every individual piece that criterion needs (agentic search, independent validity,
formal conformance checking, a result store, deterministic replay via `flux replay`) without ever
connecting them into one loop and actually running it. D18 is that connection, checked against
real backends rather than assumed to follow from the individual pieces already working.

**What was verified, clause by clause — full write-up with exact numbers in
[docs/phase4-exit-criterion-report.md](../flux/docs/phase4-exit-criterion-report.md):**
- **(a) Beats a human-tuned baseline**: the LLM-found winner (width=32, 263.0 ZigZag cycles)
  vs. the architecture's own as-shipped baseline (width=8, 1554.0 cycles) — a real 5.9× reduction,
  both numbers from the same screening evaluator so the comparison isn't crossing methodologies.
- **(b) Independent validity + RTL conformance**: `flux_check_validity` reports `ok=True` for
  the winner (clears the independent roofline bound). `flux_conformance_check` was run twice on
  purpose: `ok=False` against an empty calibration store (the same honest-failure behavior every
  other conformance test in this repo already establishes, reproduced for a new candidate, not a
  new mechanism), then `ok=True` once seeded with a *different* candidate's real residual (the
  already-established width=8 ZigZag-vs-RTL pair, 1554 vs. 529 cycles) — a genuinely non-circular
  check, since the width=32 winner being checked is a different point than the one the
  calibration was seeded from. **A new real data point came out of this**: real Verilator RTL at
  width=32 measures 133.0 cycles, not previously pinned anywhere in this repo. The width=8-derived
  calibrated interval ([53.9, 1282.2]) correctly covers it, even though the ZigZag/RTL residual
  ratio *shifts* between the two widths (≈2.94× at width=8 vs. ≈1.98× at width=32) — the same
  qualitative "ratio moves, calibrated CI still covers it" shape
  [docs/calibration-report.md](../flux/docs/calibration-report.md) already documented for ZigZag-vs-Timeloop
  at a held-out width, now independently reproduced for a different evaluator pair
  (ZigZag-vs-real-RTL).
- **(c) Deterministic replay**: the winner's `Result` stored via a real `ResultStore`, then
  re-evaluated fresh — stored and fresh values match exactly (263.0 == 263.0), the same check
  `flux replay` runs from the CLI, now inside the loop itself.
- **(d) Cost**: **$0.00**, real and not a placeholder — every LLM call went to a local Ollama
  server, every evaluation to local evaluator adapters, no billed API of any kind.
- **Verified at all three levels this repo's convention requires**: an in-process call, a real
  `.chia_remote()` Ray dispatch (confirmed by the `(flux_agentic_dse_loop pid=...)` prefix in
  Ray's own log output), and a real MCP client round trip over the wire — three new tests in
  `tests/integration/test_chia_flux_agentic_dse_loop_live.py` plus one in
  `tests/integration/test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`, all passing.

**Implications.**
- `flows/mcp`'s `FluxTool` now exposes thirteen tools; an agent can trigger the entire reference
  loop — search, validity, conformance, store, replay, cost — with one tool call instead of
  sequencing four separate ones itself.
- **Scoped to the architecture-width axis on purpose**, not all three agentic axes: this is the
  axis with the cleanest "human baseline vs. searched winner" framing (a single default width vs.
  a swept one), and reuses D13/D17's already-verified strategy rather than introducing new
  per-axis "baseline" semantics for mapping or NoC-topology, which don't have as natural a
  single-baseline-value framing. Extending the same loop shape to those axes is real future work,
  not required for this decision's exit criterion to be met for what it covers.
- The synthesis rung (`evaluators/hammer/`) is still not part of this loop — still blocked on
  tooling per its own README, unchanged by this decision.
- docs/roadmap.md's Phase 4 exit criterion can now be pointed to a real, reproducible run rather than
  described only in the abstract — the report is checked-in, not a one-off manual finding.
