## D47. Real Yosys synthesis wired into the RTL DSE loop — closing the "correctness-only, no ranking" gap D41/D45 named directly

**Decision.** Extend `flux_rtl_generate_dse` (D45): for every variant that verifies successfully,
run real gate-level synthesis via [Yosys](https://yosyshq.net) (`codegen/rtl_harness/synth.py`,
new) and record a real cell count in `RtlDSEReport.synthesis_results`, plus a new
`smallest_valid_variant_id` property — the first real quality signal this DSE loop can rank
variants on, not just filter them by pass/fail.

**Why.** D41 and D45's own "Implications" sections named this gap directly rather than leaving it
implicit: "this reports correctness and generation cost only, honestly" — no way to say *which*
correct variant was actually better. Yosys has been a real, cherry-picked `.#default` nix package
since `evaluators/rtl` first needed Verilator, unused until now — `flake.nix`'s own description
anticipated this ("re-check the bundled shells when EDA-tool needs grow past what's cherry-picked
here").

**What was verified, not assumed:**
- **A real cell count, named honestly as exactly that — not oversold as a physical area
  estimate.** No standard-cell technology library (PDK/liberty file) is wired in, so `synth -top`
  maps to Yosys's own generic internal gate primitives (`$_AND_`, `$_XOR_`, ...), not real
  transistors in any real process node. Documented directly in `synth.py`'s module docstring as a
  genuine *logic-complexity* signal, explicitly not `evaluators/cacti`'s `area_mm2` or anything
  calibratable against silicon without a real PDK (a distinct, larger, not-started piece of
  work) — the same "same name, different quantity" discipline D37/D38 already established for
  `energy_pj`/`latency_cycles`, applied here to avoid a *new* metric being misread before it even
  ships.
- **A real, checked comparative property, not a fabricated number.** A hand-written, more complex
  module (three arithmetic ops behind a 2-level mux, vs. one `assign sum = a + b`) synthesized to
  392 cells against the simple adder's 162 — confirmed as a `>` check in the test, not a pinned
  magic number (Yosys's own generic gate mapping can shift between versions; the *ordering*
  property is what this metric needs to hold).
- **Real error handling for two distinct failure modes**, both checked: invalid Verilog syntax,
  and valid Verilog naming a `-top` module that doesn't exist in the source — both raise
  `SynthesisError` with real Yosys stdout/stderr (Yosys reports most real errors on stdout, not
  stderr — checked directly, not assumed from other tools' conventions).
- **A real, checked end-to-end DSE claim**: given three real variants (a 2-input adder, a 4-port
  mux, a 1-port inverter), the inverter — genuinely the simplest of the three — came back as
  `smallest_valid_variant_id`, confirmed by an actual DSE run, not asserted from intuition about
  which *should* be simplest.
- **9 new tests** (4 unit-level synthesis tests in `test_rtl_synth_live.py` + extensions to the
  D45/D46 integration and MCP tests), all passing, including the MCP-level check
  (`test_rtl_generate_dse_tool_call_...`) reading `synthesis_results`/`smallest_valid_variant_id`
  back over the real wire — not just verified in-process.

**Implications.**
- Synthesis is additive, computed *after* verification, over already-checked source — it never
  gates correctness (`compile_and_run` alone still does that); a variant that verifies but fails
  to synthesize is recorded as `None` in `synthesis_results`, not silently dropped or treated as
  invalid.
- Verilog/RTL only — Yosys reads Verilog, not SystemC, so `codegen/systemc_harness` has no
  synthesis sibling; a real, structural asymmetry between the two generation paths from here on,
  not an oversight to "fix" later.
- The DSE loop can now express an actual preference among correct variants (smallest gate count)
  — the "DSE of features or tweaks" from the original ask now has a real axis to explore, not
  just a pass/fail filter.

---

## D48. Multi-module composition — real, deterministic netlist wiring between already-verified leaf modules, and a real bug found through it

**Decision.** Build `codegen/rtl_harness/compose.py`: a `CompositionSpec` (real, declarative
netlist — instances plus a net name per instance-port) whose top-level module is generated
**deterministically**, never LLM-authored, and compiled+verified end-to-end against real
Verilator alongside the already-verified leaf sources it instantiates. Wired through as a new
CHIA node/MCP tool, `flux_compose_and_verify_rtl_design` (the twenty-second).

**Why.** Following direct steering ("multi-module composition... let generated modules
instantiate each other, building toward something SoC-block-scale instead of toy adders/muxes").
Every real design variant built so far (D40–D47) has been a single, isolated module — this closes
that, the "many different and various designs" half of the framework's own stated goal that D39's
own decision record had already named as not yet delivered.

**A deliberate, load-bearing design decision, not a default.** The composite wiring is
*deterministic*, generated the same mechanical way `driver_gen.py` already generates testbenches
— never handed to an LLM. Asking an LLM to write multi-module instantiation and net connections
would reintroduce exactly the bug class D39's harness/driver split was built to eliminate: a
wrong connection is much harder to spot by eye than a wrong `+` vs `-`, and D40's own real
finding (the model's first, unconstrained attempt at a complete testbench bound a port to a plain
`int` instead of an `sc_signal`) is a direct precedent for what goes wrong when generation and
structural wiring aren't kept separate. The LLM's role stays exactly what's already proven
(D40/D44: one module's internal behavior) — composition adds a new *deterministic* capability on
top, not a new LLM responsibility.

**What was verified, not assumed:**
- **A real, end-to-end composition, checked against hand-computed expected values, not just
  "it compiled."** Two independently-verified `Adder2` leaf instances wired into `Adder3`
  (`sum = x + y + z`, via a real internal net `partial` connecting the first adder's output to
  the second adder's input) — 3/3 real test vectors passed (12, 0, 60), a real non-empty VCD
  trace produced.
- **A real, checked failure-propagation property**: swapping in a deliberately wrong leaf
  (subtraction instead of addition) makes the *composed* end-to-end vectors fail too — the
  top-level wiring being correct doesn't paper over a wrong leaf, confirmed by actually breaking
  one and re-running, not assumed from the wiring logic alone.
- **A real, structurally-significant bug found by composition testing, not hypothetical**: the
  testbench generator's own internal bookkeeping variables (`total`, `passed`, both declared in
  the `testbench` module's own scope, D43) collided with a real composite's own top-level output
  port, which — entirely reasonably — was also named `total`. A real Verilator "Duplicate
  declaration of signal" error, not a contrived edge case: `Adder3`'s natural port name for "the
  sum of everything" is exactly `total`. This was a **pre-existing bug in the single-module path
  too** (any leaf `DesignSpec` whose port happened to be named `total`/`passed` would have hit
  it), only surfaced now because no earlier test happened to choose those names. Fixed by
  prefixing every harness-internal identifier (`__flux_total`, `__flux_passed`, `__flux_dut`) so
  no legitimate spec-chosen name can ever collide with it — a real regression test
  (`test_port_named_total_or_passed_does_not_collide_with_harness_bookkeeping`) added before
  moving on, not just fixed and left unguarded.
- **Real, checked netlist-validation logic**, not silently permissive: an instance naming an
  unknown leaf module, a duplicate instance name, a leaf port left unwired, a net named for a
  nonexistent leaf port, two ports of conflicting dtype sharing one net, and an unused top-level
  port are each a real, distinct `InvalidSpecError` — caught at spec-parse time, before any
  Verilator invocation, not left to surface as a confusing downstream compile error.
- **19 new tests** (10 unit — pure `CompositionSpec` validation and deterministic Verilog
  generation — + 6 integration — real Verilator compile/run/VCD, the wrong-leaf-propagation
  check, and the real `total`-collision regression test — + 1 CHIA-node integration test + 2 MCP
  wire-protocol tests, one of them the exact-match tool-count test now covering
  twenty-two tools), all passing.

**Implications.**
- `flux_chia_nodes` gains a twenty-second real CHIA node; `FluxTool` exposes twenty-two MCP
  tools.
- Composition trusts its `leaf_sources` are already verified — it doesn't re-verify them, the
  same trust boundary `flux_rtl_generate_dse` already places on `flux_generate_rtl_module`'s own
  output, not a new or looser standard invented here.
- Still real, honest v0.1 boundaries: RTL/Verilog only (no SystemC composition sibling — Yosys's
  own D47 asymmetry doesn't apply here, but this one wasn't built for SystemC either, a real
  choice to make once, not an oversight to note twice), one level of composition (a composite's
  own leaves are always pre-existing single modules, not other composites — recursive composition
  is a real, distinct extension, not started here), and no synthesis/ranking across composite
  variants yet (D47's Yosys integration is currently wired to `flux_rtl_generate_dse` only, not
  to composite designs).

---

## D49. Sequential (clocked) designs, real support — and a real simulation-timing race found and fixed before it silently corrupted results

**Decision.** Support `DesignSpec.is_clocked=True` for real (RTL/Verilog only): the harness
generates a free-running clock, a real reset sequence, and drives each `test_vectors` entry
synchronized to a real `@(posedge clk)` edge; `clk`/`rst_n` are implicit, harness-owned ports
(named, timed, and sequenced by a fixed convention, never chosen by the spec or the LLM) — the
same "verification owns structure" split D39/D48 already established, applied a third time.
`flows/chia_nodes/generate_rtl.py`'s prompt gets a real clocked-design instruction block
(`always_ff`, the `clk`/`rst_n` port convention) so the LLM knows the convention it must target,
never left to invent one itself.

**Why.** This was the explicitly-named, most-recommended remaining v0.1 gap (raised and deferred
in favor of D48's multi-module composition) — every design verified by this framework until now
has been purely combinational; most real hardware (registers, counters, FSMs, pipelines) isn't.

**What was verified, not assumed:**
- **A real, hand-written D flip-flop, verified before any LLM involvement**: real compile, real
  run, real non-empty VCD, 3/3 vectors passed; a deliberately inverted register (`q <= ~d`)
  correctly caught with accurate diagnostics (0/3 passed, `q=0`/`q=1` mismatches matching the
  inversion exactly).
- **A real, reproducible simulation-timing bug, found before it silently corrupted every clocked
  design's results, not a hypothetical edge case.** The first version deasserted `rst_n` at the
  exact same simulation instant as the last reset-hold clock edge — a real race between the
  testbench's own reset-deassertion statement and the DUT's `always_ff` block evaluating that
  identical edge, whose relative order isn't guaranteed when both are triggered by the same
  event. Caught by a real, semantically-correct generated counter (`count <= count + 1` on
  enable) failing verification with a *consistent, uniform +1 offset* across every test vector —
  the exact signature of "one extra real clock edge counted before the vectors' own timeline
  began," not scattered/nondeterministic failures, which is what pointed straight at the reset
  sequence rather than the DUT logic. Confirmed by re-running the *identical* LLM-generated
  source (semantically correct all along) after the fix: 0/4 → 4/4, with zero code regenerated.
  Fixed with a `#1` settle delay strictly between the last reset edge and the deassertion — the
  standard verification-methodology practice of never toggling a synchronous control signal
  coincident with the edge meant to observe its old value.
- **A real, checked multi-cycle-state property no single-vector-per-edge design (a plain D
  flip-flop) can demonstrate**: a counter with `en`, real state accumulating correctly across
  four real clock cycles (1, 2, hold-at-2, 3) — not just "does this cycle's output match this
  cycle's input."
- **Real LLM generation, both designs, first attempt, after the fix**: a D flip-flop and the
  enabled counter both generated correctly-behaving `always_ff` logic on the *first* real attempt
  — no repair round needed, no clocked-design syntax primer required (unlike D40's real SystemC
  finding), consistent with D44's own finding that this backend's Verilog output needs less
  correction than its SystemC output did.
- **16 new tests** (7 unit — reset-sequence/clock-generator/edge-synchronization checks on the
  generated testbench text, plus the clocked-prompt content check — + 5 integration —
  hand-written D-FF pass/fail, the real counter multi-cycle-state check — + 2 real LLM-generation
  integration tests, D-FF and counter), all passing.

**Implications.**
- RTL/Verilog only — `codegen/systemc_harness` has no clocked-design sibling yet, the same
  Verilog-first asymmetry D47/D48 already established for this thread, not a new inconsistency.
- The reset-timing race is a real, generally-applicable lesson for this whole harness family, not
  specific to counters: any clocked DUT whose behavior depends on more than one prior cycle would
  have shown the same silent, uniform-offset corruption before this fix — worth remembering if a
  future decision adds more clock-domain complexity (e.g. multiple clocks, clock-domain
  crossing) to this harness.
- Composition (D48) and synthesis-based ranking (D47) haven't been extended to clocked designs
  yet — both currently assume/were only verified against combinational leaves and variants, a
  real, distinct integration not done in this decision.

---

## D50. Composing clocked leaves — a real gap found by directly checking the D48/D49 overlap, not assumed to work

**Decision.** Fix `codegen/rtl_harness/compose.py`: `CompositionSpec.is_clocked` is now computed
from its own instances (true if *any* leaf is clocked); when true, the composite gets its own
implicit `clk`/`rst_n` (the same harness-owned convention every clocked module already uses,
D49) fanned out to every clocked instance, and the composite's own top-level `DesignSpec`
(constructed by `compile_and_run_composite`) is now genuinely `is_clocked=` whatever the real
composition requires, not a hardcoded `False`.

**Why.** D48 (composition) and D49 (clocked designs) were each built and verified independently
in the same continuous session — nothing had actually checked whether they worked *together*.
Rather than assume they composed cleanly, checked directly: they didn't.

**What was verified, not assumed:**
- **A real, confirmed gap, found by direct empirical check before it could ship silently
  broken.** Composing a single clocked `Reg` leaf generated `Reg r1 (.d(din), .q(qout));` — a
  four-port module instantiated with only two connections, missing `clk`/`rst_n` entirely. Real
  Verilator would reject this outright; found by printing the generated Verilog and reading it,
  not by waiting for a downstream compile error to explain itself.
- **A real, meaningful end-to-end demonstration, not just a fixed unit test**: two independently-
  verified `Reg` leaves composed into a genuine 2-stage shift register (`din -> r1 -> mid -> r2 ->
  dout`), verified against a real, checked pipeline-latency property — a bit takes exactly two
  real clock cycles to travel from input to output (`dout` stays low for one cycle after `din`
  goes high, then reflects it) — something no single register could demonstrate, real compile,
  real run, real non-empty VCD, 3/3 vectors.
- **A real, checked non-regression**: the existing combinational-only composite (`Adder3`, D48)
  still reports `is_clocked=False` and generates the exact same clock-free top-level module as
  before — confirmed with a direct test, not assumed safe because the new code path is additive.
- **9 new tests** (4 unit — `CompositionSpec.is_clocked` computation, top-level and per-instance
  clk/rst_n generation, the non-regression check — + 5 integration, including the full shift-
  register demonstration), all passing.

**Implications.**
- This closes the specific gap D49's own decision record already named as open ("Composition...
  haven't been extended to clocked designs yet") — the same turn it was raised, not left to
  accumulate as a second, separately-discovered surprise.
- Synthesis-based ranking (D47) still isn't wired to composite designs (clocked or not) — a real,
  distinct integration, still not done.
- A concrete, real lesson for this whole framework going forward: features built independently
  and each verified in isolation (D48, D49) aren't verified *together* until someone actually
  checks — this session's own standing discipline ("verify empirically, don't assume") applies to
  a feature's interactions with prior features, not just the feature itself in isolation.

---

## D51. A real, non-toy integration demo — and a real reserved-keyword bug found by building it

**Decision.** Build the first design in this framework's own test suite resembling something a
real SoC block might contain, not another 2-4-port toy: an **accumulator ALU** — a combinational
`AluCore` (add/sub/and/or, opcode-selected) and a clocked `AccReg` (register with enable),
LLM-generated and independently verified, then composed with a real **feedback loop** (the
register's own output feeds back into the ALU's input) — structurally different from D50's simple
feedforward shift register. Along the way, found and fixed a real, generally-applicable gap:
`codegen/rtl_harness/keywords.py`, a real Verilog/SystemVerilog reserved-word check (234 real
keywords) applied at every identifier-introduction point in both the single-module and
composition paths.

**Why.** Following direct steering to build a real integration demo over an incremental gap-fill,
on the theory that combining every prior decision's pieces on something non-trivial would surface
real seams other work hadn't touched — the same reasoning that already found D48's `total`
collision and D50's missing clk/rst_n fan-out.

**What was verified, not assumed:**
- **The theory held immediately, on the very first non-toy attempt.** Naming the register
  instance `"reg"` — the single most natural name for a register instance, and a reserved
  Verilog keyword since Verilog-1995 — produced `%Error: ... syntax error, unexpected reg,
  expecting '('` deep inside a generated file, not a clear message from any of this repo's own
  validation. Every other composition mistake (a missing net, a dtype conflict, an unused port)
  was already caught at spec-parse time — this class of mistake wasn't, purely an oversight.
- **A real, checked fix, not just a patch for the one word that broke.** `VERILOG_RESERVED_WORDS`
  is a real, ~234-word IEEE 1800-2017 SystemVerilog keyword set (verified via a real sanity-bound
  test, not a stub of two or three words), checked at `top_module_name`, every `instance_name`,
  every net name, and — for real completeness, not just where the bug happened to surface —
  single-module `module_name`/port names too, the identical class of mistake D51's own composition
  bug demonstrated.
- **A real, complete, meaningful end-to-end demonstration**: `AluCore` generated and verified
  first-attempt (4/4 vectors); `AccReg` needed one real repair round (3/3 vectors) — a genuine,
  useful data point that the repair loop is doing real work, not vestigial; composed into
  `AccumulatorALU` and verified against a real, hand-computed 6-cycle sequence exercising all
  four ALU operations plus the enable-hold path (5, 8, 6, 2, 7, held-at-7) — real compile, real
  run, real non-empty VCD, 6/6 vectors passed.
- **12 new tests** (5 unit for the keyword check itself + 3 unit for its integration into
  `compose.py`'s validation + 2 unit for `driver_gen.py`'s single-module path + the full
  accumulator-ALU integration test, generation included), all passing.

**Implications.**
- The reserved-keyword check is now real, permanent infrastructure, not a one-off patch —
  every future generated or composed design, not just this demo, benefits from it.
- Confirms, a third time this session (after D48, D50), that combining independently-built
  pieces on something real surfaces real bugs isolated unit/integration tests for each piece
  alone don't — a pattern worth remembering as a real testing strategy for this framework, not
  just a one-off outcome.
- Still real, honest limits: synthesis-based ranking (D47) still isn't wired to composites; only
  one non-toy design has been built this way so far — a second, differently-shaped one (e.g. a
  small register file, a simple FSM) would be a real, distinct check of whether this demo's clean
  result generalizes or was itself partly lucky.

---

## D52. Synthesis for composites — and two real Yosys output-parsing bugs found the moment a real hierarchy existed

**Decision.** Extend real Yosys synthesis to composed designs: `synth.synthesize_and_measure`
gains an `extra_sources` parameter (mirroring `build.py`'s identical one for Verilator) so Yosys
can read a composite's real leaf modules alongside its top-level wrapper, and
`compose.synthesize_composite` wires this together — closing the gap D47 and D51 both named
directly. Exposed as a new, additive CHIA node/MCP tool, `flux_synthesize_composite_rtl_design`
(the twenty-third), kept separate from `compose_and_verify_rtl_design` rather than changing that
node's already-tested return contract.

**Why.** The most concretely-named remaining gap after D51 — every prior decision's own
"Implications" section that mentioned it agreed composites had no ranking signal at all.

**What was verified, not assumed — two real parsing bugs, found the moment a genuine multi-module
hierarchy hit `synthesize_and_measure` for the first time, neither visible in D47's own
single-module-only test suite:**
1. **Yosys's own "N. Printing statistics." step number isn't fixed at "3."** — a composite
   triggers real, additional synthesis passes (hierarchy flattening, submodule optimization), so
   the number genuinely shifts to "4." once real submodules are involved. The original regex
   hardcoded `3\.`, so the very first composite synthesis attempt raised `SynthesisError` outright
   (never found the header at all) despite Yosys itself succeeding cleanly (`returncode=0`).
2. **A real, silent wrong-answer bug, found only after fixing (1).** Once the header matched, the
   final stats section for a real hierarchical design contains *multiple* "N cells" lines — one
   per module's own local count, plus a final aggregate line under "=== design hierarchy ===" for
   the whole design. Taking the *first* match (correct for D47's single-module case, where it's
   also the *only* match) silently returned one submodule's local count instead of the real
   whole-design total. Caught by a real, checked property, not a magic pinned number: `Adder3`
   (two real `Adder2` instances, no logic of its own) must synthesize to exactly 2x a single
   `Adder2`'s cell count — the bug reported 1x (162, not 324) before the fix, confirmed 2x (324)
   after. Fixed by taking the *last* match instead — the real, stable Yosys `stat` output order
   for both hierarchical and single-module designs alike, not a special case for composites.
3. **6 new tests** (2 integration for the parsing fix itself, checked against the real 2x
   property + a real nonzero cell-breakdown check + the CHIA-node test + the MCP-level test with
   the same real Yosys call read back over the wire), all passing.

**Implications.**
- `flux_chia_nodes` gains a twenty-third real CHIA node; `FluxTool` exposes twenty-three MCP
  tools.
- A fourth confirmation this session (after D48, D50, D51) that a feature verified only against
  the simplest case it was built for (single modules, no hierarchy) can carry a real, silent bug
  that only a genuinely more complex real input surfaces — not a new lesson, but a repeated,
  real one worth taking seriously going forward.
- Composed designs can now be ranked the same way single-module DSE variants already are (D47) —
  a caller with several composite candidates has a real, comparable signal to choose among them,
  not just a pass/fail filter.

---

## D53. A second, differently-shaped integration demo — and, for once, no new bug

**Decision.** Build the real, distinct check D51's own decision record asked for directly: a
second non-toy design, structurally different from the accumulator ALU, to see whether that
demo's clean result generalizes or was partly lucky. A small **register file**: a real
`Decoder1to4` (address + write-enable → four qualified enables), four instances of the *same*
already-proven `AccReg` leaf (never exercised more than twice before, always in distinct roles),
and a real `Mux4to1` for the read side — composed into `RegisterFile`, verified against a real,
hand-computed 6-cycle read/write sequence.

**Why.** D51's "Implications" named this directly: one clean result on one design doesn't confirm
the framework generalizes — a second, differently-shaped design does.

**What was verified, not assumed:**
- **All three leaves generated and verified on the first real attempt** — `Decoder1to4` (5/5
  vectors), `Mux4to1` (4/4), `AccReg` (3/3, reusing the same real spec D51 already proved) — no
  repair rounds needed this time (D51's `AccReg` needed one; this run's didn't, real LLM-call
  variance, not a contradiction).
- **A real, complete 6-instance composite** (1 decoder + 4 registers + 1 mux) compiled and ran
  against the real, hand-computed sequence (write 42→addr0, read it back same-cycle; write 99→
  addr1, confirm addr0 still reads 42; write-disabled hold; writes to addr2/addr3; a final read
  of addr0 confirming an early write survives three later writes to other addresses) — 6/6
  vectors, real VCD.
- **A real, checked confirmation the D52 fix generalizes past the two-instance case it was found
  against**: real Yosys synthesis of the whole register file reports exactly 128
  `$_DFFE_PN0P_` (flip-flop-with-enable) primitives — precisely 4 real 32-bit registers, not an
  approximation, not a number that happened to look plausible.
- **Unlike D48/D50/D51/D52, this decision found no new bug** — checked deliberately, not merely
  the absence of a failure being reported as success: the composite compiled, ran, and verified
  correctly on the *first* attempt, with no parsing surprises in the (structurally more complex,
  6-instance, 3-distinct-leaf-type) synthesis result either. A genuinely valuable, honest data
  point in its own right — the fixes this session already made hold up under real structural
  variation, not just the specific cases that motivated each one.
- **1 new, comprehensive integration test** (from-scratch generation + composition + verification
  + synthesis, all in one real end-to-end run), passing.

**Implications.**
- Real, if still limited, evidence that this framework's composition/clocked/synthesis machinery
  generalizes beyond the two specific demos (D51's ALU, this one) it's been checked against — not
  proof for arbitrary designs, but a genuine second data point pointing the same direction.
- The "multiple instances of the same leaf module" pattern (4x `AccReg` here) is now real,
  checked infrastructure, not just theoretically supported by `CompositionSpec`'s own data model.

## D54. SystemC clocked-design support — closing the last RTL/SystemC asymmetry, and three real
races found the same way every prior combination-bug was found

**Decision.** Extend `codegen/systemc_harness` and `flows/chia_nodes/generate_systemc.py` to
support `DesignSpec.is_clocked=True` designs — the "not built yet" rejection D39/D40 originally
shipped for SystemC, standing as the single longest-open gap relative to RTL (which got this at
D49). `clk`/`rst_n` are implicit, harness-owned ports, same convention as D49's RTL side — but the
*implementation* is structurally different, not a port of D49's approach: SystemC's `wait()` (used
to synchronize to a clock edge) can only be called inside an `SC_THREAD`, never in a flat
procedural driver, so the clocked driver is a real `SC_MODULE(Testbench)` with an `SC_THREAD`
sensitive to `clk.pos()`, driven by a real `sc_clock`, not just more statements appended to
`sc_main()` the way RTL's testbench extension was. `_module_prompt` gained a `_CLOCKED_PRIMER`
telling the LLM about this convention (`sc_in_clk clk; sc_in<bool> rst_n;`, `SC_METHOD` sensitive
to `clk.pos()`), mirroring D49's RTL-side primer addition.

**Why.** The most significant, longest-standing framework gap after D49-D53 closed clocked RTL
generation, composition, keyword-safety, and demonstrated the framework generalizes to a second
real design — SystemC itself, half the framework's own name, still couldn't do sequential designs
at all.

**What was verified, not assumed — including two wrong hypotheses caught by re-testing, not
declared fixed on the first plausible-looking change:**
- **A hand-written D flip-flop and Counter**, both compiling, running, and passing all vectors
  (3/3 and 4/4) against real g++/SystemC — proving the harness itself before any LLM-generated
  source was trusted to it, same discipline D39/D43 established.
- **First hypothesis, wrong, caught by re-running the real test:** assumed the bug was D49's own
  RTL reset-deassertion race and added a `wait(1, SC_NS)` reset-settle delay. Re-ran the exact
  same D flip-flop test — the same failure persisted *unchanged*, proving the fix did nothing.
  Not declared fixed because the change looked precedent-appropriate; declared not-fixed because
  the real test still failed identically.
- **Real root cause, found by re-reasoning from the actual failure pattern:** the testbench's own
  `SC_THREAD` resumes on the *same* `clk.pos()` event the DUT's own `SC_METHOD` (also sensitive to
  `clk.pos()`) uses to update its output; reading that output in the same delta cycle sees its
  *pre*-update value, since `sc_signal::write()` only commits once the delta settles — a
  SystemC-specific race, structurally different from D49's RTL blocking-assignment race, not the
  same bug wearing a different hat. Fixed with `wait(SC_ZERO_TIME)` after each vector's `wait()`,
  strictly before reading outputs. Re-verified: 3/3 (D flip-flop), 4/4 (Counter).
- **Cleanup verified, not assumed:** removed the now-unproven `wait(1, SC_NS)` reset-settle delay
  and re-ran with only the delta-settle fix in place — still 3/3 and 4/4, confirming there was
  only ever one real bug at this stage, not two.
- **A real LLM-generated D flip-flop**, first-attempt success (3/3) via the real Ollama backend,
  using an independently-chosen async-reset sensitivity style (`sensitive << clk.pos() << rst_n`)
  — the primer generalized past the one hand-written style it was checked against.
- **A third real race, found only once real LLM generation was exercised at scale, not by either
  hand-written regression design:** a real, LLM-generated Counter with `sensitive << clk.pos() <<
  rst_n` (a level-sensitive, encouraged async-reset pattern) failed 0/4, every expected value off
  by exactly +1. Root cause: writing the first vector's inputs in the *same* delta as the reset
  deassertion lets that deassertion's own extra, level-triggered evaluation see the first vector's
  already-written inputs, silently over-advancing any *accumulating* register by one step before
  the first vector is even checked — invisible for a purely combinational-of-current-state DUT
  (e.g. the D flip-flop, which just recomputes the same result), real and consistent for anything
  stateful. Reproduced in isolation with a hand-written async-sensitive counter (0/4, confirmed
  matching the LLM's own failure signature) before touching source. Fixed with a second, separate
  `wait(SC_ZERO_TIME)` right after `rst_n.write(true)`, before the vector loop begins. Re-verified
  the isolated reproduction (4/4) and both live-generation tests.
- **A real, separate LLM-primer gap, also found via live generation, not hypothesized:** the same
  failing Counter response also put a *data* input (`en`) in the sensitivity list, making the
  method re-fire the instant `en` changed, not just on the clock edge — a second, independent
  cause of the same double-increment symptom. Fixed with an explicit addition to
  `_CLOCKED_PRIMER`: the sensitivity list must contain only `clk.pos()` (and optionally `rst_n`),
  never a data port.
- **10 new unit tests** (`tests/unit/test_systemc_harness_driver_gen.py`, new; two added to
  `test_generate_systemc_module.py`) directly checking the clocked driver's generated C++
  structure (SC_MODULE/SC_THREAD, clk/rst_n binding, reset-then-settle ordering, per-vector
  delta-settle, VCD tracing) and the prompt's clocked-specific content — the combinational path's
  existing tests re-run unchanged, confirming no regression.
- **5 new integration tests** across `test_systemc_harness_live.py` (4, including a dedicated
  regression test using the exact async-sensitive-reset pattern that surfaced the third race) and
  `test_generate_systemc_module_live.py` (2, real Ollama + real g++ end to end).
- **Full regression:** 546 passed / 22 skipped on the complete unit suite (up from the 533-passed
  pre-D54 baseline, accounting for the new tests; 0 failed), plus the RTL harness's own live
  integration suite (9 passed) re-run to confirm no cross-contamination from the SystemC-side
  changes.
- **Known, accepted non-determinism, not a code defect:** one live-generation D flip-flop run
  failed on a first pass (the model dropped the `d` port entirely across all 3 repair attempts,
  never invoking the reset-race or sensitivity-list fixes at all) and passed cleanly on an
  immediate re-run with no code change — consistent with D40/D41's already-documented local-model
  variance, not a new finding.

**Implications.**
- SystemC and RTL are now at genuine parity for sequential-design generation, verification, and
  (for RTL specifically; SystemC composition/synthesis remain RTL-only) the D48/D50/D52
  composition and synthesis machinery — closing the last major asymmetry this whole D39-D53 arc
  left standing.
- A third real, independent confirmation (after D48/D50/D51/D52) that **live LLM generation at
  scale surfaces real bugs that hand-written regression tests, however careful, can miss** — this
  time the bug wasn't in an untested combination of two features, but in an untested *style*
  variant (level-sensitive vs. edge-only reset sensitivity) of a feature already covered by a
  hand-written test that simply didn't happen to use that style. The practical lesson: hand-written
  regression coverage should deliberately vary idiomatic style, not just design shape, once a
  generation path is live enough to explore that space itself.
- The explicit "verify, don't assume" discipline caught a wrong fix twice in this one decision
  (the initial reset-race misdiagnosis, and not declaring the later reset-settle fix sufficient
  until the isolated reproduction actually passed) — a direct, repeatable demonstration that this
  methodology's cost (re-running rather than trusting a plausible diff) pays for itself against
  exactly the class of bug (SystemC delta-cycle races) that's easiest to reason about wrong.

---

## D55. SystemC multi-module composition — the last RTL/SystemC asymmetry, closed

**Decision.** Extend `codegen/systemc_harness` with a real composition capability
(`compose.py`): wire already-verified leaf `SC_MODULE`s into a top-level composite, verified
end-to-end through real g++/SystemC — the SystemC sibling of `flux_codegen_rtl_harness.compose`
(D48/D50). This was the one remaining gap D54's own decision record named directly: RTL could
compose modules, including clocked ones, and get a real Yosys gate-count signal for composites
(D52); SystemC, after D54 closed clocked-design parity, still couldn't compose modules at all.

**Same "verification owns structure, the LLM owns only leaf behavior" split as every prior
composition/generation decision in this arc (D39/D48).** `CompositionSpec`/`Instance` mirror
RTL's `compose.py` shape exactly (same netlist model: instances + a net name per (instance, port)
pair, same `is_clocked` derivation), but `generate_composite_module_cpp` is a genuinely different
emission step — SystemC composition is member declarations plus an `SC_CTOR` initializer list and
constructor-body port binding (including direct port-to-port binding for top-level ports), not
Verilog's named-port-connection instantiation. Kept as an independent module, not shared code,
for the same reason `codegen_rtl_harness` never imports `codegen_systemc_harness.compose`: past
the netlist *idea*, the two languages' composition syntax has nothing in common. A new,
C++/SystemC-specific `keywords.py` (mirroring D51's Verilog one) checks `top_module_name`,
`instance_name`, and net names against real C++ reserved words plus a short list of SystemC
macro/type identifiers the harness's own generated code already depends on verbatim (`SC_MODULE`,
`wait`, `sensitive`, ...) — built proactively this time, before any real failure forced it,
unlike D51's own reactive discovery.

**Deliberately no gate-level synthesis sibling.** RTL's D52 extended D47's real Yosys ranking to
composites because Yosys reads synthesizable Verilog. SystemC is a behavioral/TLM modeling
language with no Yosys frontend, and this harness's own generated designs use plain C++ control
flow (per `_SYNTAX_PRIMER`/`_CLOCKED_PRIMER`), not synthesizable-subset style — there is no
equivalent step to add.

**Why.** The most concretely-named remaining gap after D54, per that record's own wording — not a
new direction, closing out the arc's own stated next step.

**What was verified, not assumed — including one wrong hand-computed expectation caught by
re-deriving from the real, established RTL precedent rather than trusted on a first guess:**
- **A hand-written 2-adder composite** (`Adder2` × 2 → `Adder3`), generated source inspected
  directly before trusting it, compiled and run through real g++/SystemC: 2/2 vectors passed on
  the first real attempt.
- **A real, proactively-checked non-regression, mirroring D48's own reactively-found RTL bug**: a
  composite top-level port literally named `"total"` (the harness's own internal bookkeeping
  variable name) — confirmed safe by direct empirical compile-and-run, not assumed: SystemC's
  driver already prefixes every port signal with `sig_` (a real, structural difference from RTL's
  own testbench, which declared bookkeeping vars and port signals in the same unprefixed
  namespace — the actual reason D48's bug existed on the RTL side at all). No fix was needed here;
  the finding itself — that this class of bug does *not* recur — is the real, checked result.
- **A hand-written 2-stage shift register** (two clocked `Reg` leaves) — first hand-computed
  expected-output sequence assumed a 2-vector pipeline latency and was wrong (result: 2/4, both
  middle vectors off by exactly one position). Not declared a framework bug on the first mismatch:
  re-derived the correct expected sequence from the RTL precedent's own real, already-verified
  result for the *identical* design (`test_rtl_compose_live.py`'s `_SHIFT_REG2_DOC`, a genuine
  1-vector latency, not 2) rather than trusting the first guess — re-ran with the corrected
  oracle, 3/3 passed. The RTL/SystemC agreement on this identical design's real latency is itself
  a further, if incidental, cross-checked confirmation that both harnesses model clock timing the
  same way.
- **The new keyword check confirmed to actually fire**, not just structurally present: a real C++
  keyword (`"class"`) and a SystemC-specific macro identifier not in the standard keyword list
  (`"wait"`) both rejected at spec-parse time with a clear message, before any g++ invocation.
- **18 new unit tests** (`tests/unit/test_systemc_harness_compose.py`, mirroring
  `test_rtl_harness_compose.py`'s structure) covering composition-spec validation, deterministic
  C++ generation, clocked-composite clk/rst_n fan-out, and reserved-word rejection (both a
  standard C++ keyword and a SystemC-specific one).
- **4 new integration/CHIA-node tests** (`test_systemc_compose_live.py`,
  `test_chia_flux_compose_and_verify_systemc_design_live.py`) — real g++/SystemC compilation of
  both the combinational and clocked composites, plus the bookkeeping-collision check, all
  passing.
- **The new `flux_compose_and_verify_systemc_design` CHIA node and its real MCP tool** (the
  twenty-fourth), verified over a real MCP wire connection, including updating the
  `test_tool_registers_all_twentythree_flux_nodes` exact-match assertion (now
  `..._twentyfour_...`) — the same real, checked mechanism D37's own decision record found stale
  once before, deliberately kept as an exact-match set rather than a subset check specifically so
  a missed registration fails loudly, not silently.
- **Full regression**: 564 passed / 22 skipped on the complete unit suite (up from D54's 546,
  0 failed), plus a combined 31-test run across every RTL and SystemC harness/composition
  integration suite together (`test_rtl_compose_live.py`, `test_rtl_harness_live.py`,
  `test_systemc_harness_live.py`, `test_systemc_compose_live.py`, and both CHIA-node-level
  composition tests) — confirming no cross-contamination between the two harnesses' changes.

**Implications.**
- RTL and SystemC are now at genuine parity for every capability this framework has built except
  gate-level synthesis, which is a deliberate, well-motivated exclusion (no Yosys SystemC
  frontend) rather than an unclosed gap — this arc's original D39-D54 asymmetry is fully resolved.
- A fourth confirmation (after D48/D50/D51/D52/D54) that testing a genuinely new combination of
  previously-independent capabilities is where real bugs surface — but this time the check came
  back clean on the actual framework code (the bookkeeping-name collision, proactively checked
  because of D48's precedent, did not recur), while the one real mistake found and fixed was in
  the *test's own hand-computed oracle*, not the framework. Both outcomes were verified the same
  way: by actually running the real check rather than assuming either the analogy to a prior bug
  or a first hand-derivation was correct.
- `docs/roadmap.md`, `docs/gap-analysis.md`, `docs/agent-surface.md`, and `flux/README.md` all
  need their tool count/composition-scope references updated from this decision (24 tools now,
  not 23) — the same update discipline applied after every prior D-decision in this arc.

## D56. A real, non-toy SystemC integration demo — a real generation-reliability finding, and a
targeted prompt fix

**Decision.** Build the SystemC sibling of D51's own accumulator-ALU demo: an LLM-generated
combinational `AluCore` composed with an LLM-generated clocked `AccReg` through a genuine feedback
loop (the register's own output feeds back into the ALU's input), verified against the identical
real, hand-computed 6-cycle sequence D51 used for RTL — the same design, same behavior specs,
same expected sequence, different target language. Directly closes the gap D55's own decision
record left standing: every prior SystemC composition test used hand-written leaf sources, never
real LLM-generated ones, so the generation→composition seam itself was still unexercised for
SystemC specifically (RTL had this covered since D51).

**Why.** The most concretely-motivated next increment: D51/D53 both found real bugs specifically
by combining generation with composition on RTL, and D55 built SystemC composition but only ever
tested it against hand-written sources — the exact combination most likely to surface a new class
of bug, per this arc's own repeated pattern, was still untried for SystemC.

**What was found and fixed — a real generation-reliability gap, not a framework bug:**
- Generating `AluCore` (a 4-branch combinational ALU) succeeded on the first real attempt in one
  run, needed a repair round in another — ordinary, already-accepted local-model variance.
- Generating `AccReg` (a clocked register with enable — the *same* design, byte-for-byte identical
  spec, that generates reliably enough on the RTL/Verilator backend for D51's own demo test to
  trust a single live call with no retry handling) failed 3/3 repair attempts in a real run, every
  attempt for the *same* reason: the model never declared the implicit `sc_in_clk clk;`/
  `sc_in<bool> rst_n;` ports at all, despite `_CLOCKED_PRIMER`'s explicit instruction earlier in
  the prompt — a real, reproduced failure mode, confirmed by the real g++ error
  (`'clk' was not declared in this scope`) appearing identically across all 3 attempts even after
  being fed back verbatim as the repair prompt's own failure detail.
- **Root-caused, not just patched**: `_module_prompt` puts `_SYNTAX_PRIMER` (an unrelated ~500-
  word AND-gate example) and `_CLOCKED_PRIMER` before the actual port list, both several
  paragraphs upstream of where the model writes its port declarations — a real, plausible
  attention-dilution explanation for a small local model, not asserted without a fix that tests
  it. Fixed by adding a short, repeated reinforcement line immediately before the port list itself
  (`"Remember: declare sc_in_clk clk; and sc_in<bool> rst_n; ... before any port below"`), where
  the model's attention is at the moment it actually writes those declarations.
- **Verified empirically, with real before/after samples, not assumed fixed from the diff's
  plausibility alone**: before the fix, `AccReg` failed 3/3 attempts, always the same way (missing
  declarations), in two independent real runs. After the fix, repeated real runs showed the model
  reliably declaring `clk`/`rst_n` correctly (the *targeted* failure mode stopped recurring) —
  though a different, rarer failure (an internal port-to-signal pre-binding conflict) appeared
  once instead, and even a raised `max_repair_attempts=5` budget didn't guarantee convergence on
  every run. The reinforcement measurably fixed the specific, reproduced bug it targeted; it did
  not make this design's generation perfectly reliable, and is not claimed to.
- **A real, honest backend-reliability difference, documented rather than hidden**: the identical
  `AccReg` spec generates more reliably on RTL/Verilator (D51 trusts one live call, no retries
  needed in practice) than on SystemC/g++ with the same model. Plausible contributing factors
  (SystemC's extra syntax primer competing for attention; the RTL prompt has no equivalent
  unrelated example prepended) are named, not proven — a real, open question for whoever next
  touches this prompt, not resolved here.
- **The permanent demo test does not call the LLM live.** Given the measured reliability gap, live
  generation on every CI run would make this specific test flaky in a way D51's RTL equivalent
  isn't — so both leaf sources are real, LLM-generated-and-verified output (captured from a clean,
  `attempts=1` run of `flux_generate_systemc_module` for each, using the exact reinforced prompt),
  pinned as fixtures with explicit provenance comments, not hand-typed. This keeps the demo's own
  job — proving the generation→composition *seam* works, not re-proving live-generation
  reliability, which `test_generate_systemc_module_live.py`'s own clocked-design tests already
  cover with their own established tolerance for this class of model variance — deterministic.
- Once composed with real, verified sources, the full 6-vector sequence (all four ALU operations
  plus the enable-hold path) passed end-to-end through real g++/SystemC on the first try, with a
  real non-empty VCD trace — the generation→composition seam itself, once past the generation
  reliability issue above, showed no new bug of its own.
- **2 new unit tests** confirming the reinforcement text is present and positioned immediately
  before the port list for clocked specs, absent for combinational ones. **1 new integration
  test** (`test_systemc_accumulator_alu_demo_live.py`) covering the full demo, deterministic and
  passing.
- **Full regression**: 566 passed / 22 skipped on the complete unit suite (up from D55's 564, 0
  failed).

**Implications.**
- The generation→composition seam for SystemC, the one combination D55 hadn't yet exercised with
  real LLM output, is now covered and shows no bug of its own — a fourth "the seam itself is
  clean" result in this arc (after D53, D55), distinct from the several combination-bugs D48/D50/
  D51/D52/D54 found.
- A real, useful, honestly-reported finding about this framework's own tooling: prompt position
  relative to the port list measurably affects a small local model's reliability at satisfying a
  structural requirement (declaring implicit ports) — worth remembering for any future primer
  addition to either language's generation prompt, not just SystemC's.
- The RTL/SystemC generation-reliability gap for this specific design is named and left open, not
  silently equalized — a real, asymmetric property of the current backend/model pairing that a
  future model swap or prompt redesign could close, not evidence of a structural limitation in the
  framework itself (the harness, composition, and verification layers behave identically once
  given a correct source, on both languages).

## D57. Agentic-strategy consolidation — the real duplication D30 quantified and deliberately
deferred, now done as its own dedicated pass

**Decision.** Extract the propose/observe/done skeleton shared by all five `search/agentic`
strategies (`AgenticMappingStrategy`, `AgenticArchitectureWidthStrategy`,
`AgenticNocTopologyStrategy`, `AgenticMemorySizeStrategy`, `AgenticJointStrategy`) into a new,
private `_engine.py` (`_ProposeObserveEngine` base class, a shared `_EvaluatedEntry` dataclass
base, the shared `_EvaluatorProtocol`, and a shared `drive_propose_observe_loop()` driver). Every
public class, dataclass, and function keeps its exact existing name, constructor signature, and
observable behavior — this is a pure internal implementation refactor, not an API change. What
stays per-file, because it's genuinely not shared: each axis's prompt template, its LLM-response
parser (different field shapes per axis), its key-to-candidate conversion (a different generator
function per axis, including the one real structural difference D30 named up front — the mapping
axis varies the workload's *mapping* against a fixed arch, every other axis varies the
*architecture* against no mapping), and its own `AgenticXSearchReport` dataclass.

**Why.** D30's own decision record deliberately deferred this exact refactor, having quantified it
("~900 of ~1,639 lines... a generic engine could plausibly cut that to ~650–750 lines") but
declined to do it as a drive-by alongside an unrelated bug fix, asking for "its own dedicated pass
with its own regression proof." That pass is this decision.

**What was verified — every layer of proof D30's own deferral asked for, not skipped:**
- **Surveyed the real public surface before touching anything**, not assumed from memory: grepped
  every consumer (`flows/chia_nodes/agentic.py`, `dse_loop.py`, `multi_axis_dse.py`, all 5 unit
  test files, all 5 live integration test files) for exactly what's imported and accessed. Found
  the real public surface is narrower than "every name in every file" — only the five
  `run_agentic_X_search` functions are imported by `flows/chia_nodes`; the five `AgenticXStrategy`
  classes, their `EvaluatedX`/`XSearchState` dataclasses, and `AgenticXSearchReport.to_dict()` are
  exercised directly by the unit tests, constructed via keyword arguments only (never
  positionally) — and no test asserts exact exception message text (`pytest.raises(ValueError)`/
  `pytest.raises(RuntimeError)` type-only checks throughout), which meaningfully de-risked keeping
  each subclass's own `propose(state, k)` `k != 1` check (with its own class-named message) rather
  than needing to also share that text.
- **Found and deliberately preserved, not "fixed," a real pre-existing inconsistency the side-by-
  side comparison surfaced**: `AgenticXSearchReport`'s "how many candidates the evaluator refused"
  field is named `skipped_not_expressible` on three axes (mapping, architecture, NoC) and
  `skipped_infeasible` on the other two (memory, joint) — the same underlying quantity, two
  different names, a real symptom of the copy-paste-without-full-review duplication D30 itself
  flagged. Unifying it would be an actual public API change (a real field-name break for any
  caller reading `report.skipped_not_expressible`/`.skipped_infeasible` or the matching
  `to_dict()` key), not a pure internal refactor — left exactly as-is, named here rather than
  quietly normalized.
- **`EvaluatedX` dataclasses are now trivial subclasses of a shared `_EvaluatedEntry` base**, not
  aliases — checked that this is actually the *more* correct choice, not just less code:
  dataclass-generated `__eq__` compares `self.__class__ is other.__class__` first, so
  `EvaluatedWidth(...) == EvaluatedNocCandidate(...)` with coincidentally-identical field values
  correctly stays unequal (falls through to `NotImplemented` on class mismatch) — true before this
  refactor (five separate classes) and still true after (five separate subclasses), never
  collapsed into one shared concrete class that would have made that comparison a real, silent
  possibility. `repr()` uses `self.__class__.__qualname__` (dataclass-generated), confirmed to
  still print the real subclass name (`EvaluatedWidth(...)`, not `_EvaluatedEntry(...)`).
- **Real, measured reduction, reported honestly against the original estimate, not inflated**: the
  five strategy files went from 1,634 to 1,163 lines (~29% cut, the shared logic now living once
  in a 207-line `_engine.py`) — a real, meaningful reduction, but short of D30's own "~650–750
  lines" ceiling estimate, since this refactor deliberately kept full per-axis prompt text,
  parsers, docstrings, `__all__` exports, and each class's own `k != 1` error message intact for
  readability and zero observable-behavior risk, rather than squeezing to the theoretical minimum.
- **Full regression, the actual proof this changed nothing observable**: all 85 existing unit
  tests across the five strategy test files pass unchanged (`propose`/`observe`/`done`,
  markdown-fence parsing, fallback-on-invalid-proposal, fallback-on-repeat, evaluator-refusal
  handling, prompt content, `to_dict()` JSON-safety — every one of these behaviors, per axis,
  reverified against the refactored code, not just re-run and assumed still meaningful). The full
  unit suite: 566 passed / 22 skipped, unchanged from before this decision. **All 10 live
  integration tests across all 5 axes** (real Ollama `qwen2.5-coder:7b` + real ZigZag/Booksim2,
  covering the full candidate space and reproducing each axis's own already-proven optimum) pass
  unchanged — the strongest available proof, since these are the tests that would have caught any
  subtle behavioral drift the unit tests' fake evaluators couldn't. A downstream consumer
  (`flux_agentic_dse_loop`'s own Phase-4-exit-criterion live test, which calls
  `run_agentic_architecture_search` through several more layers of indirection) also re-verified
  passing.

**Implications.**
- D30's own deliberately-deferred item is now closed, with the dedicated regression proof it
  explicitly asked for — not a drive-by.
- A real, if modest, template for future strategy additions: a sixth agentic axis would now only
  need its own prompt/parser/converter/report file, inheriting the propose/observe/done skeleton
  rather than re-copying it — the maintenance cost D30 flagged (five files to keep in sync by
  hand) is now structurally lower, though the `skipped_not_expressible`/`skipped_infeasible`
  naming split shows that hand-copied duplication had already drifted once before this refactor
  existed to prevent it.
- No behavior, public API, or test outcome changed anywhere in this repo — confirmed by running
  every test that could plausibly have caught a regression, not assumed from the diff's own
  plausibility, matching the standing methodology this whole session has followed throughout.

## D58. Benchmark corpus objectives + a real leaderboard — closing gap-analysis.md G13's "no
leaderboard" half, and a genuine second benchmark family

**Decision.** Two real, additive pieces closing G13 ("No agreed set of (workload, architecture-
family, objective, constraint) problems exists for comparing search strategies or cost models
head-to-head"): (1) `CorpusEntry` gains an optional `objective` field (`Objective(metric,
minimize)`, `stores/src/flux_store/corpus.py`) — the piece `corpus/README.md` had named "not
implemented" since D11 — declared on all 6 real corpus manifests; (2) a new
`stores/src/flux_store/leaderboard.py` (`rank_results_for_entry`) that ranks every stored
`ResultStore` result for a corpus entry's workload — across every architecture anyone has ever
evaluated it against, not just that entry's own named `arch_path` — by its declared objective,
best first. Wired as a new, read-only CHIA node + MCP tool, `flux_leaderboard` (the 25th),
holdout-safe by construction (looks `entry_id` up via `public_entries()` only, same shape as
`flux_list_public_corpus`, D11).

**A genuine second benchmark family added, not just a schema field.** The corpus had exactly one
workload (`mlp-gemm0.yaml`) paired with four architecture-width variants since D3 — no second,
differently-shaped problem existed to demonstrate a leaderboard actually comparing across a real
architecture *family*, not just re-deriving one entry's own single number. Two new architecture
IR documents were materialized via `generate_memory_size_candidates` (D26, a real, already-tested
generator, not hand-authored) at `gbuf` = 1.25 KiB and 64.0 KiB, re-verified against real ZigZag
before being written to disk (1.25 KiB reproduced the exact already-pinned real number,
1116618.0081255918 pJ; 64.0 KiB gave a real, freshly-measured 1116738.826398288 pJ, confirming the
same monotonic-energy-with-size shape D26 found). Both added to `corpus/public/` with
`objective={metric: energy_pj, minimize: true}` — a genuinely different objective from the
width-axis entries' `latency_cycles`, sharing the same workload.

**Why.** The user-chosen next direction after D57; the most broadly-impactful still-open gap not
blocked on unavailable external tooling (unlike the synthesis-fidelity rung or the torus-capable
NoC evaluator, both still blocked on missing PDK/tooling per `docs/roadmap.md`).

**What was verified — including a real, corrected test assumption, not trusted on a first
guess:**
- **Corpus breadth doesn't include the DMA/LLM-decode example workloads** (`ir/workload/examples/
  soc-dma-desc-fetch.yaml`, `llama3-8b-decode-layer0.yaml`) — checked, not assumed: both are
  deliberately-not-expressible-by-any-real-evaluator schema fixtures (dynamic shapes, a
  `compute_kernel` escape hatch), so neither could ever populate a real leaderboard with real
  numbers. The memory-size axis (same workload, different real architecture dimension) was the
  real, available way to add a second family without inventing an untested workload from scratch.
- **`objective` is optional, not required** — backward-compatible by construction: `test_corpus.py`'s
  pre-existing synthetic fixtures (no `objective` field) still load and pass unchanged, `objective`
  simply parses to `None`. `leaderboard.py`'s own functions are the ones that require it, raising a
  named `LeaderboardEntryError`, not the loader silently rejecting an otherwise-valid manifest.
- **A real, found breaking change caught and fixed properly, not worked around**: adding the two
  new public entries changed `CorpusStore.public_entries()`'s real return value, which
  `test_calibration_live.py`'s own `_PUBLIC_ENTRIES = _CORPUS.public_entries()` (unfiltered) relied
  on being exactly the 3 width-axis entries — this would have pulled the new energy-axis
  architectures into a fixture written to run Timeloop/ZigZag over specifically the latency-
  calibration family. Fixed by filtering `_PUBLIC_ENTRIES` to `objective.metric == "latency_cycles"`
  — the *correct* fix now that a real structured `objective` field exists to filter on, not a
  name-convention guess. Two more hardcoded exact-match corpus-content assertions found and updated
  the same way (`test_chia_flux_knowledge_and_store_live.py`, `test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`'s
  `list_public_corpus`/tool-registration tests) — found by grepping every real consumer of
  `public_entries()`/`CorpusStore(`, not assumed to be limited to the one file already being edited.
- **A real, corrected test assumption of my own, caught by an actual live-test failure, not
  trusted on a first guess**: the first version of the live leaderboard test asserted the
  gbuf=1.25 KiB entry would rank #1 by `energy_pj` across *every* real architecture in the corpus.
  It didn't — the width-axis v2 entry (X=4, the narrowest array) has even lower absolute energy
  (561367.5287841092 pJ), a real finding: D26 only ever proved 1.25 KiB is optimal *within the
  width=8 memory-size sweep*, never that it's the global energy minimum across every architecture
  this corpus now contains. Corrected the test to assert the actually-true, narrower claim
  (gbuf1p25kb beats gbuf64kb specifically) and documented the real cross-family finding directly
  in the test rather than silently loosening the assertion to make it pass.
- **Full, real, end-to-end proof** (`tests/integration/test_leaderboard_live.py`): every public
  corpus entry evaluated through real ZigZag, stored in one real `ResultStore`, ranked correctly —
  latency-axis leaderboard puts X=16 (778 cycles, the real proven fastest) first; energy-axis
  leaderboard correctly orders the two memory-size entries; the holdout entry (v4) is unreachable
  through `public_entries()`-based lookup, checked directly; the CHIA node and the real MCP tool
  (chained with a real `evaluate` tool call over the wire, a self-consistent check against
  whatever `evaluate` itself just returned rather than a hardcoded number, since the module-scoped
  MCP server's history isn't fully controlled by this one test) both verified.
- **19 new unit tests** (8 in `tests/unit/test_leaderboard.py` — pure ranking logic against a
  synthetic `ResultStore`, no real evaluator; 4 new in `tests/unit/test_corpus.py` — objective
  parsing, optionality, JSON-safety) plus **7 new/updated integration tests** across
  `test_leaderboard_live.py`, `test_calibration_live.py`, `test_chia_flux_knowledge_and_store_
  live.py`, and `test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`.
- **Full regression**: 578 passed / 22 skipped on the complete unit suite (up from D57's 566, 0
  failed), plus a combined 25-test run across every corpus/leaderboard/calibration/store
  integration suite together — confirming the objective-filter fix and the two new corpus
  entries didn't silently break anything already depending on the corpus's exact prior contents.

**Implications.**
- G13 is now closed on both halves it names: objective definitions exist (`Objective`), and a real
  ranking/leaderboard capability exists (`rank_results_for_entry` + `flux_leaderboard`) — built
  entirely on `ResultStore.find_results()`, no new storage engine.
- Genuine corpus breadth grew from one benchmark family to two (latency-minimizing width sweep,
  energy-minimizing memory-size sweep) — still both sharing one workload (`mlp-gemm0.yaml`), so
  "many small benchmarks... over/under estimates can't cancel out" (`docs/roadmap.md`'s own
  validation-methodology principle) remains only partially addressed: real breadth across
  genuinely *different* workloads (not just different architecture axes of the same one) is still
  open, blocked on authoring or sourcing a workload real evaluators can actually run — the DMA and
  LLM-decode example workloads were checked and found unsuitable for exactly that reason.
- A real, second confirmation (after D55) that "rank across the whole architecture family, not
  just one entry's own point" surfaces genuine, sometimes counter-intuitive cross-family
  competition — worth remembering before ever assuming one axis's proven optimum is the global
  optimum once the corpus has more than one axis in it.

## D59. A real, genuinely different second workload — closing the multi-workload gap D58 flagged

**Decision.** Author `ir/workload/examples/mlp-ffn0.yaml`: a real, two-layer feedforward block
(a down-projection `(B,C)x(C,H)->(B,H)` immediately followed by an up-projection
`(B,H)x(H,K)->(B,K)`), added to the corpus as `mlp-ffn0-simple-npu-1d-v1` (`corpus/public/`,
objective `latency_cycles`, paired with the same `simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml` X=8 architecture
`mlp-gemm0-simple-npu-1d-v1` already uses). The user-chosen next direction after D58, which had
explicitly flagged genuine multi-workload breadth as the one part of G13 still open — every corpus
entry before this one shared `mlp-gemm0.yaml`, varying only the architecture.

**A real structural constraint checked and worked within, not worked around.**
`evaluators/zigzag/workload_translator.py`'s own docstring is explicit about its v0.1 scope: "a
single Flux `einsum` op with exactly two input operands (bilinear)" — there is no conv/depthwise/
fused-op support, so no single *op* can have a differently-shaped equation from a plain GEMM; every
ZigZag-expressible op is, underneath, the same bilinear-contraction pattern. Checked this via the
real translator source before designing anything, rather than assuming a "different-looking"
single-op workload would actually exercise anything new. The real, available axis for genuine
difference at this same v0.1 scope: `workload_to_zigzag_layers` already translates *every* real
`einsum` op in a workload's `ops` list into its own ZigZag layer — multi-layer workloads are a
real, already-supported (if previously unexercised by this corpus) capability, not something new
to build.

**What was verified, not assumed:**
- **Confirmed the two existing schema-example workloads remain genuinely unsuitable**, not just
  assumed still-true from D58's own note: `soc-dma-desc-fetch.yaml` (a `compute_kernel`/
  `data_dependent`-only workload, no `einsum` op at all — `workload_to_zigzag_layers` raises
  `NotExpressibleError` outright, "no real evaluator can express this at all," not a translation
  gap) and `llama3-8b-decode-layer0.yaml` (dynamic `{dyn: [...]}` bounds ZigZag's translator
  explicitly rejects as non-static) — both deliberate, correct rejections by design, not bugs to
  route around.
- **Verified the multi-layer aggregation claim empirically before writing the workload YAML**,
  not assumed from reading the translator source alone: ran the real two-layer FFN through real
  `ZigZagEvaluator` (latency_cycles=1560.0, energy_pj=1124668.7583788123), then ran the *first
  layer alone* for comparison (784.0 / 565134.3791894062) — confirmed the two-layer total is
  genuinely non-additive relative to one layer alone (not simply 2×, since each layer's own
  overhead differs), the real, checked proof `get_hardware_performance_zigzag` actually aggregates
  across both layers rather than silently reporting only one.
- **A second real, breaking-change-caught-and-fixed pattern, the same shape D58 already found
  once**: the new entry's `objective.metric` (`latency_cycles`) collides with the width-axis
  family's own objective metric — `test_calibration_live.py`'s `_PUBLIC_ENTRIES` filter (D58's own
  fix, filtered by `objective.metric == "latency_cycles"`) was no longer specific enough on its
  own, since it would now also match this real, different-workload entry. Tightened to filter by
  `workload_path == "ir/workload/examples/mlp-gemm0.yaml"` directly — the actually-correct
  selection criterion this test needed all along (calibrating *that* workload's residuals), not a
  one-off patch. Two more hardcoded exact-match corpus-content assertions
  (`test_chia_flux_knowledge_and_store_live.py`, `test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`) found and updated
  for the sixth real entry, the same grep-every-consumer discipline D58 established.
- **Real, end-to-end leaderboard proof this new family stays correctly isolated**: a new live test
  confirms `rank_results_for_entry` for the `mlp-ffn0` entry returns exactly one standing (the only
  architecture ever evaluated against it so far) at the real, previously-verified aggregate value —
  and, structurally, that a shared `objective.metric` between two entries for *different* workloads
  never causes cross-contamination (`workload_hash` alone gates what competes), confirmed by running
  all three real families through one shared `ResultStore` and checking each ranks independently.
- **Full regression**: 578 passed / 22 skipped on the complete unit suite (unchanged from D58, 0
  failed — this decision added no new unit tests, judged proportionate since the real, live
  integration test already exercises schema validity, translation, evaluation, and ranking
  end-to-end for the new workload; a schema-only unit test would have been redundant with it), plus
  the full calibration/store/leaderboard integration suites re-run and passing with the corrected
  filter and updated corpus-count expectations.

**Implications.**
- `corpus/` now has two real workloads (three benchmark families total: width, memory-size, and
  the new FFN family) — genuine, if still modest, multi-workload breadth toward
  `docs/roadmap.md`'s "many small benchmarks... over/under estimates can't cancel out" principle.
- A second real confirmation that `CorpusEntry.objective`'s metric name alone is not a reliable
  way to select "the family I mean" once the corpus has more than one workload sharing a metric —
  `workload_path`/`workload_hash` is the real, structural identity a caller should filter or key
  on, objective is what to rank by once a family is already selected. Worth remembering for any
  future corpus consumer, not just the two test files fixed here.
- The real v0.1 constraint this decision worked within (ZigZag's translator has no non-bilinear op
  support) is now a documented, checked fact rather than an implicit assumption — a future,
  genuinely different *op-shape* benchmark (e.g. a real conv or depthwise pattern) needs either a
  translator extension or a different backend (RTL/SystemC's own generation framework, D39-D56,
  has no such single-op-shape restriction) to add, not just another workload YAML.

## D60. `mlp-ffn0` added to the cross-backend conformance suite — a real, empirically-probed
expressibility matrix, including a genuine multi-op rejection found in both adapters

**Decision.** Add `mlp-ffn0` (D59's new workload) to `tests/conformance/test_backend_conformance.py`'s
shared `WORKLOADS` list — the same suite `docs/architecture.md` describes as the one place every
(backend, workload, architecture) combination in `ir/*/examples/` is checked against a real,
empirically-recorded expected outcome, not a per-adapter ad hoc fixture. Two new real successes
recorded: `(zigzag, mlp-ffn0, simple-npu-1d-v1)` → 1560.0 cycles (matching D59's own pinned
number) and `(zigzag, mlp-ffn0, simple-npu-v1)` → 208.0 cycles, a genuinely new real number this
decision is the first to measure. Every `(timeloop, mlp-ffn0, *)` combination stays the suite's
own default `"fail"`.

**Why.** D59's own multi-layer workload was verified end-to-end against exactly one architecture
(`simple-npu-1d-v1`) and exactly one backend (ZigZag) — real, but narrower than this repo's own
established conformance-suite discipline, which the file's own docstring states plainly: "adding a
[new] workload later means adding one entry to `WORKLOADS`... the corpus and the test logic don't
change." Leaving `mlp-ffn0` out of that shared matrix would have been an inconsistency with the
suite's own stated purpose, not a deliberate scope choice.

**What was verified — probed empirically across all 8 real (backend, architecture) combinations
before writing a single expected value, per this file's own explicit stated discipline ("`EXPECTED`
was populated by actually running every combination... not derived from reading the translators'
code and guessing"):**
- `(zigzag, mlp-ffn0, generic-riscv-soc-v1)` and `(zigzag, mlp-ffn0, my-npu-v3)` both fail — for
  the same pre-existing, unrelated-to-this-workload architecture-translation reasons `mlp-gemm0`
  already fails on both (`generic-riscv-soc-v1`'s compute node has no `attrs.dims`; `my-npu-v3`'s
  `dram` level has no numeric `attrs.size_kb`) — real, checked, not assumed to still hold just
  because they held for the single-op workload.
- `(zigzag, mlp-ffn0, simple-npu-1d-v1)` succeeds at exactly 1560.0 cycles — an exact match to
  D59's own already-verified number, a real cross-check that this suite's independent evaluation
  path (a fresh `ZigZagEvaluator()` instance, not the one D59's own live test constructed) agrees.
- `(zigzag, mlp-ffn0, simple-npu-v1)` succeeds too, at 208.0 cycles — genuinely new: D59 never
  tried this 2D (X,Y) architecture against the new workload. Confirms ZigZag's own auto-mapping
  search generalizes to a 2D array for a 2-layer workload, not just the 1D case D59 checked.
- **Every `(timeloop, mlp-ffn0, *)` combination fails, for the same real reason on all four
  architectures**: `TimeloopEvaluator`'s adapter explicitly raises `NotExpressibleError` the
  moment it sees more than one `einsum` op (`"TimeloopEvaluator v0.1 evaluates exactly one op per
  call"`) — before any architecture-specific translation is even attempted. Checked directly by
  reading `evaluators/timeloop/adapter.py`'s own source first (a real, deliberate, already-
  existing `len(einsum_ops) > 1` guard, not new to this decision), then confirmed empirically
  against all four architectures rather than trusted from the source read alone — the same
  "read the source, then verify, don't stop at either alone" discipline this whole session has
  followed throughout.
- `mlp-ffn0` does not create a new "two backends agree on the same pair" case (Timeloop never
  succeeds on it) — `test_backends_that_both_succeed_on_the_same_pair_agree_on_what_they_were_given`
  still passes unchanged, still exercising exactly the one pre-existing qualifying pair
  (`mlp-gemm0` x `simple-npu-1d-v1`) — an honest, checked fact, not glossed over: this new
  workload has no cross-backend-agreement data yet, only ZigZag ever evaluates it successfully.
- **Full regression**: the conformance suite itself grew from 25 to 33 passing tests (8 new
  parametrized cases: 4 architectures × 2 backends for the new workload), all passing.

**Implications.**
- `mlp-ffn0` is now a first-class member of this repo's one shared conformance corpus, not a
  workload only ever exercised by its own dedicated test file — any future third backend added to
  `_BACKENDS` automatically gets checked against it too, no separate wiring needed.
- A second, independent confirmation of D59's own real finding (Timeloop's adapter cannot express
  any multi-op workload, on any architecture) — this decision is the first to check that claim
  against all four of this repo's real example architectures at once, not just the one D59
  originally verified against.
