## D82. Real multi-core Architecture IR + a full, registered `StreamEvaluator` — closing the last
remaining piece of the Stream integration arc D80/D81 opened, discovering the hard part was
already built

**Decision.** A new Architecture IR block, `interconnect.multi_core` (`ir/src/flux_ir/schemas/
architecture.schema.json`, documented to the same depth `chiplet_noc` already established):
`cores[]` (each a genuine, recursive, single-core Flux Architecture IR document — no `dram`-class
memory level), `core_links[]` (real point-to-point or shared-bus inter-core bandwidth), and
`offchip_core_id`. Top-level `hierarchy` is relaxed from `minItems: 1` to `minItems: 0` — a
genuinely multi-core architecture's real structure lives entirely inside `interconnect.multi_core`
now, not at the top level. A new package, `evaluators/stream/`, translates this block into a real
Stream multi-core hardware YAML bundle (`architecture_translator.py`) and composes it with D81's
own workload exporter into a full, registered `StreamEvaluator` (`adapter.py`) — `"stream"` in
`flux_cli.registry`, reachable through the generic `flux_evaluate` CHIA node, no dedicated tool
needed, the same shape D64/D74/D75 already established.

**Why.** D81's own record named this exact remaining piece explicitly: "a real multi-core
Architecture IR concept... deliberately deferred." A bare "continue" went straight to it. Before
designing a new schema concept, D80's own real, already-verified finding was checked first: a
real Stream per-core hardware config (`cores/tpu_like.yaml`) was read directly against
`evaluators/zigzag/architecture_translator.py`'s own real output — structurally identical
(`memories`/`operational_array`, same real field names). This was the decisive finding: the hard
part (real per-operand memory/port/bandwidth translation) was **already built and already
validated**, sitting in a completely different package for an unrelated reason. Given a genuine
design choice between a narrow "reuse Stream's own cores by name" v0.1 and this fuller
per-core-translation approach, the user chose the fuller one — made real and low-risk by this
exact reuse discovery, not a from-scratch undertaking.

**What was verified — real, incremental proof at every layer, the translator confirmed against
real Stream before the full adapter was assembled:**
- **A real schema addition**, JSON-validated, documented to the same depth every other real
  `interconnect` block already carries — `additionalProperties: true` throughout means no
  existing document was invalidated by this change (confirmed: the full conformance suite still
  passes unchanged).
- **11 new unit tests** (`test_stream_architecture_translator.py`): the real dual-core example
  translates to the exact expected `hardware.yaml`/per-core-YAML structure; rejections for no
  `multi_core` block, empty `cores`, a core missing its own `architecture`, a core declaring a
  `dram`-class memory level, duplicate core ids, `core_links` referencing an undeclared core,
  non-positive bandwidth, and an `offchip_core_id` colliding with a real compute core's own id;
  a 3-core shared-bus link correctly typed `"bus"` (Stream's own real convention, `"link"` for
  exactly 2 cores); no declared `coordinates` correctly omits `core_coordinates` entirely (not a
  silently-invented default).
- **A real, hand-built two-core architecture** (`ir/architecture/examples/
  simple-npu-1d-dual-core-v1.yaml`) — two real compute cores (each `simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml`'s own
  gbuf/pe_array shape, minus its own `dram` level), real inter-core links, a real off-chip core
  — translated and run through actual Stream *before* the full adapter existed, confirming the
  translator's own real output (`Core(0, zigzag.compute)` in Stream's own log) works standalone:
  `total_latency=1148.0`.
- **The full `StreamEvaluator`, composing all three pieces**, verified end to end twice — once
  calling `.evaluate()` directly, once through the generic `flux_evaluate` CHIA node — both
  reproducing the identical real number (`latency_cycles=1148.0`, `provenance.evaluator=
  "stream-dse@real"`). 4 new integration tests (`test_stream_multicore_live.py`): the real
  dual-core run pinned exactly, the CHIA-node round trip, a single-core architecture (no
  `multi_core` block) correctly rejected, and an explicit `Candidate.mapping` correctly rejected
  (Stream's own real value proposition is automatic allocation + mapping search).
- **A second, deeper look at D81's own flaky-test fix, found insufficient, not just re-tried**:
  this decision's own full-suite regression check hit the *same* `test_search_annealing_strategy.py`
  failure D81 had already "fixed" with a discarded warm-up run — reproduced again, with a real
  ~12x speed variance between two back-to-back calls even with that warm-up in place. The warm-up
  fix was real but insufficient: comparing two *separately-timed* calls stays genuinely fragile
  under real system load (CPU scheduling/cache-state noise from running alongside hundreds of
  other tests), not something a single warm-up call fully controls for. Redesigned properly this
  time: a single real call with `max_iterations=10⁶` and a tiny fixed `wall_clock_budget_s=0.05`
  — robust because it doesn't depend on two calls running at comparable relative speed at all,
  only on this evaluator's own real per-iteration cost (tens of microseconds) making 10⁶
  iterations take real seconds regardless of system load. Verified fixed for real this time: 3/3
  clean full-suite runs (the failure condition D81 left unresolved).
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **760 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D81's 749: 11 new `evaluators/stream` unit tests, 0 net change
  from the flaky-test redesign), confirmed stable across three independent full-suite runs. The
  4 new integration tests confirmed passing separately.

**Implications.**
- The Stream integration arc this session opened at D80 is now genuinely complete: real
  plumbing (D80), real workload translation (D81), real architecture translation and a full,
  registered evaluator (D82) — `docs/roadmap.md`'s own Phase 5 "multi-core" item, named as
  fully open at the start of this arc, is real now, not aspirational.
- The real, generalizable lesson this decision adds to D78's own ("check whether an existing
  dependency already covers a 'new' gap before building from scratch"): the check isn't only
  about *external* tools — `evaluators/zigzag`'s own architecture translator, built for a
  completely unrelated single-core evaluator, turned out to already solve the hardest part of
  this decision's own real work. Worth checking this repo's *own* existing code for a structural
  match before assuming new translation logic is needed, not just the field's own external tools.
- Real, explicitly-named future work, not attempted here: layer fusion (`intra_core_tiling`,
  Stream's own other real headline capability), energy/power/area metrics beyond
  `latency_cycles`, and pooling/SIMD auxiliary core types (no real workload shape in this repo
  yet would route to them).

## D84. Real bottleneck reporting for `StreamEvaluator` — replacing a placeholder with Stream's
own real, structured cost breakdown

**Decision.** `StreamEvaluator.evaluate()` now builds a real `Bottleneck` from Stream's own real
`StageContext.data["group_allocations"][group_id]["performance"]` structure — `bottleneck.
{compute_bound_cycles, transfer_bound_cycles, compute_bound_pct, transfer_bound_pct}` and
`aggregate.{compute_cores_available, compute_cores_used,
latency_weighted_mac_spatial_utilization}` — instead of the placeholder
`Bottleneck(limiter=Limiter.DEPENDENCY)` with no supporting data D82 shipped. `Limiter.COMPUTE`
or `Limiter.NOC` (real inter-core/off-chip transfer, not a generic memory stall) is chosen by
whichever real percentage dominates; multiple real fusion groups (v0.1 never actually produces
more than one, but the aggregation is real and checked regardless) sum cycles and recompute
percentages from the sums, never average percentages directly — a real, checked
"don't silently get this wrong" case this decision's own tests exist to catch.

**Why.** A bare "continue" after D83's own explicit checkpoint. Rather than force a new gap-
analysis item from an already-thin list, this picked up one of D82's own explicitly-deferred
items (energy/power/area metrics) and checked it directly rather than assuming: a real Stream run
was probed field by field (`ctx.data.keys()`, then `group_allocations[0]`'s own real, nested
`performance` dict) to see what Stream's own real output actually contains. Energy/power/area
turned out to be genuinely absent (confirmed, not assumed) — but the probe surfaced a different,
real, valuable structure this repo's own "Explainable-DSE" design principle (docs/gap-analysis.md
G4) directly calls for and `StreamEvaluator` wasn't using at all: a real, structured
bottleneck breakdown, sitting unused since D82.

**What was verified — real field-by-field inspection before any code was written, then a real
end-to-end confirmation:**
- **Real inspection, not documentation-reading**: `ctx.data.keys()` listed after a real run
  (`['accelerator', 'backend', ..., 'group_allocations', ..., 'total_latency', ...]`) — no
  `energy`/`power`/`cost`/`edp` key anywhere at the top level. Drilling into
  `group_allocations[0]["performance"]` found the real, structured
  `{schema_version, latency, bottleneck, aggregate, nodes}` shape used here — confirmed against
  the real numbers already established in D82 (828 compute-bound / 320 transfer-bound cycles,
  72.13%/27.87%, 2/2 real cores used, matching `total_latency=1148.0` exactly:
  828+320=1148).
- **6 new unit tests** (`test_stream_bottleneck.py`): the real dual-core shape correctly reports
  `Limiter.COMPUTE`; a synthetic transfer-dominated case correctly reports `Limiter.NOC`; an exact
  tie defaults to `Limiter.COMPUTE`; empty `group_allocations` reports `Limiter.DEPENDENCY` with
  no fabricated data (an honest "no data" case) rather than a silently-faked compute-bound result;
  two synthetic differently-sized groups aggregate by summing real cycles and recomputing
  percentages from the sums (not naively averaging two groups' own percentages, a real, checked
  correctness case); core counts take the real max across groups, not a nonsensical sum.
- **Real end-to-end confirmation**: the existing dual-core integration test extended with real
  bottleneck assertions — `Limiter.COMPUTE`, `compute_bound_cycles=828.0`,
  `transfer_bound_cycles=320.0`, `compute_cores_available=compute_cores_used=2.0` — all matching
  the hand-probed real numbers exactly, `latency_cycles` unchanged at `1148.0` (a purely additive
  change, no regression to the already-verified core metric).
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **766 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D83's 760: 6 new unit tests). The extended integration test and the
  cross-evaluator leaderboard test (D83, which also exercises `StreamEvaluator`) both confirmed
  passing separately.

**Implications.**
- `evaluators/stream`'s own "Not modelled at all" section now states energy/power/area absence as
  a *checked fact* about Stream's own real output, not an unverified assumption — a small but
  real precision improvement matching this whole session's own standing discipline.
- A real, generalizable lesson for any future "what does this real tool actually report" question:
  probing a live object's own real attribute/dict keys directly (`ctx.data.keys()`, then drilling
  into whatever nested structure appears) found real, valuable data this repo's own design
  principles already asked for, that neither Stream's own docs nor this repo's own prior
  decisions had surfaced — worth doing before writing off a "not modelled" line as final.

## D85. Closing G11's real remaining piece: CHIA's submodule-fetch bug was fixed upstream —
`flake.nix`'s pin just hadn't caught up

**Decision.** `flake.nix`'s `chia` derivation now pins CHIA to `098764c04c1260ee83b324153539bec6febab684`
(2026-08-10), 14 commits past the previous pin (`beda03db84045b7b3e43873c6e3045d1033f0120`, D23).
The derivation's `pname` changes from `"chia"` to `"chialoops"` to match — the same upstream
commit that fixes the submodule issue also renamed the *distribution* (not the import package or
console script, both still `chia`) for real PyPI publication, since plain `chia` on PyPI belongs
to an unrelated project. `flows/chia_nodes/README.md` and one integration-test docstring are
updated to state the fix as verified fact, not the old workaround as still-necessary.

**Why.** The user picked this up explicitly as one of four gap-analysis items to work through
this session (alongside G5, G9, G16) after a git-state cleanup pass. G11's own status row named
one concrete open piece: "CHIA's own submodule-fetch bug still requires a `--no-deps` workaround."
Worth checking whether that was still true before doing anything else with it.

**What was verified — real, from scratch, not assumed from the existing D23/README text:**
- **The actual root cause, read directly from CHIA's own `pyproject.toml` at the old pin**: no
  `include=` restriction under `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]`, only an `exclude=` list — so
  setuptools' default namespace-package discovery walked into `examples/benchmarks` and
  `examples/riscv_extensions/prebuilt_stress` (two git submodules) whenever they weren't fetched,
  and broke.
- **A genuinely surprising finding along the way**: a real `git clone --recurse-submodules`
  (unshallowed) of CHIA's own upstream repo still leaves `examples/benchmarks/` completely empty
  — `git submodule update` reports `fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref
  6c0ac99f273c2d720586c27e6856e26ca8a1495c`. Confirmed via GitHub's own commits API
  (`GET /repos/ucb-bar/chia_benchmarks/commits/6c0ac99...` → `422 No commit found for SHA`) that
  this isn't a transient fetch failure — the pinned submodule commit is permanently unreachable,
  a dangling gitlink in CHIA's own git history (most likely a force-push/rebase in the
  `chia_benchmarks` fork after CHIA's superproject last pinned it). `--recurse-submodules` could
  never have recovered this, regardless of shallow vs. full clone — a real, load-bearing finding:
  the nix derivation's own existing `doCheck = false` + explicit `propagatedBuildInputs`
  workaround (sidestepping dependency resolution entirely, chosen over trying `fetchSubmodules`)
  was the *only* viable route for the nix path, not merely the path taken.
- **Upstream already fixed the actual bug**, unprompted, before this decision: `git log -- pyproject.toml`
  on CHIA's own repo shows `84851e5` ("Prepare pyproject.toml for PyPI publication") added
  `include = ["chia*"]` — scoping package discovery away from `examples/`/`docs/`/`test/`
  entirely, submodules fetched or not. That commit sits between the old pin and current HEAD.
  Confirmed by reading `pyproject.toml` at both the old pin and HEAD directly (`git show
  <rev>:pyproject.toml`), not inferred from a changelog.
- **The 14 commits between the old pin and the new one, checked for anything that could break
  Flux, not assumed safe**: `git diff --stat` shows only `chia/chipyard/{cosim_node,
  riscv_dv_gen_node}.py`, `chia/cli/*`, `chia/cluster/*` changed. Cross-checked against every
  `from chia...import` this repo actually has (`grep -rn "^from chia\|^import chia"`): only
  `chia.base.ChiaFunction`, `chia.base.tools.ChiaTool`, `chia.vlsi.sram_cacti.*`,
  `chia.simulators.gem5.Gem5Node`, `chia.models.ollama.OllamaLLM` — none overlap with the changed
  files. `pyproject.toml`'s own `version = "0.1.0"` is unchanged across the bump too (checked
  directly — nixpkgs' `pythonMetadataCheckPhase` enforces this must match the derivation's
  `version`).
- **Real, disposable-venv proof the fix actually works**: fresh `git clone --recurse-submodules`
  of CHIA at the new pin, then a plain `python3 -m venv` + `pip install -e .` — **no `--no-deps`**
  — succeeded outright: real dependency resolution, ~90 packages installed, despite
  `examples/benchmarks/` still being genuinely empty (the dangling-commit finding above). Then
  confirmed every module Flux actually imports still resolves from that install
  (`from chia.base.ChiaFunction import ChiaFunction, get`, `chia.vlsi.sram_cacti.cacti_runner`,
  `chia.simulators.gem5.Gem5Node` — all real imports, not just a bare `import chia`).
- **The nix path itself, not just the plain-pip path**: updated `flake.nix`'s `rev`/`sha256`,
  rebuilt with `nix build .#devShells.x86_64-linux.default` — first attempt failed with a real,
  new (not previously seen) error: nixpkgs' `pythonMetadataCheckPhase` reporting `No package
  metadata was found for chia`, because the wheel's real METADATA `Name` is now `chialoops` (the
  same commit that fixed packages.find also renamed the PyPI distribution — read directly from
  `[project] name = "chialoops"` in `pyproject.toml`, with a comment explaining the rename is
  exactly for the PyPI name-collision reason above). Fixed by changing the derivation's own
  `pname` from `"chia"` to `"chialoops"` — nix attribute name (`chia`, used by every caller in
  this flake) is unaffected. Second build succeeded cleanly.
- **Full regression against the bumped, rebuilt nix shell**: `python3 -m pytest tests/unit/
  tests/conformance/` — **766 passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed**, identical to before the bump. Then,
  separately, the four CHIA-heaviest integration test files — real Ray dispatch
  (`test_chia_flux_evaluate_live.py`), architecture DSE via Ray
  (`test_architecture_dse_chia_live.py`), the `flux_search` node including nested Ray dispatch
  (`test_chia_flux_search_live.py`), and memory characterization via real CACTI plus D79's own
  caching (`test_chia_flux_characterize_memory_level_live.py`) — **28 passed, 0 failed**, real Ray
  instances started fresh each time, not skipped or mocked.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G11 moves from "Partial" to "Mostly closed" — the submodule-fetch piece
  named as the one real open item is genuinely fixed and reverified, not just re-described; what's
  left of G11 is the original, different tier-1 concern (Timeloop/PyTimeloop/islpy-with-Barvinok
  as a real adoption barrier for anyone not using this repo's own nix shell or containers), which
  this decision doesn't touch.
- A real, generalizable lesson matching this whole session's own standing discipline: before
  reproducing or patching around a workaround an earlier decision recorded, check whether the
  upstream problem it was working around has itself moved — D23's note was accurate when written,
  but an unprompted upstream fix silently outdated it. Worth a habit: for any pinned external
  dependency with a documented workaround, periodically re-check whether the workaround is still
  load-bearing, not just whether the pin still builds.
- The "permanently dangling submodule commit" finding is worth remembering in isolation: it means
  this repo's own nix-side workaround (skip submodule fetching, source dependencies explicitly)
  isn't just the *convenient* choice — for `examples/benchmarks` specifically, it is the *only*
  workaround that can ever work against CHIA's current upstream history, short of CHIA re-pinning
  or removing that submodule reference itself.

## D86. Generalizing D79's incremental-caching pattern past its one original consumer —
`flux_sweep_dynamic_shape`/`flux_sweep_moe_routing` gain real warm-start too

**Decision.** `flux_sweep_dynamic_shape` and `flux_sweep_moe_routing` (`flows/chia_nodes/
dynamic_shape.py`/`moe_routing.py`) both gain an optional `result_db_path: str | None = None`
parameter, mirroring `flux_evaluate`/`flux_search`'s own convention exactly (a path, not an
already-open `ResultStore`, unlike D79's `flux_characterize_memory_level(..., store=...)`): when
given, the per-sample evaluator each sweep calls once per entry in `sample_points`/
`routing_samples` is wrapped in `flux_store.CachingEvaluator` before being handed to
`sweep_dynamic_shape`/`sweep_moe_routing`. Neither underlying library function
(`workload_dynamism/src/flux_workload_dynamism/{sweep,moe_routing}.py`) changes at all — the
wrap happens entirely at the CHIA-node call site, the same shape D79 itself used.

**Why.** The user picked this up explicitly as one of four gap-analysis items this session
(alongside G11, G5, G16). G9's own status row named its one real remaining piece precisely:
"this pattern is proven for one narrow, single-consumer case, not generalized to every
evaluator's own dependency shape." Worth actually surveying for a second real case rather than
declaring the gap closed on the strength of one example.

**What was verified — a real survey first, then the same off-the-shelf mechanism applied, not a
new one invented:**
- **The survey itself**: read every file in `flows/chia_nodes/src/flux_chia_nodes/` for its own
  `from`/`import`/`def flux_*` shape. `flux_evaluate` and `flux_search` already had
  `CachingEvaluator` wired (D19, exact-match caching on the full `Candidate`). `flux_sweep_dynamic_shape`
  and `flux_sweep_moe_routing` — both real, both calling `make_evaluator(backend)` raw with zero
  caching of any kind — stood out as a clean, close analogue to D79's own shape: many real,
  potentially-repeated per-sample evaluator calls against the same real backend, with an
  off-the-shelf mechanism (`CachingEvaluator`) already sitting unused one import away. Confirmed
  by reading `sweep.py`/`moe_routing.py` directly: each loops `for value in sample_points:` /
  `for selection in routing_samples:` calling `evaluator.evaluate(...)` once per entry, with no
  deduplication of its own — a literal duplicate entry in the caller's own list was, before this
  decision, always a second real evaluator call.
- **Two distinct kinds of real repeat identified, not assumed**: *within* one call (a duplicate
  value/routing decision in the caller's own list — a real, expected shape for a Monte-Carlo-style
  sampler, MoE routing especially, where a small discrete space of `top_k` combinations gets many
  draws) and *across* calls sharing a store (an overlapping sweep re-probing some of the same
  points, e.g. from a broader agentic search loop revisiting nearby candidates).
- **9 new unit tests** (`test_dynamic_shape_sweep_caching.py`, `test_moe_routing_sweep_caching.py`),
  same discipline as D79's own `_CountingEvaluator` stub: no-`result_db_path` behavior is
  unchanged (real call per sample, every time); a duplicate sample point/routing decision *within
  one call* is a real cache hit; repeating an entire sweep *across calls* is a real cache hit for
  every point after the first sweep; a genuinely different `arch` for the same sample points is a
  real cache miss (D79's own "not over-broad" discipline, re-checked here); and — a correctness
  case specific to MoE routing, not just a hit-rate check — `["expert0","expert1"]` and
  `["expert1","expert0"]` resolve to the byte-identical static workload (`resolve_moe_routing`
  filters by set membership, order-independent, confirmed by reading its own implementation before
  writing the test) and therefore correctly hit cache, not coincidentally.
- **Real, end-to-end confirmation against real ZigZag**, not just the stub: extended
  `tests/integration/test_dynamic_shape_sweep_live.py` and `test_moe_routing_sweep_live.py` with a
  monkeypatched `zigzag.api.get_hardware_performance_zigzag` call counter — the exact same
  technique D79 used against real CACTI's own `run_cacti`, applied to ZigZag's real entry point
  here (found by reading `evaluators/zigzag/src/flux_evaluator_zigzag/adapter.py` directly, not
  guessed). A dynamic-shape sweep over `[1, 8]` then `[1, 8, 1]` against the same store: 2 real
  ZigZag calls total (T=1 and T=8, each exactly once), not 3. A MoE-routing sweep over one routing
  decision, then a second call repeating it in reversed list order: 1 real ZigZag call total,
  reproducing the exact real, previously-pinned number (`494.0`) on the served, cached second
  result.
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **775 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D85's 766: 9 new unit tests). The two extended live-ZigZag
  integration test files (13 tests total, including the two new caching tests) confirmed passing
  separately, run for real, not skipped.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G9 stays "Mostly closed" but its own remaining-piece note is rewritten:
  the pattern now has two independently-verified real consumers (CACTI-backed memory
  characterization, ZigZag-backed dynamic-shape/MoE sweeps), not one — genuinely generalized, not
  just re-asserted. The survey wasn't exhaustive, though: `rtl_dse`/`systemc_dse`'s own real
  Yosys/Verilator calls (`codegen/rtl_harness`'s `compile_and_run_composite`/
  `synthesize_composite`) are a real, currently-uncached call site too, but a structurally
  different shape — whole-composite synthesis with no naturally *reducible* sub-document the way
  `minimal_arch`/per-sample-workload were (Yosys flattens the full hierarchy, so the real
  dependency already *is* the full composite, not a narrower one hiding inside it) — left open,
  named honestly rather than force-fit into this decision's own pattern.
- A real, generalizable lesson worth keeping: the two new consumers found here weren't discovered
  by guessing which nodes "seemed similar" to `flux_characterize_memory_level` — they were found
  by actually reading every CHIA node's own import list for `make_evaluator` calls with no
  adjacent `CachingEvaluator`/`ResultStore` import, a mechanical, repeatable survey step worth
  reusing if this pattern gets generalized further later.

## D87. Real, ingested distribution data for the dynamic-shape case — closing docs/gap-analysis.md
G5's own last-named open piece, half of it

**Decision.** `knowledge/corpus/distributions/kv-cache-len-v1/` now holds real, ingested data: a
real, computed percentile table (0-100, 101 real integer order statistics) derived from the real
`ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json` dataset (Apache-2.0,
`anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered`, HuggingFace) — the first 20,000 real conversations,
each message tokenized with real `tiktoken` `cl100k_base`, recording the real cumulative token
count immediately before every real assistant turn as one real observation (69,601 total). A new
module, `flux_workload_dynamism.distributions` (`load_empirical_distribution`,
`quantile_sample_points`), resolves a `"empirical@corpus/<name>"` reference to this real data and
derives `n` real, evenly-probability-spaced quantile sample points from it — no change to
`sweep_dynamic_shape`'s own aggregation formula at all, since a uniform mean over real
quantile-based points is already a real, standard Monte-Carlo estimate of the distribution's
expectation. `flux_sweep_dynamic_shape` (CHIA node) and its MCP tool both gain an `n_samples`
parameter as an alternative to caller-supplied `sample_points`; `llm-decode-attn-qk0.yaml`'s own
declared `T` range widens `[1, 256]` -> `[1, 4096]` so the real distribution's own mass (p95≈1762)
isn't degenerately clipped away.

A real, documented search for MoE routing-frequency data (HuggingFace + GitHub) found nothing
with clear licensing and clear provenance — `sweep_moe_routing`/`"measured@corpus/..."` stay
placeholder for now, a checked-and-absent finding, not an unwired one.

**Why.** The user picked this up explicitly as one of four gap-analysis items this session
(alongside G11, G9, G16). G5's own status row named its one real remaining piece precisely: "Real
(not placeholder-URI) distribution data — for either dynamic shapes or MoE routing frequencies —
is the one real piece still open." Worth actually resolving it for at least one real case rather
than leaving both halves permanently placeholder.

**What was verified — real data, sourced, licensed, and processed for real, not fabricated:**
- **License checked before ingesting anything** (the same discipline D31 established for
  `knowledge/corpus/riscv-unpriv/`): HuggingFace's own dataset API confirms
  `anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered` is `license:apache-2.0`, checked directly via
  `GET https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/...`, not assumed from the dataset's popularity.
- **Real, streamed processing, never fully downloading the 672 MB source file**: `curl | ijson`
  piped together, parsing conversations incrementally and terminating the source connection once
  20,000 real conversations were read (19,864 non-empty). Real `tiktoken` `cl100k_base`
  tokenization (a real, standard BPE tokenizer, not a `len(text)//4` heuristic) of every message,
  recording the real cumulative token count immediately before every real `"from": "gpt"` turn —
  69,601 real observations, min=1, max=161281, mean≈795.8, median=726 (real, heavily right-skewed,
  matching the real, well-known shape of chat conversation lengths). Only the real, computed
  101-value percentile table (1.7 KB) is vendored into the repo — not the raw dataset — with full
  reproduction details in `knowledge/corpus/distributions/kv-cache-len-v1/PROVENANCE.md`.
- **A real design choice, not a shortcut**: quantile sampling (the midpoint of `n` equal
  probability-mass buckets) turns `sweep_dynamic_shape`'s existing uniform-mean aggregation into a
  real, distribution-weighted estimate with zero changes to that aggregation code — verified by
  hand-checking the math against a synthetic `uniform[0,100]` distribution (`n=4` -> percentiles
  12.5/37.5/62.5/87.5 -> Python's own banker's-rounding gives 12/38/62/88, confirmed by direct
  interpreter check before writing the test that asserts it) before trusting it against the real
  ShareGPT-derived data.
- **The declared-range widening was checked safe, not assumed**: timed real ZigZag calls at
  T=256/1000/1762/4096 (all well under 1.5s) before widening `llm-decode-attn-qk0.yaml`'s own
  `T` bound; confirmed by reading `resolve_dynamic_bound`'s own implementation that a wider `hi`
  never affects evaluation of an already-resolved concrete value — the four already-pinned sample
  points (T=1/8/32/128) still evaluate to the exact same real numbers.
- **A real, documented search for MoE routing-frequency data, not a quiet skip**: HuggingFace
  dataset search (`moe+routing`) surfaced three real candidates, each checked directly — one
  (`TahaBa/flan-routing-MoE-dataset`) is task-clustering data for a routing *predictor*, not real
  per-token expert-selection frequencies from a deployed model; the other two had no license tag
  and unclear/unverifiable provenance. A follow-up GitHub repository search across five real
  queries (`mixtral expert routing frequency`, `switch transformer routing statistics`, `mixture
  of experts load balance dataset`, `expert utilization histogram moe`) returned `total_count: 0`
  or one clearly-unrelated toy CIFAR10 repo. Concluded genuinely absent, not merely unsearched.
- **13 new unit tests** (`test_workload_dynamism_distributions.py`, 9; extending
  `test_dynamic_shape_sweep_live.py`, 3 new integration tests; one new MCP-surface exercise via
  the existing live suite) covering: ref parsing, unknown-name rejection, quantile-bucket
  midpoints, `n=1` reads the real median, `lo`/`hi` clipping, `n<1` rejection, and — against the
  real ingested `kv-cache-len-v1` data with no synthetic override — a real right-skew check
  (median < mean) and monotonic, in-range quantile points.
- **Real, end-to-end confirmation against real ZigZag**: `flux_sweep_dynamic_shape("zigzag",
  workload, "attn.qk", "T", n_samples=5, ...)` against the real workload/real distribution,
  independently re-deriving the exact same expected sample points via
  `dynamic_bound_range`+`load_empirical_distribution`+`quantile_sample_points` called directly,
  not trusting the CHIA node's own internal resolution as self-verifying.
- **Three-surfaces consistency, checked and fixed, not just the new capability**: found
  `flows/mcp/src/flux_mcp/tool.py`'s own `sweep_dynamic_shape`/`sweep_moe_routing` wrappers had
  silently fallen behind D86 too (no `result_db_path` at all) while auditing them for this
  decision's own `n_samples` addition — fixed both in the same pass, so the MCP surface now
  matches the typed function/CHIA node for both D86 and D87 (`corpus_root` deliberately excluded
  from the MCP surface — a local filesystem override with a different risk profile than
  `result_db_path`, not needed by any real remote caller).
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **784 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D86's 775: 9 new distribution unit tests). Real integration suites
  (`test_dynamic_shape_sweep_live.py`, `test_moe_routing_sweep_live.py`,
  `test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`) confirmed passing separately against real ZigZag and the real MCP
  server.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G5 stays "Mostly closed" but its own remaining-piece note now correctly
  distinguishes the two real halves: dynamic-shape distribution data is real now; MoE
  routing-frequency data was searched for and genuinely not found, a different, more durable kind
  of "open" than "nobody tried yet."
- A real, generalizable lesson worth keeping alongside D31/D84's own precedent: "checked and
  confirmed absent" is a real, distinct, more valuable finding than either fabricating a
  substitute or leaving a claim unchecked — recorded here with the exact queries run, so a future
  decision doesn't have to redo the same search from nothing.
- A documentation-process lesson from this same decision's own drafting: appending a new D-entry
  via a string-replacement edit whose `old_string` ends at the "## Still open" header (rather than
  stopping just *before* it) silently deletes that header if `new_string` doesn't reproduce it —
  found and fixed immediately after D85/D86 were mis-inserted past the end of the "Still open"
  list instead of before it. Worth a standing habit: when inserting a new decision, anchor the
  edit on text that ends *before* "## Still open", never on the header itself.

## D88. Real, tested dollar-cost machinery — scoped, not wired to spend real money

**Decision.** `flows/chia_nodes/cost.py` (new): `compute_usd_cost(model, input_tokens,
output_tokens) -> float`, against a real, published per-token pricing table for six real models
across Anthropic and OpenAI (base input/output rates, no cache-tier discounts modeled — a real,
named simplification), sourced directly from each provider's own official pricing docs.
`agentic.py`'s new `CostTrackingProposer` wraps any `LLMProposer` whose own `._llm` exposes real
per-call token usage as `_last_metadata` — real, confirmed behavior of CHIA's own
`chia.models.openai_compat` backend family (found by reading its source directly) — and
accumulates a real, running `total_usd_spent`. **Neither is wired into any real node**: every one
of `agentic.py`'s five CHIA nodes still constructs `_OllamaProposer` only, so
`flux_agentic_dse_loop`'s own `estimated_cost_usd=0.0` stays exactly as correct as it already was.
No real API call, no real spend, anywhere in this decision.

**Why.** The user picked this up explicitly as one of four gap-analysis items this session
(alongside G11, G9, G5) — the AskUserQuestion option offering it was itself framed as "scope what
a real, non-zero dollar figure would need," not "make a real, billed API call." G16's own status
row named the real remaining piece: no real, non-zero dollar figure exists to optimize against,
because no paid API has ever run in this sandbox. Spending real money against a real paid API is
a consequential, outward-facing action this session isn't authorized to take unilaterally — this
decision draws that line deliberately, and builds everything real that's possible before it.

**What was verified — real investigation and real, tested arithmetic, with an explicit boundary
at real spend:**
- **The actual current state, read from the code, not assumed from the gap-analysis summary
  text**: `Provenance.usd_cost` is never populated by any real evaluator adapter anywhere in this
  repo (always `None`, not even a placeholder `0.0`); `Budget.usd` is essentially never read.
  `flux_agentic_dse_loop`'s own `estimated_cost_usd=0.0` (the one real place a dollar figure is
  reported at all) is a hardcoded literal — genuinely honest for what this loop's own code
  actually does (always `_OllamaProposer`, free and local), not a placeholder standing in for a
  real number nobody computed yet.
- **The real structural reason no cost has ever been tracked, found by reading CHIA's own real
  source (a cloned checkout, not guessed)**: `chia.base.llm_call.QueryResult` — the return type
  every real CHIA LLM backend shares — carries no token-usage or cost field at all (`result`,
  `returncode`, `stderr`, `stream_result`, `success` only). A real, wireable mechanism exists
  anyway: `chia/models/openai_compat.py`'s own real implementation captures real
  `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from each real API response's own `usage` field and stores them
  as `self._last_metadata` — a real, accessible instance attribute, just not part of `QueryResult`
  itself. `chia.models.claude.py` is the Claude Code CLI backend (subprocess-based), a genuinely
  different shape with no equivalent token-metadata capture.
- **Real, current, sourced pricing data, not guessed or stale**: fetched directly from
  `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing.md` and
  `https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing.md` (both providers' own official docs, current as of
  2026-08-12) — six real models (`claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `gpt-5`,
  `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-4o`), a deliberately small, hand-picked subset (the same "keep a first
  ingestion small and hand-picked" precedent D3 established for `knowledge/corpus/riscv-unpriv/`),
  base (non-cached) rates only.
- **11 new unit tests** (`test_chia_nodes_cost.py`, `test_cost_tracking_proposer.py`): real
  per-token arithmetic checked by hand (`claude-sonnet-5` at 1M input + 1M output tokens =
  exactly $2 + $10 = $12, computed and verified before trusting the function), linear scaling,
  input priced separately from output, an unpriced model raising `UnknownModelPricingError`
  rather than silently reporting `$0.00` (the real safety property this module exists for),
  negative-token rejection; `CostTrackingProposer` accumulating real cost across multiple calls
  against a synthetic stub shaped exactly like CHIA's own real `_last_metadata` (confirmed
  against the real source before the stub was trusted), returning the wrapped proposer's own real
  response unchanged, treating missing metadata (e.g. a real Ollama backend, which never sets
  `_last_metadata`) as zero cost rather than crashing, and propagating
  `UnknownModelPricingError` for an unpriced model.
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **795 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D87's 784: 11 new unit tests). No integration test exercises
  either new class against a real backend — deliberately, matching the "no real spend" boundary
  this decision draws.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G16 stays "Mostly closed" but its own remaining-piece note is
  rewritten to name precisely what's left: a real, paid backend adapter (the concrete next step
  would be a `_OpenAICompatProposer` analogous to `_OllamaProposer`, wrapping
  `chia.models.openai_compat`) and the real, billed API call that would prove
  `CostTrackingProposer` end to end — both explicitly out of this decision's own scope, not
  forgotten.
- A real, generalizable lesson worth keeping alongside this session's other "checked, not
  assumed" findings: the actual blocker for real cost-tracking wasn't "nobody built the pricing
  math" (that's the easy, safe part, now real and tested) — it was a real, structural gap in
  CHIA's own `QueryResult` type having no usage-reporting channel at all, worked around here by
  reading `_last_metadata` out of band rather than needing an upstream CHIA change.
- A standing boundary worth naming explicitly for any future session picking this back up:
  wiring `CostTrackingProposer` into a real node and proving it against a real paid call requires
  (a) a real API key and (b) the user's own explicit authorization to spend real money — this
  decision deliberately stops short of both, not because the remaining work is hard, but because
  spending real money is a different kind of action than everything else this session did.

## D89. Closing G9's real remainder — real, content-hash-keyed caching for `codegen/rtl_harness`'s
own real Yosys synthesis calls

**Decision.** A new module, `codegen/rtl_harness/src/flux_codegen_rtl_harness/cache.py`:
`content_key(*parts) -> str` (a real, deterministic SHA256 digest) and `ToolResultCache` (a real,
disk-backed SQLite cache mapping a content-hash key to a real, previously-computed tool result —
plain JSON-safe dicts, not a fixed result type, so the same cache serves more than one real result
shape). `synth.synthesize_and_measure` gains an optional `cache: ToolResultCache | None = None`
parameter, keyed on exactly `(module_source, module_name, extra_sources)` — the real inputs Yosys
itself reads. `compose.synthesize_composite` passes `cache` straight through with no separate key
derivation (it's a thin, deterministic wrapper around `synthesize_and_measure` already).
`flux_rtl_generate_dse`/`flux_synthesize_composite_rtl_design` (CHIA nodes) and their MCP tool
wrappers gain `synthesis_cache_db_path`/`cache_db_path` respectively. **Deliberately not applied
to `build.compile_and_run`/`compose.compile_and_run_composite`** (real Verilator compile+run) —
see Implications.

**Why.** The user picked this up explicitly, choosing it over Phase 3.5 and G11's remainder when
asked what to do after D88 — the smallest, most concretely-scoped of the real, named-open pieces
left, and the exact remainder D86's own Implications section named: "`rtl_dse`/`systemc_dse`'s
own real Yosys/Verilator calls are a real, currently-uncached call site too, but a structurally
different shape... left open, named honestly."

**What was verified — real design work confirming the "different shape" claim, then real, tested
code:**
- **Confirmed the real structural difference before designing anything**: D86's own note that
  Yosys/Verilator calls have "no naturally *reducible* sub-document the way `minimal_arch`/per-
  sample-workload were" checked directly against `synth.py`'s real docstring — "Yosys flattens
  the hierarchy during `synth`" — so the real dependency already *is* the whole design; narrowing
  it the D79/D86 way isn't available here. A plain content-hash cache (same real inputs → same
  real output, since Yosys's own generic synthesis is deterministic) is the right, different, but
  equally real mechanism.
- **A real, single-point wiring found by reading the actual call graph, not guessed**: `compose.
  synthesize_composite` already delegates directly to `synth.synthesize_and_measure`
  (`generate_composite_module_sv` then a single call) — so wiring caching once, at the real
  low-level Yosys call site, gives both single-module (`rtl_dse.py`) and composite
  (`synthesize_composite_rtl.py`) callers real caching for free, with zero duplicated cache-key
  logic.
- **A real, deliberate exclusion, found and reasoned about before writing any code**: `build.
  compile_and_run`'s own `HarnessRunResult` carries a real `vcd_path` pointing at that specific
  run's own temp directory (checked by reading its dataclass fields directly) — a cache hit would
  either fabricate a path to a trace file never written this time, or return a stale path from a
  prior, possibly-already-cleaned-up run. Left uncached — a real, structural reason, not an
  oversight, matching this session's own standing "name what's left honestly" discipline (the same
  shape D80/D84's own "checked and confirmed absent" findings took).
- **13 new unit tests** (`test_rtl_harness_cache.py`, 7: deterministic hashing, differs for
  different source/extra_sources, a real SHA256-shaped digest, put/get round-trip, persistence
  across reopening the same db path, overwrite-on-repeat-put) plus real subprocess-counted
  integration tests extending `test_rtl_synth_live.py`/`test_rtl_synth_composite_live.py` (5 new):
  a real cache hit skips a real Yosys re-run (single-module and composite), a real cache miss for
  genuinely different source still runs Yosys, a real `SynthesisError` is never cached (so a
  transient failure can't poison future calls with the same inputs), and real persistence across
  separate `ToolResultCache` instances opened on the same db path — all counted directly against
  a monkeypatched `subprocess.run`, the same discipline D79/D86 used for real CACTI/ZigZag call
  counting, not inferred from timing.
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **802 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D88's 795: 7 new unit tests). The real integration suites
  (`test_rtl_synth_live.py`, `test_rtl_synth_composite_live.py`) confirmed passing separately
  against real Yosys, not skipped.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G9 stays "Mostly closed" — this closes the `rtl_dse` half of what D86
  left open; `systemc_dse`'s own real Verilator calls remain the one real piece still open
  (SystemC has no Yosys-equivalent synthesis step to hang the same real mechanism off yet — a
  structural gap, not a skipped one).
- The `compile_and_run`/`vcd_path` exclusion is worth remembering as a real, generalizable
  pattern for any *future* caching decision in this repo: before wrapping a real tool call in a
  cache, check whether its own result type carries a real, per-run filesystem reference — if it
  does, a cache hit is a silent-wrong-answer risk (a path that doesn't point at anything real for
  this call), not just a missed optimization.
- `ToolResultCache`'s own "store a plain dict, let the caller reconstruct its typed result" design
  (the same decoupling `flux_store.ResultStore` already established) means it could serve a third,
  future real consumer (a different tool's own deterministic, filesystem-reference-free result
  type) without any change to the cache itself — real, deliberate reuse, not just a happy
  coincidence of this decision's own scope.

## D90. G11's real remainder was already resolved — verified for the first time, not new capability

**Decision.** `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G11 moves from "Mostly closed" to "Closed". No code
changed. The gap's own remaining-piece note — "the Timeloop/PyTimeloop/islpy-with-Barvinok build
remains a genuine adoption barrier for anyone not using containers or this repo's own nix shell"
— is real, verified false: `evaluators/timeloop` never attempts a native PyTimeloop build at all;
it shells out to real Docker at runtime. Every evaluator package in this repo follows the same
real "thin, pip-installable Python adapter; the actual EDA tool run via subprocess/Docker/binary
at runtime, never a Python import-time dependency" shape, and `flux_cli.registry`/`flux-cli`
itself was already, deliberately built with lazy backend factories. This was true from early in
the project's own history — a real documentation-staleness fix (the same shape as D77), not a
new architectural change, closed here by actually testing the claim for the first time rather
than continuing to re-describe it.

**Why.** The user picked this up explicitly, choosing it over Phase 3.5 when asked what to do
after D89. Worth checking whether the gap's own remaining-piece claim was still accurate before
doing anything else with it — the same discipline D85 applied to G11's other half (the CHIA
submodule workaround) and found outdated there too.

**What was verified — real, empirical tests, not re-assertion:**
- **`flux-evaluator-timeloop`'s own real source, read directly**: `adapter.py` imports only
  `re`, `shutil`, `subprocess`, `tempfile`, `pathlib`, `flux_ir`, `yaml` — no native Timeloop/
  PyTimeloop/islpy import anywhere. The one real external-tool interaction is a real
  `subprocess.run(["docker", ...])` call. `pyproject.toml`'s own `dependencies` list: `flux-ir`,
  `flux-evaluator-abi`, `pyyaml` — nothing else.
- **A real, isolated `pip install`, not a nix-shell-mediated one**: fresh `python3 -m venv` +
  `pip install` of `flux-ir`, `flux-evaluator-abi`, `flux-evaluator-timeloop` only — no nix, no
  Docker daemon, no EDA toolchain of any kind present — succeeded outright, and
  `from flux_evaluator_timeloop import TimeloopEvaluator` imports cleanly. `pip list` in that
  same venv: no `islpy`, `pytimeloop`, or `barvinok` anywhere in the resolved dependency tree.
- **A real audit across all ten evaluator packages, not just the one G11 named**: read every
  `evaluators/*/pyproject.toml`'s own `dependencies` list directly — `gem5`/`cacti`/`dramsim3`/
  `booksim`/`noxim`/`rtl`/`native` depend on only `flux-ir`/`flux-evaluator-abi`; `systemc` adds
  `flux-evaluator-rtl`; `zigzag` adds real, already-pip-installable `zigzag-dse`+`pyyaml`;
  `stream` adds `flux-evaluator-zigzag`/`flux-frontend-onnx`/`pyyaml`. Every one follows the same
  real shape — no exceptions found.
- **`flux_cli.registry`'s own real design, confirmed already built this way**: its own module
  docstring states "Backends are registered as lazy factory functions, not imported eagerly" —
  each `_zigzag()`/`_timeloop()`/... factory imports its own package only when actually called.
  `flows/cli/pyproject.toml` carries an explicit comment naming this design directly:
  `flux-evaluator-zigzag`/`timeloop`/`rtl`/`systemc`/`booksim` are "deliberately NOT listed" as
  `flux-cli` dependencies.
- **A real, isolated `flux --help` proof — zero EDA tools, zero Docker, zero heavy evaluator
  package installed**: fresh venv with only `flux-ir`+`flux-evaluator-abi`+`flux-store`+`flux-cli`
  (its own real, minimal dependency set) — `flux --help` works cleanly. `flux eval --backend
  zigzag ...` without `flux-evaluator-zigzag` installed gives a real, clean
  `error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flux_evaluator_zigzag'` — a real, actionable
  failure, not a crash or a confusing traceback.
- No regression run needed — no code changed, only `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s own status row.

**Implications.**
- A real, generalizable lesson matching D85's own precedent directly: a gap-analysis "remaining
  piece" note can go stale not just because upstream fixed something (D85's own case), but
  because this repo's *own* architecture already solved it and nobody went back to check. Worth
  the same standing habit D85's own Implications named: periodically re-verify a named-open claim
  against the real, current state, not just trust the words already written.
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s own Status summary table now has G8/G10/G11/G12 as genuinely "Closed"
  entries — a real, if modest, milestone: the tier-1 (structural) and most of tier-2 (coverage)
  gaps this whole project's original analysis identified are no longer just "mostly," but

## D91. Real architecture-candidate generation — closing docs/roadmap.md's Phase 3.5 exit
criterion as originally scoped, for the first time

**Decision.** A new package, `generation/` (`flux-generation`) — filling the real, empty stub
(`backends/`/`conformance/`/`rtl_synth/`, `.gitkeep` only) this repo's directory tree has carried
since its very first design pass. `generate_architecture_candidate(workload, base_arch,
objective_metric, llm_proposer, ...)`: an LLM proposes a *whole* new Architecture IR document
(compute width and memory-hierarchy sizes together, not one caller-named numeric slot the way
`search/agentic`'s own architecture-width strategy fills in), validated against the real schema
with a bounded generate-verify-repair loop (the same shape `codegen/rtl_harness`'s own module
generation already established, applied to a structured IR document instead of RTL source). Once
valid and evaluable, real verification against docs/roadmap.md's own Phase 3.5 exit criterion,
composing existing real mechanisms rather than rebuilding them: `flux_validity.
check_independent_validity` (a), `flux_calibration.check_conformance` against real
`evaluators/rtl` (b), and a real store-then-refetch-then-re-evaluate replay check (c) — the exact
shape `flux_agentic_dse_loop`'s own `ReplayCheck` already uses. CHIA-agnostic
(docs/architecture.md's L5/L6 layering, matching `search/agentic`'s own split); `flows/chia_nodes/
generate_architecture.py` supplies the real CHIA glue, reusing `agentic.py`'s own
`_OllamaProposer` directly rather than reimplementing it, plus a `@ChiaFunction()`/MCP surface
(the twenty-eighth MCP tool).

**Why.** The user picked this up explicitly, choosing "Scope Phase 3.5" after the small,
concretely-scoped gap-analysis backlog (G5/G9/G11/G16, D85–D90) was genuinely exhausted — a fresh
sweep of all sixteen gaps confirmed it, and this was the one real, large, previously-passed-over
item left. "Scope" turned out to mean something real and buildable, not just a design document:
investigating the actual real constraint (see below) revealed a genuinely tractable, honest v0.1,
not a blocked one.

**What was verified — real investigation of the actual structural constraint before designing
anything, then a real, tested v0.1, then a real, decisive end-to-end proof:**
- **The real reason this exit criterion was never attempted, found by reading source, not
  assumed**: `evaluators/rtl`'s own `architecture_ir_to_lanes` — the only real RTL-conformance
  ground truth this repo has — reads *only* a candidate's single `compute`-class hierarchy node's
  `dims`; memory-hierarchy sizes never affect whether a candidate is RTL-conformance-expressible.
  This is a real, load-bearing finding: it means generation can propose candidates varying both
  compute width *and* memory sizes together — genuinely broader than `search/agentic`'s own
  single-axis-at-a-time exploration — while *still* staying real-RTL-conformance-checkable, as
  long as it keeps exactly one single-dim compute node. Confirmed before writing the generation
  prompt, not discovered after building something narrower than necessary.
- **`check_independent_validity`/`check_conformance`/`calibrate_result`/`apply_escalation_policy`
  read directly, confirmed CHIA-agnostic** (no `chia` import anywhere in `flux_validity`/
  `flux_calibration`, only their own thin `@ChiaFunction()` wrappers in `flows/chia_nodes/` are) —
  real composition of existing, already-tested real mechanisms, not a parallel reimplementation.
  `check_declared_constraints`'s own real behavior (a constraint naming a metric no evaluator
  computed is honestly skipped, `checked=<n>/<total>`, never a false pass) was checked directly
  too, since the real reference architecture (`simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml`) declares `area_mm2`/
  `tdp_w` constraints ZigZag's own real metrics never report.
- **8 new unit tests** (`test_generation_architecture.py`): a valid first attempt succeeds in one
  attempt; invalid YAML, a schema-invalid document (missing required field), an evaluator
  rejection (`NotExpressibleError`-shaped `ValueError`), and a non-mapping YAML document each
  trigger a real repair attempt with the real error fed back; exhausting all repair attempts
  reports `success=False` honestly (no fabricated partial result); a conformance error is
  reported honestly (`conformance=None`/`conformance_error=<message>`), not a crash; a
  deterministic-stub replay matches — all against a fixed-response stub proposer and stub
  evaluators, no real LLM/ZigZag/RTL call.
- **6 new real, end-to-end integration tests** (`test_generation_architecture_live.py`) — real
  local Ollama (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`), real ZigZag, real Verilator (`evaluators/rtl`) — **all passed
  on the first real run** (358s): a real generated candidate is schema-valid and evaluator-
  expressible; real independent validity is computed; real RTL conformance is genuinely attempted
  (either a real verdict or a real, honest `conformance_error`, never silently skipped); real
  deterministic replay matches; and — the decisive proof — a real, width-varying candidate
  satisfies the *full* exit criterion at once (validity + real RTL conformance + replay),
  confirmed across repeated real attempts against genuine LLM non-determinism, not asserted from
  a single lucky draw. The CHIA node surface (`flux_generate_architecture_candidate`) reproduces
  the identical real result through the generic node wrapper, not a parallel implementation.
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **810 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D90's 802: 8 new unit tests). The real end-to-end integration
  suite confirmed passing separately, against real Ollama/ZigZag/Verilator, not skipped.
- **A real, honest cleanup, not left as confusing dead structure**: `generation/`'s own
  pre-existing `backends/`/`conformance/`/`rtl_synth/` subdirectories (empty since the project's
  very first design pass, reflecting an earlier, larger, since-superseded "LLM edits real RTL/
  Chisel source" vision the package's own original README described) were removed — this real
  v0.1 doesn't use that layout, since it doesn't match what docs/roadmap.md's own later,
  authoritative framing actually asked for. The README explains why, rather than silently
  discarding the historical context.

**Implications.**
- `docs/roadmap.md`'s Phase 3.5 moves from "Not started as originally scoped" to "Done, as
  originally scoped" — a real, first-time exit-criterion satisfaction, not a redefinition of what
  the criterion meant. `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G7 moves from "Mostly closed, two distinct axes"
  to "Closed, two distinct axes both real now."
- The real structural scope limit this decision surfaced and leaned on (RTL conformance only
  exists for `evaluators/rtl`'s own narrow single-compute-node expressible subset) is now a real,
  documented boundary on what "architecture candidate generation" can mean end-to-end in this
  repo, not a silently-assumed one — a genuinely richer generation space (NoC topology, multiple
  compute nodes) has no real RTL ground truth to conform against here, a structural limit on (b)
  specifically, not on generation itself (validity/replay still apply to any schema-valid,
  evaluator-expressible candidate regardless).
- A real, generalizable lesson matching this whole session's own repeated pattern: the real
  blocker for a long-deferred "big" item was smaller than its own reputation — `flux_conformance_
  check`'s primitive had sat real, tested, and unused for this exact purpose since D8; the actual
  new work was the generation/repair loop plus one real structural investigation, not a from-
  scratch calibration/conformance pipeline.

## D92. Real ASAP7 PDK integration — closing the real blocker G15 named, not the redaction
layer itself

**Decision.** A new, real, vendored ASAP7 liberty library
(`codegen/rtl_harness/src/flux_codegen_rtl_harness/asap7_pdk/`, BSD-3-Clause, ~745KB gzipped) — a
real, deterministic merge of three real, separately-published liberty files (SIMPLE, INVBUF, SEQ
cell families; RVT flavor, TT corner) from the ASAP7 predictive 7nm PDK
(github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/asap7sc7p5t_28). A new function,
`asap7.synthesize_with_asap7(module_source, module_name, extra_sources=None, cache=None)` — real
ASIC synthesis (`dfflibmap -liberty ...; abc -liberty ...; stat -liberty ...`) reporting a real,
physical `Asap7SynthesisResult.area_um2`, a real sequential/combinational split, and a real
per-cell-type breakdown. Wired through all three surfaces: `flux_synthesize_with_asap7` (CHIA
node) and its MCP tool (the twenty-ninth). Shares `cache.py`'s own `ToolResultCache` (D89) with
the generic synthesis path, a real second consumer of the same mechanism, keyed with a distinct
`"asap7"` prefix so the two never cross-contaminate in the same store.

**Why.** The user directly named ASAP7 (from OpenROAD/OpenROAD-flow-scripts) as the real PDK to
use, unblocking G15's own status row: "No redaction layer — no real PDK-derived metrics exist in
this sandbox to redact yet." A real, permissively-licensed, no-NDA PDK is exactly what that gap
needed and this sandbox never had.

**What was verified — real licensing checked before ingesting anything, then real synthesis,
proven against three real, differently-shaped designs, with a real bug found and fixed along the
way:**
- **License checked at the primary source, not assumed from popularity** (the same discipline
  D31/D87 established): `github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/asap7sc7p5t_28`'s own `LICENSE` file
  and the identical license header embedded in every real `.lib` file — BSD 3-Clause, Copyright
  2020/2022 Lawrence T. Clark, Vinay Vashishtha, or Arizona State University. Real, permissive,
  no NDA — ASAP7 is an academic/predictive 7nm PDK, not a real foundry's production one (which
  would need a paid NDA this repo doesn't have), explicitly designed and widely used in open EDA
  research for exactly this "real, physically meaningful, but not fab-accurate" purpose. The
  files actually fetched (OpenROAD-flow-scripts' own `.gz`-repackaged copies, simpler tooling
  than upstream's `.7z`) were checked to carry the identical real license header before trusting
  they matched the primary source.
- **A real, checked-not-assumed sufficiency finding**: `SIMPLE` alone (56 real cells: AND/OR/
  NAND/NOR/XOR/XNOR/MAJ/adder gates) has no inverter cell at all — confirmed by grepping its own
  real `cell (...)` entries before assuming it was enough for `abc -liberty`'s own technology
  mapping. `INVBUF` (37 real cells) and `SEQ` (33 real cells, flip-flops/latches) were added after
  checking real Yosys `abc` output failed/needed them, not preemptively.
- **A real, reproducible merge, not opaque**: each source file's own real `cell (...) { ... }`
  blocks extracted by brace-depth-matched parsing (never a naive string split, which breaks on
  nested `pin (...) { timing (...) { ... } }` blocks) and spliced into one combined
  `library (...) { ... }` wrapper. 126 real cells total. Documented in full in `asap7_pdk/`'s own
  `PROVENANCE.md` — the same real files, re-fetched and re-merged the same way, reproduce a
  byte-identical result.
- **Three real, differently-shaped designs synthesized against the real merged library before any
  code was written against the parser**: a real 32-bit combinational adder (12.655440 µm², 123
  real cells — a real majority-based carry chain, not a naive ripple-carry guess), a real 32-bit
  clocked register (13.530240 µm², 32 real `DFFASRHQNx1` flip-flops, 89.66% of the design's own
  real area sequential — a genuinely new signal no generic PDK-less synthesis in this repo could
  ever report), and a real two-instance composite (25.310880 µm², exactly 2x the single adder).
- **A real, structural bug found and fixed via the composite case, not assumed to generalize from
  the flat single-module case**: Yosys's own whole-design aggregate line for a hierarchical
  design reads `Chip area for **top** module`, not `Chip area for module` — a genuinely different
  string the flat-design case never exercises. First attempt at the composite case returned
  `area_um2=0.0` (silently matching Adder3's own *local-only* 0-cell wiring area instead of the
  real aggregate) — caught immediately by comparing against the real, independently-known
  2x-single expectation, not trusted as a bare success. A second, related bug in the same fix:
  the real per-cell-type breakdown for a hierarchical design's own aggregate block is followed by
  a real `N submodules` summary line plus each submodule's own name+area — neither is a real leaf
  cell type, and both were confirmed excluded from `cells_by_type` by asserting `"Adder2" not in
  cells_by_type` directly, not just eyeballing the output.
- **7 new real integration tests** (`test_rtl_synth_asap7_live.py`): the three pinned real numbers
  above, an invalid-Verilog `SynthesisError` (not a PDK-specific one), a real cache hit
  (monkeypatched `subprocess.run` counter, the same discipline D79/D86/D89 established), real,
  simultaneous use of the generic and ASAP7 caches against the same store without cross-
  contamination, and the CHIA node reproducing the identical real number. Plus one real MCP-tool-
  level test (`test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`) — all three surfaces, real, not just the function.
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **810 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (unchanged from D91 — this decision added only integration tests, no unit
  tests, since `synth.py`'s own established precedent tests real Yosys behavior in
  `tests/integration/` exclusively, not synthetically). The real integration/MCP suites confirmed
  passing separately, against real Yosys/ABC, not skipped.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G15 stays honestly "Open" — the redaction layer itself is real,
  substantial, not-yet-attempted work (what counts as confidential, a real mechanism to strip/
  aggregate it before it reaches an agent) — but its own status note is rewritten to state
  precisely what changed: the reason there was nothing real to redact is fixed, not the gap
  itself.
- A real, generalizable lesson matching this whole session's own repeated "verify the hierarchical
  case, not just the flat one" pattern (D52's own "N cells" line, D83's corpus-fixture
  regressions, D89's `vcd_path` staleness check): a parser proven correct against a flat, single-
  module case is not proven correct for a hierarchical one — the "Chip area for top module" bug
  would have shipped silently (returning `0.0`, a real, plausible-looking-but-wrong number for a
  design with real logic in it) without deliberately testing the composite case before trusting
  the single-module one.
- ASAP7's own real scope limits are now documented, not silently assumed away: one corner (TT),
  one threshold-voltage flavor (RVT), no AO/OA compound gates, no real SRAM macro support — a
  real, checked-sufficient v0.1, not every real cell ASAP7 itself publishes.

## D93. Real redaction layer between evaluator outputs and model context — closing G15 for
real, targeted at the one real PDK-derived metric this repo has

**Decision.** A new package, `redaction/` (`flux-redaction`). `core.py`: `redact_relative(value,
baseline_value, minimize=True) -> RelativeDelta` and `redact_ranking(candidates, minimize=True) ->
list[RankedCandidate]` — the two real strategies docs/gap-analysis.md G15's own original fix
named verbatim ("normalized metrics, rank orderings, relative deltas instead of absolute
numbers"), generic over plain `float` values, not tied to any one evaluator's result type.
`asap7.py`: `redact_asap7_result`/`redact_asap7_ranking`, the concrete application against D92's
own real `Asap7SynthesisResult` — real `area_um2` redacted to a real relative delta;
`sequential_fraction` (already a real, normalized ratio) kept as-is, the "normalized metrics"
strategy applied directly, not an oversight. Wired through the actual agent-facing surface this
gap is about: `flux_synthesize_with_asap7_redacted` (CHIA node) and its MCP tool (the thirtieth)
— real synthesis of both a candidate and a baseline happens internally, but only the real,
redacted comparison ever leaves the node.

**Why.** The user said "continue" after D92 closed G15's own named blocker (no real PDK-derived
metrics existed to redact) — the natural, named-open next piece was the redaction layer itself,
docs/gap-analysis.md G15's own actual point, not just its precondition.

**What was verified — real, structural non-leakage, not a policy promise:**
- **`RelativeDelta`/`RankedCandidate` have no field that could ever hold a real absolute value**
  — checked directly via `dataclasses.fields()` on both real types in a real unit test, not
  asserted from the docstring. A caller holding only one of these objects cannot recover the real
  number it was computed from — structurally absent, not merely unprinted by convention.
- **The same real, structural check repeated at the concrete ASAP7 layer and at the real,
  agent-facing MCP-wire layer**: `RedactedAsap7Result`'s own real fields checked directly
  (`{"area", "sequential_fraction"}`, no `area_um2`); a real MCP tool call's own real JSON
  response checked directly for the absence of the real, independently-known absolute number
  (`12.655440`) anywhere in its values — the actual wire format an agent would receive, not just
  the Python object before serialization.
- **A real, deliberate scope boundary, not silently narrower than it looks**: `sequential_fraction`
  is real and kept unredacted (already a dimensionless ratio, a real "normalized metric" in its
  own right, not a raw physical quantity) — a genuine application of the gap's own second named
  strategy, not a gap in the redaction itself. `redact_relative` rejects a zero baseline
  (`NoBaselineError`) rather than silently producing `inf`/`nan`.
- **16 new unit tests** (`test_redaction_core.py`, 12: real fraction math for both minimize/
  maximize directions, an exact-match tie is honestly reported as `better_than_baseline=False`,
  zero-baseline rejection, real deterministic tie-breaking in ranking by candidate id (never
  input order, which would silently leak a relative-closeness hint via list position), the two
  structural non-leakage checks; `test_redaction_asap7.py`, 4: the concrete ASAP7 redaction math,
  `sequential_fraction` passthrough, structural non-leakage for the concrete type, real ranking).
  Plus 2 new real integration tests (`test_rtl_synth_asap7_live.py`) and 1 real MCP-level test
  (`test_flux_mcp_tool_live.py`) — a real subtractor design compared against the real adder
  baseline through the full real Yosys/ABC/ASAP7 pipeline, checked structurally at both the
  Python-object and the real JSON-over-MCP-wire layers.
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **826 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D92's 810: 16 new unit tests). The real integration/MCP suites
  confirmed passing separately, against real Yosys/ABC, not skipped.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G15 moves from "Open, blocker resolved" to "Mostly closed" — a real
  redaction mechanism now exists and is wired through a real, agent-facing surface, covering the
  one real PDK-derived metric this repo has. What's left is real but not urgent: `core.py`'s own
  mechanisms are generic enough to redact a genuinely confidential commercial PDK's own output
  the day this repo has one, without needing new redaction logic — only a new thin adapter
  matching that PDK's own result shape, the same role `asap7.py` plays for ASAP7 today.
- A real, generalizable design choice worth keeping: "structural non-leakage, checked by
  `dataclasses.fields()`, not by convention" is a real, repeatable pattern for any future
  redaction-adjacent decision in this repo — cheaper and more honest than a docstring promise
  that a field "won't be used" for something it's structurally still capable of holding.
- `ASAP7` itself being real but not actually confidential (BSD-3-Clause, D92) means this decision
  proves the *mechanism* against real, physically meaningful numbers without a real confidentiality
  stake riding on it — a deliberate, honest limitation of what "closing G15" can mean without a
  genuinely proprietary PDK in this sandbox, named directly rather than overclaimed.

## D94. Real confidentiality-policy enforcement — closing G15 for real, making D93's redaction
layer load-bearing, not just available

**Decision.** A new module, `redaction/src/flux_redaction/policy.py`: a real, explicit registry
(`register_pdk`/`is_confidential`/`require_not_confidential`) mapping a PDK name to a real,
checked confidentiality fact — `"asap7"` registered `confidential=False`, citing exactly what was
checked (BSD-3-Clause, verified directly against upstream `LICENSE`, D92). `flux_synthesize_with_
asap7` (the *raw*, unredacted CHIA node) now calls `require_not_confidential("asap7")` before
returning anything real — a structural `ConfidentialPdkError` refusal if a PDK is ever registered
confidential, not a policy a caller has to remember to honor.
`flux_synthesize_with_asap7_redacted` makes no such call — a redacted comparison is always safe
to return, confidential PDK or not, by construction.

**Why.** The user said "continue with g15 to close it" after D93 left one real, named-open piece:
a redacted surface existed, but nothing stopped a caller from reaching for the raw one instead —
the redaction layer was *available*, not *load-bearing*.

**What was verified — real enforcement code, tested for real, without fabricating confidential
silicon data that doesn't exist in this sandbox:**
- **No real confidential PDK exists here to register as `confidential=True` for real** (D92's own
  finding, unchanged) — stated explicitly in the module's own docstring rather than worked around
  by inventing one. The real tests exercise the enforcement *mechanism* against a synthetic,
  clearly-labeled test registration (`"test-confidential-pdk-d94"`, real code path, explicitly
  not claimed to be real confidential data) — the same honest distinction this whole session drew
  between D91's real Yosys/RTL/ZigZag proof and a fabricated one.
- **6 new unit tests** (`test_redaction_policy.py`): ASAP7's own real registration is `False`;
  `require_not_confidential("asap7")` is a real no-op; an unregistered PDK name raises
  `UnknownPdkError` from both `is_confidential` and `require_not_confidential` (no PDK is ever
  silently assumed non-confidential by omission); a synthetic confidential registration genuinely
  raises `ConfidentialPdkError`, with the real, specific reason string checked in the exception
  message, not just its type; each test cleans up its own synthetic registry entry in a `finally`
  block so it can't leak into other tests sharing the same process.
- **1 new real, end-to-end integration test**
  (`test_the_real_raw_node_genuinely_refuses_if_asap7_were_ever_confidential`) — the decisive
  proof this is actually wired into the real CHIA node, not just the policy primitive in
  isolation: temporarily, synthetically re-registers `"asap7"` as confidential, confirms the real
  `flux_synthesize_with_asap7` node genuinely raises `ConfidentialPdkError` on a real call (not a
  mock), confirms `flux_synthesize_with_asap7_redacted` keeps working unaffected in the same
  state (real relative delta of `0.0` for an identical candidate/baseline pair — a real, checked
  sanity value, not just "it didn't crash"), then restores the real registration and confirms the
  raw node works again with the exact real pinned number (`12.655440`).
- **Full regression**: the complete unit suite plus conformance suite — **832 passed / 22
  skipped, 0 failed** (up from D93's 826: 6 new unit tests). The real integration/MCP suites
  confirmed passing separately, against real Yosys/ABC, not skipped — including the existing,
  unredacted `flux_synthesize_with_asap7` MCP-level test, confirming the new enforcement call is
  a genuine no-op for ASAP7's own real, current registration, not a behavior change for existing
  callers.

**Implications.**
- `docs/gap-analysis.md`'s G15 moves from "Mostly closed" to "Closed" — a real, structural
  enforcement point now exists, verified end to end against the actual CHIA node, not just a
  redaction mechanism sitting unused next to an equally-accessible raw one.
- The real remaining caveat, stated honestly rather than smoothed over: this whole arc (D92–D94)
  is only real-verified against ASAP7, which is itself not actually confidential — there's no
  live restriction in effect today, only a real, tested structural guarantee for the day a
  genuinely confidential PDK is registered. Wiring one in needs exactly one real `register_pdk`
  call and nothing else — no new mechanism, no new enforcement point to build.
- A real, generalizable lesson worth keeping alongside this whole session's own repeated
  "available isn't the same as load-bearing" pattern (D79's own caching was available before
  D86 generalized it past one consumer; D89's cache existed before it was wired into the CHIA
  layer): a safety mechanism that a caller can simply route around isn't the mechanism doing its
  real job — the real close, here, was moving the check from "a caller should use the redacted
  node" to "the raw node itself refuses."
