## D232. Natural language to a validated objective: authored, audited, never auto-executed

**Decision.** `flux_author_objective` (48th tool): a local LLM drafts an Objective IR document
from prose; the REAL campaign validator (schema + `parse_objective` semantics) accepts or
rejects; rejections are repaired with the actual validator error fed back, bounded at 3 rounds —
the D44 generate-validate-repair shape with the validator this time being the campaign's own
parser. Three deliberate properties: the LLM never sees or echoes the workload/architecture
documents (the node injects them post-parse, so a large model cannot mangle a large document);
the document's provenance records the model and the **exact prose**, inside the content-hashed
identity, so any campaign is auditable back to the sentence that asked for it; and authoring
never runs anything — execution is the caller's separate, explicit act.

**What was verified, and what the failures taught.** Live end to end: one sentence ("minimize
latency and energy over widths 8/16/32, screen with zigzag, escalate through rtl, at most 8
evaluations") -> validated document with every numeric clause correctly extracted -> the real
campaign from D231's ONNX workload -> the fidelity-labeled frontier. Two real failure modes
surfaced and were handled honestly rather than papered over:

1. qwen persistently attached weights in pareto mode and the repair loop did not converge in 3
   rounds — the D153 primer class again: a specific repeated mistake corrected up front ("with
   pareto, entries must have NO weight field") rather than through repairs it cannot climb.
2. Run-to-run variance drops optional clauses: the same prose produced `escalation: ["rtl"]` on
   one real run and no escalation on the next — and the clause-less document is *valid*, so no
   repair fires. The validator checks well-formedness, not faithfulness to prose; the committed
   test pins the guaranteed invariants (validity, audit trail, reliably-cued numerics, an
   executed campaign) and branches on the one clause extraction can drop, with the variance
   stated in its docstring. Prose-faithfulness checking is real, named future work — it would
   need a second, independent reading of the request, not a stronger prompt.

**Implications.** The four-roles mapping's "spec interpretation — thin everywhere" slot now has a
real occupant with the repo's own safety shape around it. The full demo chain — prose -> ONNX
model -> bounded campaign -> labeled frontier — is a committed, Ollama-gated test, which also
means it inherits the known CI hole until the runner exists.

---

## D233. Generative campaigns: the LLM invents architectures, and campaigns stop being parameter sweeps

**Decision.** `strategy.kind: "generative"` paired (bidirectionally enforced) with
`search.kind: "open_architecture"`: each round the LLM writes a **complete Architecture IR
document** instead of picking from an enumerated list. Every proposal passes the real schema
validator plus a structural guard — same hierarchy skeleton as the base, same compute dim keys,
positive sizes — which keeps every candidate inside the screening backend's expressible space
(D131's own scope, now as a guard instead of a prompt hope). Candidates are deduplicated by
content hash against everything ever tried; a failed or duplicate proposal falls back to a
seeded deterministic mutation of the base (double/halve one knob, skipping seen hashes), so the
campaign progresses regardless of LLM behavior. Full D219 provenance on every trial:
`deterministic=False`, model, prompt/response hashes, `used_fallback`/reason. The shared prompt
history moved to one `_screen_history` helper — the agentic branch had it inline, and a second
copy would have been the fix-never-travels shape.

**Why.** The gap named in this block's own planning: every campaign strategy selected from a
pre-declared grid, while `flux_generate_architecture_candidate` (D131) — an LLM proposing novel
architectures with validation and repair — sat outside the campaign machinery entirely. "Full
DSE: expand and improve" (the original use-case language) stopped at the edges of whatever list
the objective enumerated. This closes that: the objective declares *what better means* and the
budget; the model supplies the candidates.

**What the live run showed.** Six evaluations, real qwen2.5-coder + real ZigZag, zero fallbacks:
six genuinely novel architectures — widths 6, 7, 9, 9, 12, 8 with co-varied gbuf/dram sizes,
values no grid in this repo has ever enumerated — with the history visibly steering the search
(widths climb as the model reads wider→faster from its own measured results), and the frontier
landing on the invented X=12/gbuf-384 design at 1166 cycles / 839 uJ, beating every architecture
this repo had hand-written for that workload's sweep family. The committed Ollama-gated test
asserts what holds under model variance (novelty vs the base hash, dedup, structure
preservation, attribution, a frontier over invented candidates) rather than pinning any specific
invention; the structural guard and the mutation fallback's determinism are unit-pinned.
`flux_author_objective`'s prompt now names the strategy, so a prose request for "invent new
designs" can reach it. Regression: 1318 unit + conformance (up from 1316), 22 skipped.

**Implications.** The three original use cases now compose end to end at their strongest form:
prose -> authored objective -> generative campaign -> novel architectures screened, escalated
through RTL/OpenROAD, frontier labeled by fidelity. Named residues: the structural guard limits
invention to knob values within a fixed skeleton (new hierarchy levels or dims are refused, not
explored — widening it means widening every translator's scope first), and generative campaigns
inherit the Ollama CI hole.

---

## D234. Calibration follows the workloads, and a holdout failure now drives regeneration — without disclosing a single vector

**Decision.** Two closures that turn stated claims into measured or live behavior:

1. **The flywheel covers the second workload family.** Real RTL references for the ONNX-born
   `wide-proj` at widths 8/16/32: ZigZag's bias is 3.014/3.018/3.027 — the same near-constant
   shape as `mlp-gemm0`'s 2.94x, now a two-family observation rather than a one-family one.
   Calibration corrects in-pool points to <=0.2% of RTL with ~2% intervals, prices the held-out
   width 64 honestly wide, and the campaign contender set grows {64} -> {64, 32} exactly at the
   extrapolation — D222's result reproduced on a workload no hand ever wrote.
2. **Holdout-driven regeneration.** `flux_generate_rtl_for_architecture` re-prompts generation
   when the holdout fails (bounded, default one round), carrying ONLY the failure count — the
   held-out vectors stay undisclosed, because telling the LLM which inputs failed would convert
   the holdout into more shown vectors and revive exactly the overfit D223 exists to catch. The
   report carries `holdout_regens`; `flux_generate_rtl_module` gained an `llm` injection point
   (the campaign runner's make_evaluator pattern), which is what makes the control flow testable
   without an LLM in the loop.

**What was measured, and the mistake worth keeping.** The first calibration experiment produced
correct corrected values with USELESS intervals — every CI spanned ~15x its value, in-pool points
included. The cause is a lesson about identity, not arithmetic: the pool was built from hand-made
"equivalent" architectures whose `id` differed from the campaign's generated candidates, and
calibration identity is the content hash — an equivalent-looking document with a different id
matches nothing, so every campaign point was priced as extrapolation. Rebuilt from the campaign's
own `generate_width_candidates`, the intervals collapsed to ~2% in-pool. The committed test
states this in its docstring: the pool must come from the same generator the campaign uses.

The regeneration test scripts only the proposer (real Verilator throughout): a memorizing module
passes every shown vector, fails the holdout, triggers exactly one regeneration whose prompt is
then checked for every held-out input value — none present, only the failure count — and the
second, honest proposal passes both sets. The diagram's feedback rail (the artifact's
evaluator->orchestrator->generator edges) is now fully live code on this path.

Regression: 1318 unit + conformance, 22 skipped; the ONNX suite is 4 tests, the holdout suite 6.

**Implications.** Honest CIs and contender growth now exist on two structurally different
workload families; the "one workload family" caveat on calibration is retired (equivalence
between Timeloop runners still measures only the original family — narrower, and still noted).
Generation now recovers from the exact failure mode its own grading was built to catch, at zero
disclosure cost.

## D235. Prose becomes a graded DesignSpec: the authored reference is executed, never believed

**Decision.** Add `flux_author_design_spec` (49th MCP tool): natural-language prose -> a
harness-validated combinational DesignSpec plus a disjoint holdout twin, closing the last gap in
the "give a spec, get a verified module" use case for behaviors the derivation bridge does not
cover. The load-bearing choice mirrors D223's discipline exactly: the LLM authors ports and a
**Python reference function**, and the node EXECUTES that reference (restricted
arithmetic-builtins namespace — an accidents guard, not a sandbox; the trust boundary is stated
in the module docstring and is the same trust already extended to LLM-written C++/Verilog that
gets compiled and run) to COMPUTE every golden vector. Expected outputs are never
model-asserted. Vectors are seeded from the sha256 of the authored design's own identity
(module/ports/reference), so the same design always grades on the same vectors and the
"holdout" salt yields a disjoint, equally-golden set by construction.

Validation is real and layered, every failure fed back for bounded repair: JSON shape, port
dtype/bits bounds, `check_not_reserved` (pulled forward from the testbench generator — see
below), reference determinism (run twice, compared), reference-output width fit (the D193/D228
wrap-vs-unbounded mismatch caught at authoring time — an overflowing reference would make
correct RTL fail), and the real `design_spec_from_dict` on both specs.

**Why.** The standalone-agentic target's first use case is "spec/algo -> module". Until now the
only path from intent to a graded DesignSpec was `derive_design_spec`, which covers the
dot-product family it was built for. D232 authored the objective side; this authors the
implementation side, and together with D223/D234 the full chain is: prose -> executable golden
reference -> shown + held-out vectors -> generated RTL -> holdout grading with regeneration.

**What was verified.** Unit (5, scripted proposer, no LLM): disjoint shown/holdout with every
expected value recomputed independently; overflow -> repair round 2 with the real width error in
the repair prompt; reserved port name -> repair with the real D51 error; import and
nondeterminism refused; fail-closed after bounded repairs. Live (2, real qwen2.5-coder:7b + real
Verilator): a saturating adder and an absolute-difference unit — for each, authoring, an
independent probe of every shown AND held-out vector against the test's own lambda (checking the
reference, not trusting it), generation, and holdout grading.

Getting the live path stable surfaced four qwen-7b failure modes, all D153 primer-class (the
repair loop did NOT climb out of any of them in three rounds; a one-line correction up front
fixed each):
1. **JSON double-escape**: the reference string arrives with literal backslash-n, compiling to
   "unexpected character after line continuation character". Fixed by unambiguous normalization
   in `_load_reference` (only when the source has no real newline) plus a prompt instruction.
2. **Verilog `abs()`/`min()`/`max()`**: SystemVerilog has none of them; Verilator's "Can't find
   definition of task/function" error did not steer the model. Primer in `_module_prompt` now
   says to express them as conditional expressions.
3. **Intermediate wrap**: the saturating adder computed its sum in an 8-bit intermediate, so the
   clamp compared a value that had already wrapped (2/4 vectors, off-by-wrap outputs 120/119).
   The width primer now demands intermediates one bit wider than their operands and that
   comparisons read the wider value.
4. **Reserved port name**: qwen names a port `output`. `design_spec_from_dict` does not check
   reserved words — that guard lived only in the testbench generator, so authoring "succeeded"
   and generation crashed three nodes downstream with the raw D51 error. The check is now pulled
   forward into authoring validation, where the same error message becomes repair input.

After the primers: 5/6 successes over three back-to-back sweeps of both behaviors (the one miss:
abs-diff left a negative result after 3 rounds). The live test therefore branches per the
standing variance discipline — authoring and the vector probes assert unconditionally; the
generation half runs at 5 repair rounds and, on the rare non-convergence, asserts a fail-closed
result with a real verification failure on record. Regression: 1323 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** "Build me a module that does X" is now a two-node chain
(`flux_author_design_spec` -> `flux_generate_rtl_module`) with computed golden vectors and
holdout grading throughout — no hand-authored IR anywhere. The reference-execution pattern is
the template for richer authored specs (sequential behaviors would need a state-carrying
reference; the trust boundary paragraph is where that extension must start). Prose-faithfulness
(does the authored reference match the INTENT?) remains the model's responsibility — the tests
probe it with an independent lambda, but production callers get determinism and width guarantees,
not intent guarantees; that residue is noted below.

---

## D236. Composition against an objective: per-op engines, composed by code, measured by the same real tools

**Decision.** Campaigns can now search COMPOSITIONS: `search.kind: composition_width` assigns
each einsum op of a multi-op workload its own dedicated engine (base architecture at a per-op
width), and a new `ComposedEvaluator` evaluates an assignment by slicing the workload into
single-op documents, calling the REAL inner backend once per component, and composing the
results. The physical model is stated, because the numbers only mean something under it: one
engine per op, the chain runs sequentially, so latency and energy are sums over components and
area is the sum of the engines (separate silicon). Everything else — `power_w`, `edp` — is
OMITTED via the ABI's standard absence semantics: average power across a time-multiplexed chain
is not a sum of engine powers, and a metric this wrapper cannot compose honestly is refused,
never approximated. CIs sum (conservative), method is the weakest across components, validity
requires all components valid, the dominant (slowest) component supplies the bottleneck story,
and provenance is `<inner>+composed` with every component's evaluator named — the `+composed`
suffix keeps the inner backend's string as the prefix, so the campaign cache probe accepts the
rows unchanged.

Wiring is deliberately thin: candidate geometry delegates per-op to `generate_width_candidates`
(a composition candidate is exactly N documents every evaluator already accepts); the grid and
agentic strategies gained a `workload` parameter (the one axis whose geometry depends on the
workload); the runner wraps the screening backend and every escalation rung identically; the
composition document is stored under its own document kind (`composition`) — it is not
Architecture IR and is filed as what it is. Everything else — budget latch, resume, escalation
idempotence, composite frontier, stop targets — is untouched and applies as-is.

**Why.** This was the ranked capability gap toward D1's full-SoC ambition: campaigns optimized
one architecture for a whole workload, and `derive`'s uniform width is a single knob. A chained
workload's layers differ by orders of magnitude in MACs (mnist-mlp: 6.4M / 1.0M / 41k), and the
right spend is per-layer. The unit suite pins the shape of the payoff exactly: at equal total
area, widening the HEAVY layer dominates widening the light one — the frontier literally says
"spend area where the MACs are", and the non-uniform point that wins is one a uniform width
sweep cannot even express.

**What was verified.** Unit (9, synthetic inner evaluators — the claims are composition
arithmetic and wiring): full-grid geometry with real per-op arch documents; sliced workloads
are schema-valid single-op IR; sums with CI-sums and weakest-method; component-refused and
unsummable metrics omitted; provenance prefix + per-component naming; typed refusal of a
non-composition arch; objective validation; and a full grid campaign over a 2-op workload whose
every trial equals the sum of its components, whose composition documents land under the
`composition` kind, and whose frontier is exactly {uniform-small, heavy-wide, uniform-wide}
with the wrong non-uniform point excluded. Live (3, real tools): composed(zigzag) at uniform-8
on the ONNX 3-layer chain reproduces D231's whole-chain pin EXACTLY (2,822,445 cycles /
2,023,163,742 pJ — composition arithmetic reproducing the monolithic evaluation, the two pins
failing independently by design); the true 10-class head at width 16 is evaluators/rtl's own
typed NotExpressibleError (lanes divide the OUTPUT dim; 10 admits no 16-lane engine) surfaced
on the sliced layer; and a full campaign on a padded-head chain (784/256/128/16) screens all 8
assignments of {8,16}^3 with real ZigZag — a mixed assignment's latency decomposes exactly into
per-op terms solved from the uniform trials — then escalates the winner through THREE real
Verilator simulations, one per engine, summed: 471,843 cycles at rtl fidelity (471,040 ideal
MACs/lane + 803 measured fill/drain), pinned. This is the first path that measures a multi-op
workload through evaluators/rtl at all: that adapter refuses chains by design, and the per-op
slicing is exactly the decomposition it asks its caller for.

Regression: 1332 passed, 22 skipped; the ONNX/escalation/mixed-fidelity campaign suites re-run
green after the strategy-signature change.

**Implications.** The campaign frame and Flow 2's per-module machinery now meet: an objective
can drive per-component sizing with real-tool escalation, which is the system-level step D1
promised. Residues, named: the width list is global (a per-op width list — e.g. {2,10} for a
10-wide head — is a schema extension away, and the head-refusal test documents why it will
matter); calibration applies at the composed level only (a composed arch hash matches no
residual pool — per-component calibration inside the wrapper is the flywheel extension);
`area_mm2` sums engines but no screening backend here produces a nonzero one yet (ZigZag's
area is 0.0 by construction, D206) — an OpenROAD-rung area objective is the honest way to get
a real area axis, at real cost.

---

## D237. The real-area composition frontier: calibration reaches inside, engines are paid for once, and silicon confirms the claim

**Decision.** Three additions that together turn D236's synthetic payoff claim into a measured
one. (1) **Per-component calibration**: `ComposedEvaluator` takes `calibration_db_path` and
applies D98's flywheel to each engine's raw estimate — keyed by the (workload-slice,
engine-arch) content hashes — BEFORE summing; the composed hash matches no residual pool by
construction, so component granularity is the only place calibration can reach a composition.
The runner passes the path inside the wrapper and skips its own composed-level pass, which
would find no stats under the `+composed` evaluator name and clobber the honest per-component
domains. (2) **Component-level dedup**: assignments share engines, and the store-backed
`CachingEvaluator` cannot serve a partial rung (its covering rule wants every REQUESTED metric
in the stored row; a rung request names latency alongside area, and an openroad row carries
only area+power — measured as 8 placements where 4 engines existed). A request-keyed in-memory
memo of raw component results inside `ComposedEvaluator` serves identical (slice, engine,
mapping, metrics) requests once per instance — sound because the key includes the request
shape; raw so every serving still gets today's calibration. The store cache stays underneath
for coverable requests and resume. (3) The flows/campaign surface already spoke every needed
word; no new tool.

**Why.** With point estimates, the contender set collapses to the single fastest assignment —
a one-point "frontier" measures nothing. The honest widener is D234's calibration CIs: a pool
built at engine widths the campaign never visits makes every campaign point EXTRAPOLATED
(corrected value, conservative interval, D122), the wide per-component intervals sum into wide
assignment intervals, and the CI-aware contender set keeps every assignment alive for the
rungs to settle.

**What was verified.** Unit (2 more): a real CalibrationStore corrects component estimates
(3x family bias) before summing — in-pool assignment tight, one-unmeasured-engine assignment
>3x wider; a campaign with a counting evaluator pays for exactly 4 unique engines across 4
assignments x 2 components. Live, in the physical shell (real ZigZag + Verilator + OpenROAD on
ASAP7, an ONNX-born 8:1-imbalanced 2-op chain, pool at widths {2,4}, campaign over {8,16}^2):
pool ratios 2.986-3.006 (the family bias, again); all four screened assignments carry wide
extrapolated intervals (e.g. 18572 in [11012, 281672] — and the corrected 18572 sits 0.3% from
the 18530 rtl later measured); all four stay contenders and BOTH rungs run all four; exactly 4
placements for 8 component slots; and the composite frontier — latency at rtl fidelity, area
at openroad fidelity — is {(8,8): 18530 cyc / 802 um^2, (16,8): 10306 / 1208, (16,16): 9266 /
1614}, all pinned. The flagship fact: the two mixed assignments are the same two engines
swapped, so their REAL placed areas are equal (1208 um^2 both) — and at that equal area,
heavy-wide is 1.7x faster than light-wide (10306 vs 17490), so (8,16) is off the frontier.
"Spend area where the MACs are", previously a synthetic-model unit claim, now measured end to
end. Regression 1339 passed, 22 skipped; the mixed-fidelity physical suite re-runs green.

**Implications.** Objective -> per-component sizing -> real silicon numbers is one campaign
document now. Residues: composed-level cache hits keep their stored calibration vintage
(stated in the runner); the memo is per-instance (a resumed run re-pays engines whose rung
requests the store cache cannot cover).

---

## D238. Parallel screening: the runner batches, the flows layer supplies the concurrency

**Decision.** `run_campaign_steps` gains `screening_parallelism` (default 1): GRID screening
proposes up to that many candidates per round, gives every miss its durable intent row BEFORE
dispatch, and carries the batch through ONE `evaluate_batch` call. Whether the batch actually
runs concurrently belongs to the injected evaluator — `flux_campaign_step`/`flux_campaign_start`
pass `screening_parallelism` through and inject `ChiaParallelEvaluator`, whose
`evaluate_batch` dispatches each candidate as a Ray task (the same L5/L6 split that evaluator
was built to embody: the campaign package stays CHIA-agnostic). Agentic and generative
strategies ignore the parallelism — proposal t+1 legally depends on outcome t, and batching
them would change what the strategy is. The batch is capped by the evaluations budget (running
rows do not count as spent, so an uncapped batch would overshoot the latch) and by max_trials.
`evaluate_batch` has no per-candidate error isolation, so a failed batch falls back to
per-candidate sequential calls — each in its own try, the poisoned candidate recorded as its
own error trial, and the fallback recorded as a `batch_fallback` event, never silently
absorbed. Stop criteria move to per-batch checks: a no-improvement limit can overshoot by at
most batch_size - 1, stated in the code and the tool docstring. `ComposedEvaluator` gains
`evaluate_batch` with in-batch engine dedup: the batch's unique (slice, engine, mapping,
metrics) components go to `inner.evaluate_batch` in one call, so a Caching/ChiaParallel stack
underneath dispatches exactly the distinct engines concurrently.

**Why.** Composition multiplied the screening bill: {8,16}^3 is already 27 independent trials,
and "standalone agentic work over some time frame" pays it serially today. The batching had to
live in the runner (trial records, budget, resume) while the concurrency had to stay out of it
(layering), which is exactly the seam `evaluate_batch` was designed to be.

**What was verified.** Unit (5): batched grid is result-identical to sequential (same values
by candidate key; batches of 4 then 2 for 6 candidates at parallelism 4, zero sequential
calls); the evaluations budget caps the batch (grant 3, parallelism 8 -> one batch of 3,
budget_exhausted); agentic ignores parallelism (3 sequential calls, no batch surface touched);
a failed batch falls back with isolation (3 ok + 1 error from a poisoned candidate,
batch_fallback event recorded); a composed batch names each of 4 unique engines once in one
inner batch call. Live: `flux_campaign_start` -> `flux_campaign_step(screening_parallelism=3)`
on the ONNX wide-proj family — three REAL ZigZag evaluations as concurrent Ray tasks — lands
bit-for-bit on D231's sequential pins (98958 / 49550 / 24846). Regression: 1339 passed, 22
skipped.

**Implications.** Long campaigns can now spend wall-clock proportional to the slowest batch
member rather than the sum, without touching durability: a SIGKILL mid-batch leaves `running`
intent rows that `classify_interrupted` replays, same as ever. Residue: escalation rungs still
run contenders serially (the cascade's idempotence bookkeeping is per-trial; batching it is
mechanical but was not needed while contender sets stay small).

---

## D239. The capstone chain: one sentence to the pinned silicon frontier

**Decision.** Close the last authoring seam and prove the whole standalone-agentic chain as ONE
run. The seam: `flux_author_objective`'s prompt enumerated the search kinds it may emit and
`composition_width` was not among them — an agent literally could not author a composition
campaign from prose. The prompt now offers it (with the one sentence of per-op semantics), the
node gained the `llm` injection parameter its D235 sibling already had (scripted-proposer
testability), and a second primer landed (below). The capstone integration test then runs the
full chain: prose --qwen--> validated composition Objective --real zigzag vs rtl--> calibration
pool at never-visited widths --campaign--> calibrated parallel screening (parallelism 4, all
four assignments contenders) --rtl + openroad rungs--> composite frontier. The integration
claim is exact: the chain must land on D237's independently-measured pins — same three-point
frontier, same (8,16) exclusion at equal area, same cycles and areas.

**Why.** Every stage existed (D232 authoring, D236 composition, D237 calibrated real-area
escalation, D238 parallel screening) but had never been proven composed; the standing lesson
(D237's cache-covering miss was found by the first full run, not by review) is that the first
end-to-end run finds the real seam. It did, twice: the missing search kind, and a primer-class
authoring miss.

**What was verified.** Unit (3, scripted proposer): the prompt offers `composition_width` and
an authored composition objective passes the real parser with documents attached; an invalid
generative/composition pairing is repaired with the parser's own message in the repair prompt;
a model-echoed (mangled) workload copy is discarded, never trusted. Live (physical shell +
Ollama): the first capstone run failed honestly — qwen dropped `measured_at: "escalation"` on
`area_mm2` even though the prompt's example named exactly that case, which would have made
area a screen metric ranked on ZigZag's constant 0.0. The D153 primer class again: the clause
was rewritten from an example into an imperative RULE ("when screening is zigzag, any
area_mm2/power_w objective MUST carry measured_at: escalation"), after which the capstone
passed three consecutive full runs (~2 min each), every strongly-cued clause landing (kind,
widths [8,16], both metrics, rung order [rtl, openroad], budget) and the final frontier
matching D237's pins exactly: {(8,8): 18530 cyc / 802 um^2, (16,8): 10306 / 1208, (16,16):
9266 / 1614}, latency at rtl fidelity, area at openroad fidelity. The D232 live suite re-runs
green under the revised prompt. Regression: 1342 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** The tool now demonstrably does its stated job end to end: a sentence in, a
real fidelity-labeled per-layer silicon frontier out, with lineage from the frontier back
through the campaign, the calibration pool, and the authored document to the exact prose. The
prose-faithfulness residue (D232/D235) is now the sharpest remaining edge on this chain — the
capstone's own first failure was precisely a faithfulness gap the validator could not see, and
the fix was a primer, not a checker. A checker (backend-capability table at authoring time, or
a second-model cross-examination) is the named next step on this path.

---

## D240. The backend-capability check: authoring learns what the tools can measure

**Decision.** `flux_author_objective` now validates authored documents against a small static
table of what each backend the prompt offers can actually produce — read from the adapters,
not asserted: zigzag emits exactly latency+energy (its adapter never writes an area key), rtl
populates latency only, openroad parses area and power from the placed design. Two rules,
checked after `parse_objective` in the same repair loop: a screen-measured objective metric
the screening backend cannot produce is rejected (with the fix in the message: add
`measured_at: escalation` and a rung that measures it), and an escalation-measured metric no
declared rung produces is rejected (with the rung suggestion). Backends absent from the table
are UNCHECKED — an honest "don't know", never a refusal, so custom backends pass authoring
untouched and the runtime classifier stays the judge. The D239 prompt primer stays: the primer
prevents, the check catches.

**Why.** This is the mechanical half of prose-faithfulness, bought by a real failure: D239's
first capstone run authored `area_mm2` as a screen metric over zigzag — schema-legal,
semantically dead (every screening trial would refuse at runtime). The fix then was a primer;
this makes the mistake a typed authoring-time rejection whose message becomes repair input —
the same pull-it-forward shape as D235's reserved-word check, one layer higher.

**What was verified.** Unit (3 more, scripted proposer): the exact D239 failure document is
rejected and repaired on round 2 with the actionable message in the repair prompt; deferred
area with rungs ["rtl"] only (nothing measures it) is rejected with the rung suggestion; an
unknown-backend document passes authoring in one attempt. Live: the D232 authoring suite and
the D239 capstone re-run green with the check active. Regression: 1347 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** The capability table is authoritative only for the three backends the
authoring prompt names; extending the prompt's backend vocabulary means extending the table —
they live side by side in the same module so the drift is visible in one diff. A registry-level
capability declaration (each adapter stating its own metrics) would be the principled
generalization if authoring ever offers many backends.

---

## D241. Per-op width lists: the head gets its own engine sizes

**Decision.** `search.kind: composition_width` accepts `widths_per_op: {op_id: [ints]}`
alongside (or instead of) the global `widths` list — each op's engine is drawn from ITS OWN
allowed widths, ops not named fall back to the global list, and the grid is the product of the
per-op lists. Validation at parse time (shapes), typed generator errors for an op with no
allowed widths and for a `widths_per_op` entry naming an op the workload does not have. The
authoring prompt documents the field. No JSON-schema change needed — the search object was
left open for per-kind fields by design (D216), with the Objective view validating per kind.

**Why.** Bought by the pinned D236 refusal: mac_array's lanes divide the OUTPUT dim, and the
true MNIST head (K=10) admits engine widths {2, 10} while the heavy layers want {8, 16} — a
single global list structurally cannot express that campaign, which is why D236's live test
had to pad the head to 16 classes.

**What was verified.** Unit (2 more): per-op grid geometry ({8,16} x {4-only} -> exactly two
assignments, engines materialized at every named width including per-op-only ones; uncovered
op and unknown op-id are typed refusals) and objective validation (per-op-only is valid; empty
lists and a bare kind are rejected). Live: the TRUE 10-class MNIST chain — unmodified, no
padding — runs a full campaign with `widths: [8,16], widths_per_op: {mm2: [2,10]}`: 8
assignments screened by real zigzag, head widths really {2,10}, and the winner
(mm0:16, mm1:16, mm2:10) escalates through three real Verilator simulations to 471,843 cycles
— measured EQUAL to the padded-16 pin, and that is arithmetic, not accident: 10 lanes over 10
outputs and 16 lanes over 16 outputs both run one output column per lane, so the schedules are
cycle-identical. The unpadded classifier costs nothing over the padded one; it was just
inexpressible before. Regression: 1347 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** Composition campaigns can now follow each op's own divisibility instead of
forcing a common denominator — the prerequisite for chains with awkward heads, attention
shapes, and any workload whose ops disagree about legal widths. The authored-objective path
knows the field exists; whether qwen uses it well from prose is part of the standing
faithfulness residue.

## D242. CI's cache was dead, not its tests: magic-nix-cache out, GitHub's own cache in

**Decision.** Replace `DeterminateSystems/magic-nix-cache-action` in every CI job with a shared
composite action (`.github/actions/nix-setup`) that (1) deletes the runner's preinstalled
toolchains this repo never uses (~25 GB back on a ~14 GB-free root disk), (2) installs nix via
`nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action` (single-user, so the cache step can read and purge the
store it saves — the pairing cache-nix-action itself documents), and (3) restores/saves `/nix`
through `nix-community/cache-nix-action` against GitHub's own actions cache — no third-party
account required — keyed per shell closure (default / physical / timeloop) on the flake files'
hash. Every job also gained a separate "build the shell" step with `df -h` after it, so an
environment-build failure is visibly distinct from a test failure and disk exhaustion names
itself in the log if it ever recurs.

**Why, with the evidence laid out.** Every CI run since 2026-08-14 failed identically — the
regression job at a consistent ~43 minutes, "Process completed with exit code 1" thousands of
lines into nix build output — across THREE unrelated commits, each green locally at the time
(1318-1347 passed). The one non-code signal in every failing run's annotations:
magic-nix-cache's "Unable to authenticate to FlakeHub" — FlakeHub ended anonymous cache
access, so the action has cached nothing since, and every run cold-built the full closure. The
measured default dev shell runtime closure is 6.0 GB; a cold build additionally materializes
sources, compilers and intermediates on the same root disk that starts with ~14 GB free. The
last green run (2026-07-31) predates both the cache's death and much of the closure's growth.
The job logs themselves need repo-admin auth this machine does not have, so the exact failing
line is unverified — the fix therefore addresses the full evidenced class (no cache + no
disk), and the new split step + df output will pin the exact cause on the next failure instead
of leaving it behind an auth wall.

**What was verified.** Both YAML files parse; the pinned action versions exist upstream and
`cache-nix-action@v7`'s input names were checked against its own action.yml (v7 kept every
input this setup uses). What CANNOT be verified from this machine: an actual green run — CI
triggers on push, and pushing is deliberately not this workflow's to do (the standing
stage-only rule). The next push is the test.

**Implications.** CI runs now depend on GitHub's 10 GB per-repo cache budget shared across the
three shell namespaces (LRU eviction on overflow — a cold rebuild, not a failure). The
gc-before-save cap (8 GB) keeps any single save inside the budget. The nightly jobs
(integration / physical / timeloop) inherit the same setup; the physical shell's or-tools +
OpenROAD from-source build remains the largest closure and the most likely to test the disk
headroom first.

---

## D243. Knowledge mining: facts computed from stores, with the boundary of the claim as a field

**Decision.** New package `knowledge/mining` (`flux_knowledge_mining`) plus the 50th MCP tool
`flux_mine_knowledge`: typed facts computed from campaign and calibration stores — the
Knowledge role finally learning from the Evaluator's own measured history rather than only
from ingested spec text. Five fact kinds: `estimator_bias` (observed prediction/reference
ratio range per residual family), `measured_point` (rung measurements per campaign),
`observed_ratio` (the effect of ONE knob doubling between two measured candidates),
`refusal_pattern` (stored failure messages, grouped verbatim), `frontier_outcome` (completed
campaigns' frontiers with per-metric fidelity labels).

The design center is the requested property — factual, well-pointed, never inviting a wrong
inference — enforced by construction rather than by care:
- **Computed, never asserted**: every number comes from stored rows; statements are generated
  by fixed wording from those numbers; there is no free-text field an author fills in.
- **Measured language only**: "measured", "observed on", "refused with" — never "is",
  "scales as", or "will".
- **The boundary is part of the fact**: every fact carries `scope` (exactly where the evidence
  lives) AND `not_established` (the inference the numbers do NOT license) as FIELDS the
  consumer receives, not documentation.
- **Pointers or it didn't happen**: campaign ids, trial seqs, calibration record ids, content
  hashes — every fact re-derivable from the rows it names.
- Deliberate refusals to mine: no fitted scaling laws (only measured point-pairs and their
  ratio); no screen-phase estimates presented as measurements (they appear only inside bias
  facts, AS the predictions they were); caveated calibration records counted but never pooled
  (mining must not launder what the calibrator excludes, D112); non-done campaigns counted in
  `skipped`, never silently dropped; refusal messages never normalized or clustered (grouping
  two different messages under one pattern is an interpretation).

Supporting additions: `CampaignStore.list_campaigns()`, `CalibrationStore.
evaluator_metric_pairs()`, the package wired into the flake's path list.

**Why.** The last substantial item of the standalone-agentic ranking, now that the stores hold
enough real history to mine (two workload families, silicon measurements, residual pools,
campaign trails). An agent that can ask "what has been measured, exactly where, and what does
it NOT establish" spends budget better than one that starts cold — and the user's stated
requirement (factual, good pointers, nothing that leads to incorrect interpretation) is this
repo's honesty discipline applied to the one place it was missing: the summary layer.

**What was verified.** Unit (8, real stores in tmp, synthetic rows with known values,
asserting the anti-misleading rules themselves): bias ranges with record-id pointers and a
100x caveated outlier NOT pooled; the D106 below-threshold caveat; a range spanning 1.0
makes no direction claim; measured points come only from escalation (the analytic screen
estimate never reads as a measurement); ratios are pairs anchored to two trial seqs with
"scaling law" in not_established; refusals grouped by the exact message; a paused campaign is
counted in skipped, a done one yields a fidelity-labeled outcome. Live (real ZigZag + real
Verilator, the D231 wide-proj family): pool at widths {2,4,64}, calibrated campaign over
{8,16,32} escalating all three widths, then mining — the bias fact's ratios all in the
family's 2.9-3.1x band over exactly 3 record ids; the measured points verbatim equal to the
suite's own independent pins (32833/16417/8209); both doubling ratios at 0.500x with two trial
seqs each; the frontier outcome naming width 32 at rtl fidelity 8209; skipped empty; and no
refusal facts because no refusals happened — mining reports what exists, nothing else.
Regression: 1355 passed, 22 skipped; MCP parity green at fifty tools.

**Implications.** Facts are a return value today: nothing persists or retrieves them yet.
The named next steps on this path are (a) feeding mined facts into the agentic strategy's
prompt and objective authoring (the consumer they were shaped for), and (b) a facts store the
BM25 corpus deliberately does NOT absorb — mined facts and licensed spec text have different
provenance classes, and mixing them would blur exactly the boundary the `pointers` field
exists to keep sharp.

---

## D244. The design-guidance corpus: wisdom in our own words, with its provenance class in every chunk

**Decision.** A third knowledge class joins the corpus: `knowledge/corpus/design-guidance/` —
curated design wisdom for building better RTL/SystemC, hand-written FOR this repository in
original prose, ingested by the existing AsciiDoc connector into the same BM25 index
`flux_knowledge_lookup` already serves. Three documents: memory implementation choices
(flip-flop arrays vs latch arrays vs SRAM macros; port count as a first-order SRAM cost),
multi-port memory composition (replication, banking, multipumping, LVT, XOR-based — with cost
structures, coherence/bypass obligations, and the honest selection rule), and datapath PPA
guidance (parallelism, true-precision sizing, pipelining, activity-driven power). Generation
gained the consumption path: `flux_generate_rtl_module(guidance=...)` and its SystemC sibling
append caller-curated text (e.g. retrieved chunks) to the module prompt as an ADVISORY block —
the verifier stays the judge, so bad guidance costs repair rounds, never correctness.

Three provenance classes now coexist and are kept distinguishable ON EVERY CHUNK, because the
BM25 index retrieves paragraphs alone: verbatim licensed spec text (riscv-unpriv, CC-BY-4.0),
mined measured facts (D243, computed from stores), and now curated guidance — whose every
paragraph states inline whether it is (a) a repo-measured fact with a decisions.md pointer,
(b) a data point reported by a cited source, or (c) direction-only guidance.

The license discipline held under temptation: the requested source — T. Verbeure, "Building
Multiport Memories with Block RAMs" (2019) — sits in a blog repository with NO license file
(all rights reserved by default; checked 2026-08-18, recorded in the corpus PROVENANCE.md
alongside the ACM-copyright LaForest TRETS 2014 paper it builds on). Neither is reproduced:
both are cited, and the techniques are described in this corpus's own words — the same posture
the riscv PROVENANCE records for Arm/JEDEC/PCI-SIG/I2C.

Anti-misleading rules, applied to prose the way D243 applied them to mined facts: no SRAM
scaling formulas or technology constants anywhere — magnitude questions are deferred BY THE
TEXT ITSELF to the real quantification paths (`flux_characterize_memory_level` for CACTI, the
OpenROAD evaluator for placed numbers); the sources' FPGA-measured comparisons are referenced
only as "no technique dominates; measure per design point"; the repo's own measured claims
carry their decision pointers and their scope ("NOT established outside that range") in the
same chunk.

**Why.** The user's ask, exactly: more knowledge to build better/more performant designs —
standards, PPA impact, memory rules, and the named article — under the standing requirement
that nothing invite incorrect assumptions. The Knowledge role previously held spec text and
(since D243) measured facts; design WISDOM — the menu of structures and their cost shapes —
is what a generator consults before the evaluators price a specific choice.

**What was verified.** Unit (6): the XOR cost structure and read-before-write caveat
retrievable through the real index; the selection rule refuses global ranking and defers to
this repo's evaluators; SRAM port-cost guidance points to the CACTI path; measured-here claims
carry D-pointers AND their scope boundary in the same chunk; sources are cited never quoted;
the guidance block reaches the RTL generation prompt exactly when given (real Verilator on
both branches). Live (real qwen + Verilator, two consecutive runs green): chunks retrieved
from the corpus travel through `guidance=` into a real generation of a 4-lane MAC verified on
saturating-range vectors — with the honest observation, recorded in the test, that guidance is
advisory and once COST repair rounds (width-guidance nudged qwen into over-$signed() casts);
the plumbing claims assert unconditionally, convergence branches per the D235 variance
discipline. Regression: 1361 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** Retrieval-fed generation exists but nothing automatic wires it: choosing
WHAT to retrieve for a given spec is the caller's (agent's) judgment, deliberately — an
automatic retrieval step would need its own relevance evaluation before it could be trusted
not to stuff prompts with plausible-but-inapplicable guidance. Whether guidance measurably
improves design quality is an open, testable question (a controlled comparison over a spec
family); the corpus is deliberately small and hand-picked (D3's rule), and grows entry by
entry with the same provenance discipline.

---

## D245. The flywheel closes: mined facts reach the proposers, boundaries attached

**Decision.** D243's facts gained their consumers. `render_facts_for_prompt` (in the mining
package — ONE renderer, so the wording cannot drift between consumers) renders facts as
statement + NOT-established boundary, always together: a fact whose limits get trimmed away is
exactly the incorrect-assumption vector mining exists to avoid, so the boundary is not
optional in the rendering. The campaign package takes an opaque pre-rendered `knowledge`
string (`run_campaign_steps(knowledge=...)`, threaded into the agentic AND generative prompts
like `history` already was) — it stays free of the mining dependency, and the trial row's
`prompt_sha256` already captures exactly what the model saw, knowledge block included. The
flows layer connects the two: `flux_campaign_step(knowledge_facts=[...])` renders and threads
(also exposing D238's `screening_parallelism` over MCP, which the wrapper had not yet passed
through), and `flux_author_objective(facts=[...])` renders the same block into the authoring
prompt so budgets, stop targets and search ranges can be picked against prior measurements.
Grid strategies ignore knowledge — nothing to advise.

**Why.** Mine -> recall -> propose is the loop the Knowledge role exists for: an agent that
knows "zigzag over-predicts ~3x here" and "the frontier last time was width 32 at 8209 cycles"
spends its budget better than one starting cold — but only if the boundaries travel with the
numbers, or the same facts would teach overgeneralization instead.

**What was verified.** Unit (5): the renderer attaches the boundary to every shown fact and
states its cap when it bites (12 shown, "(3 more...)"), dict and Fact forms rendering
identically; the runner threads knowledge into the agentic prompt (block + fact + boundary all
present) and NO block appears without knowledge; the generative prompt carries the same block
(asserted on a forced-fallback proposal — the honesty contract intact); authoring receives the
rendered block. Live (real tools + real qwen): a grid campaign measures wide-proj with zigzag
+ rtl escalation; `flux_mine_knowledge` turns its store into facts (the frontier outcome
carrying rtl 8209); a SECOND campaign's agentic proposer — real qwen — receives those facts in
every real proposal prompt (number, boundary and all, asserted per prompt), completes the
3-width space, and every LLM-picked trial is recorded non-deterministic with prompt hashes
that include the knowledge block. Regression: 1366 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** The four-role loop is now closed in code: Evaluators measure, Mining turns
measurements into bounded facts, proposers and authoring consume them, campaigns record what
was consumed. What is deliberately NOT claimed: that fact-fed proposing IS better — that is
the same open, testable question as D244's guidance efficacy, and the two share an
experimental design (controlled comparison, same spec/search family, with and without). The
knowledge parameter is caller-driven at every surface; automatic mining-into-every-campaign
would need relevance selection first, same reason as D244's deliberate non-wiring.

---

## D246. The review cycle: three audits, and the rot they found is now structurally harder

**Decision.** A full review/cleanup pass over code, tests, CI and documentation — three
parallel audits (code hygiene, test inventory, documentation drift), then one fix pass. The
findings and their fixes, by severity:

**CI coverage was broken in three ways nobody could see.** (1) The D237 flagship and D239
capstone tests were runnable in NO shell in the repo: both escalate through rtl (Verilator,
default shell only) AND openroad (physical shell only) — skipped green in the nightly forever,
and they would have ERRORED if naively added to the physical job. The physical shell now
carries Verilator, the frontier test joined the physical job's list, and a new meta-test
closes the class: every openroad-gated integration file must be in that list or Ollama-gated
(no CI job supplies Ollama — the disclosed hole) — the exact guard the repo's own
glob-not-list meta-test already applied to the sweep, extended to the explicit lists.
(2) The nightly sweep FAILED every night: ten integration files drove real Ollama with no
guard, contradicting ci.yml's own "tests needing Ollama skip themselves" claim — a permanently
red job is a dead signal for the ~85 files it does cover. All ten now skip honestly (module
marks; per-test marks inside the MCP live suite, which has 24 Ollama-free tests that must keep
running). (3) The regression suite's 22 skips were audited and are benign parametrization
pruning — and notably, tests/unit + tests/conformance contain NO environment-conditional
skips at all, so nothing in the always-on suite can silently degrade.

**Duplication that had already drifted.** Eight copies of `_ollama_up` (one at a different
timeout; all blind to OLLAMA_HOST — silently skipping for anyone with a remote server), three
copies of the wide-proj ONNX builder, and two byte-identical copies of the chain builder —
the last being a duplicated ORACLE: D239's "reproduces D237's pins" claim was a claim about
two copies of the same literal staying identical. One `tests/integration/_helpers.py` now owns
all three (OLLAMA_HOST honored); one conftest fixture replaces nine identical Ray teardowns.

**Counts in prose rot; the fix is pointers, not corrections.** The MCP tool count was wrong
in SEVEN places with FIVE different values (fifteen, sixteen, thirty-one, thirty-six, fifty —
the last written by this session two decisions ago; the real number is 49, AST-verified).
Every count is now either correct or, better, replaced by a pointer to the parity-guarded
list (docs/agent-surface.md) — the same D95/D96 lesson the tool.py docstring now states
instead of exemplifying.

**Documentation had rotted against D216-D245 across ~27 files.** The worst: the evaluator-ABI
backends table documented 6 of 13 backends and marked two shipped ones "not started"; the
roadmap and two calibration docs still sent readers to build a Hammer synthesis rung that
D225 superseded with the already-working OpenROAD; ir.md claimed three document kinds and
"schema-only" dynamism; stores.md had no CampaignStore. All rebuilt against the log, the
roadmap gained a current ranked next-actions list and a D216-D245 arc section, and
knowledge/mining gained the README it alone lacked.

**Code hygiene.** Zero TODO/FIXME/debug leftovers existed (the audits' strongest positive
finding); fixed what did: five library unused imports, seven test unused imports, an empty
collected test file, two docstring pointers at deleted files, the repo's only two
private-API cross-package imports (`_composite_frontier`/`_frontier_payload`, now public
exports), four missing `__all__` entries, nine undeclared intra-repo pyproject dependencies
(with the flux-cli omission documented as deliberate — a metadata cycle), and a redundant
.gitignore.

**What was verified.** Regression 1367 passed, 22 skipped (+1: the new CI meta-test); MCP
parity and the CI/flake structural tests green; the touched live files re-run green (9/9)
confirming the consolidated helpers and conftest teardown behave identically; every count
claim re-verified by AST or registry, not by grep.

**Implications.** Deferred with eyes open, recorded here rather than lost: the 15-copy
default-LLM-model literal in flows/chia_nodes (two names for one constant), the 5-copy
`_format_history` in search/agentic (with drifted failure wording, and a shared `_engine.py`
it was never folded into), the unit suite's 31 local `_result` fixtures, usage-guide coverage
of the D216-D245 surface, and the conformance suite's unguarded Docker-Hub dependency
(intentional — a guard would let the load-bearing suite rot green — but it fails illegibly on
a rate limit). The audits' meta-lesson is already encoded where it can act: lists that must
track reality get parity tests, prose gets pointers.

## D247. The cold-cache bootstrap ratchet: fail-and-save beats timeout-and-lose

**Decision.** Two structural fixes to D242's CI cache, taught by its first real run (job
95673371891, sha 9b5b9b6). (1) **Internal caps below job timeouts on every shell-build
step**: the run showed the composite setup working (disk freed, cache plumbing, 46s) and the
cold dev-shell build consuming the full 90-minute job timeout — CANCELLED, and a cancelled
job kills the post-run cache save, so 90 minutes of building banked nothing and the next run
started cold again: a loop that never converges. Each build step now wraps `nix develop
--command true` in a `timeout` set below its job's limit and FAILS with a legible message
("partial store is cached; re-run to resume") — post steps run on failure, the partial store
is saved, and the next run resumes from it. A bootstrap ratchet: the first push or two may
fail at the build step by design, then the jobs stay green and fast. (2) **`github.run_id`
in the cache primary key**: an exact-key hit is never re-saved, so a PARTIAL first save under
the stable flake-hash key would freeze the cache at partial forever — the ratchet could bank
its first click and no other. Restore matches the newest cache by prefix; the purge deletes
superseded caches after each new save lands. The regression job timeout also rose to 120
minutes: the nixchip toolchain (verilator, yosys, systemc, cacti, dramsim3) has no public
binary cache and builds from source on 4 vCPUs; steady state with a warm cache is minutes.

**Why.** The D242 diagnosis (dead cache + disk) was right but incomplete: with disk fixed,
the build simply does not FIT one cold run, and both the cancellation semantics of GitHub
timeouts and the no-resave semantics of exact cache hits silently defeat incremental
progress. Both defeats are now structural non-events.

**What was verified.** Both YAML files parse; the CI structural tests pass (6, including the
D246 meta-test). What cannot be verified from this machine, stated as before: an actual green
run — and the honest expectation to hand the user is one or two legible build-step failures
per shell flavor before convergence, not silence.

**Implications.** Cache churn: every run uploads a fresh store snapshot (~2-3 GB compressed)
and purges the previous one — the price of resumable bootstraps, bounded by the gc cap. If
the physical shell's or-tools+OpenROAD build exceeds even the ratchet's patience across
several nightlies, the next lever is a prebuilt substituter (cachix or a FlakeHub account),
recorded here as the known escalation path.

## D248. The efficacy experiment: knowledge feeding measured, and the honest answer is "not yet"

**Decision.** The roadmap's rank-1 item, run: `flux/experiments/knowledge_efficacy.py` (a new
`experiments/` directory for measured comparisons whose outcome is unknown before running —
tests assert known invariants; experiments answer open questions). Two controlled
comparisons, each arm differing in exactly one variable, real qwen2.5-coder:7b throughout.
(A) Design guidance in generation prompts (D244's question): four precision-trap specs x 3
reps per arm, real Verilator verification — guided 7/12 verified successes (mean 1.71
attempts) vs plain 8/12 (1.38). (B) Mined facts in agentic proposals (D245's question):
{4,8,16,32}^2 composition space, budget 4 of 16 points, 4 campaigns per arm — facts arm mean
best latency 21,709 cycles (range 13,981-30,989) vs cold 16,697. Full numbers and per-run
records in `flux/docs/knowledge-efficacy-report.md`.

**Conclusion, bounded.** No measurable benefit at these sample sizes; point estimates lean
negative in both comparisons. Established: with THIS model on THESE families, knowledge
feeding does not help — the D244/D245 opt-in, never-auto-wired design is right by measurement
now, not caution. NOT established: that it cannot help — larger models, harder families,
better chunk selection, and recommendation-shaped rendering are all untested, and the harness
re-asks the question in one command. The qualitative observation matches D244's live test
(guidance once cost repair rounds): a 7B model treats advisory prompt text as context to
paraphrase, not policy to execute.

**Implications.** The roadmap entry is retired as MEASURED, not built; the follow-on worth
money is re-running the harness when the local model changes, not tuning prompts against a
model that ignores them.

## D249. The prose-faithfulness checker: a small judge, caged by rendering, guards, and votes

**Decision.** `flux_check_prose_faithfulness` (50th tool): second-model cross-examination of
an authored artifact (objective or design spec) against its requesting prose — the semantic
half of prose-faithfulness, after D240's mechanical half. Three design commitments plus two
measured additions: (1) the judge reads a CODE-RENDERED summary of the parsed document, never
raw JSON — every semantic field, fixed wording, completeness unit-guarded — with enum values
and metric names GLOSSED in plain words ("composition_width (per-op/per-layer engine
widths)", "area_mm2 i.e. silicon area (placed)"), because a judge comparing prose to raw
vocabulary measured a faithful document as missing its area objective; (2) tri-state verdict
(faithful | unfaithful | unknown) — an unparseable judgment is UNKNOWN, never a silent pass;
(3) the check is advisory, transcript preserved.

Getting a 7B judge reliable was itself an empirical arc, every step bought by a live failure:
the initial holistic judgment hallucinated mismatches on faithful documents (4/4 after a
naive primer); restructuring the output to per-requirement CHECKS (asked -> quoted document
line -> matches) gave code two mechanical guards — a failed check whose sides carry the same
value (case/punctuation/suffix-normalized) refutes itself, and one quoting a document line
that does not exist judged text nobody showed it — and the glosses removed the vocabulary
chasms. Measured single-vote reliability landed at ~75-85% per direction; `votes=` majority
voting (ties to unfaithful, the cautious direction; mismatch union; all-unknown stays
unknown) buys the rest.

**What was verified.** Unit (7, scripted judges): summary completeness for both artifact
kinds (a dropped field is a judge blind spot no prompt can fix); verdict parsing with prose
and summary both in the prompt; both mechanical guards dropping self-refuting and fabricated
checks while the honest mismatch survives; majority voting counting only decided votes and
unioning mismatches; unparseable -> unknown with the bounded retry; exactly-one-artifact
required. Live (real qwen judge): the faithful capstone-style document passes at votes=5 and
the D239-class mutilation (area dropped, widths changed, rungs dropped) is caught at votes=3
with the mismatch named — FOUR consecutive full runs green after the guards+votes, from a
baseline of 0/4 on the faithful direction mid-arc. MCP parity green at fifty tools (49 + this
one — the count D246 corrected now holds at the new value). Regression: 1374 passed, 22
skipped.

**Implications.** The checker is advisory and measured as such: a lone qwen-7b vote is
~75-85% reliable, stated in the docstring rather than hidden, and votes are priced
accordingly (a votes=5 check costs ~1-2 minutes of local model time). Wiring it as a gate
inside the authoring loops (author -> check -> repair-with-mismatches) is the natural
follow-on, best taken after a stronger local judge model exists — D248's lesson applies to
judges too.

## D250. The facts store: recall across time is re-derivation, never trust

**Decision.** `FactStore` (in the mining package) plus `flux_recall_facts` (51st tool) and a
`facts_db_path` parameter on `flux_mine_knowledge`: mined facts persist and recall — the
mine -> store -> recall lifecycle the roadmap ranked third, kept deliberately SEPARATE from
the BM25 corpus (measured facts and licensed text are different provenance classes, D243/D244;
one index would blur the boundary the `pointers` field keeps sharp). Three commitments:
identity is content (a fact's id hashes kind + statement + pointers, so re-mining unchanged
stores is idempotent — INSERT OR IGNORE, never a duplicate); staleness is CHECKABLE
(`verify()` re-mines the store each fact points at and labels it `intact` — the same
statement is still derivable — `dangling` — the source store is gone or unreadable — or
`superseded` — the store's evidence moved on; re-derivation, not a row-existence probe,
because the statement is computed FROM the rows and anything weaker could bless a fact whose
numbers moved); and recall is exact filtering by kind/substring, honest about not being a
ranker.

**What was verified.** Unit (4, real stores): the full lifecycle with idempotent re-mining;
kind and case-insensitive substring filters; a deleted source store makes every fact
`dangling` (the file is really unlinked); new evidence makes the old measured-point fact
`superseded` while re-mining stores the new statement alongside — recalled together, one
superseded and one intact. Live: covered in D251's chained test. Regression: 1381 passed, 22
skipped; MCP parity at fifty-one tools.

**Implications.** Campaigns can now consult accumulated facts without re-mining, at the cost
the design makes explicit: recall-with-verify pays a re-mine per fact source. The knowledge
loop is closed end to end at every lifetime scale — within a campaign (D245), across
campaigns in one session (D243), and now across sessions.

## D251. System-level composition: engines sized in compute AND memory, and infeasibility is a fact

**Decision.** `search.kind: composition_system` — every einsum op's engine is sized in BOTH
compute width and a named memory level: the per-op grid over (widths x sizes_kb) points.
Geometry delegates to `generate_joint_candidates` (the proven single-arch width x memory
generator), so every engine is a full Architecture IR document — which is why the ENTIRE
composed machinery (ComposedEvaluator, per-component calibration, request-keyed memo,
batching, agentic strategy) runs unchanged; the new code is one generator, objective
validation, a strategies branch, and the runner's composition test generalized from one kind
to the `composition_` prefix. The authoring prompt gained the kind (the D239 seam lesson,
applied preemptively this time).

**Why.** The step from per-op engines toward the original full-SoC ambition: heterogeneous
blocks where a small op deserves a small buffer — the memory analog of D236's "spend area
where the MACs are". Deliberately scoped to zigzag/rtl-servable metrics: placed-memory AREA
via CACTI is the named follow-on (its adapter needs exactly-one-memory archs with
word_width_bits — real plumbing, not wired glue), and no screening backend produces a
meaningful area today.

**What was verified.** Unit (3): the per-op (width x size) grid with both knobs landing in
each engine document; objective validation of all three required fields; a full campaign over
an interior-optimum pricing where the trials themselves prove heterogeneous memory wins (big
op takes the big buffer, small op refuses to pay for one) and the frontier carries the
heterogeneous point. Live (real ZigZag, probed before written): the memory model makes
heterogeneity REAL, two ways at once — mm0's tensors do not fit a 4KB gbuf (all 8 such
assignments are typed refusals, recorded as failed trials, never fudged), and among feasible
points the minimum feasible buffer is energy-optimal PER OP (mm1 at 4KB beats mm1 at 32KB at
both widths, measured from the trials). The frontier contains {mm0: 16x32KB, mm1: 16x4KB}
and no frontier point wastes buffer on the small op. The same test then runs D250's
lifecycle on the campaign store: the infeasibility itself becomes a persisted, recallable,
verified-intact refusal fact carrying all 8 trial pointers. One chain, 37 seconds — the
request-keyed component memo collapses 16 trials to the unique engine evaluations.
Regression: 1381 passed, 22 skipped; the composition and mining live suites re-run green.

**Implications.** The system-level path is open: per-op width x memory today; the recorded
next steps are CACTI-backed memory area as an escalation rung (word_width_bits + per-level
extraction), interconnect joining the per-op space (the noc_topology axis exists but has
never met composition), and per-op size/width lists (the D241 mechanism, directly
applicable). Composition kinds now share one prefix; a third kind is a generator and a
validation branch away.

## D252. The CACTI area rung: real silicon on the system frontier, without corrupting energy

**Decision.** `composition_system` campaigns can declare `area_mm2` measured at a `cacti`
escalation rung: the frontier becomes latency/energy (ZigZag, screened and calibrated) plus
REAL per-engine SRAM macro area (CACTI), per-metric fidelity-labeled — the full PPA story at
system level. Three pieces. (1) The system generator attaches `word_width_bits` (new optional
search field, validated) to the searched level of every engine — CACTI refuses to guess the
SRAM interface width, and the generator is the one place that knows the buffers are being
sized for characterization; ZigZag ignores the extra attribute (probed: the 49478 pin
reproduces). (2) `MemoryLevelAreaRung` wraps the cacti evaluator with the two transformations
the adapter's own contract demands: EXTRACTION (the adapter refuses multi-memory archs — it
characterizes one macro; the wrapper hands it a copy holding only the searched level plus
`tech`) and METRIC NARROWING to `area_mm2` alone — the trap caught at design time rather than
by a bad frontier: CACTI's `energy_pj` is PER-ACCESS energy and its `power_w` is leakage, and
under the objective's workload-energy name the composite's deepest-rung-wins rule would have
silently preferred them over ZigZag's workload energy. (3) The runner mounts the wrapper for
`cacti` rungs on composition campaigns, inside the same component cache and composed
machinery as every other rung — engine areas sum like any other area.

**What was verified.** Unit (4 more): the generator attaches `word_width_bits` only when
asked; validation of the new field; the wrapper hands a fake inner a single-memory arch with
tech and the narrowed request (asserted from inside); a full campaign with a fake CACTI that
REFUSES multi-memory archs — the wiring test fails loudly if extraction ever stops — whose
composite frontier carries per-assignment area sums at cacti fidelity. Live (real ZigZag +
real CACTI 7, probed before written: gbuf at n28 with 64-bit words is 0.005077 mm2 at 4KB and
0.036663 mm2 at 32KB): the three-metric system campaign screens the {8,16}x{4,32} per-op
space, the cacti rung covers every contender, and the composite frontier carries area at
cacti fidelity with the screened metrics at screen fidelity — every frontier point keeps the
small op at 4KB, the big op at its infeasibility-floor 32KB, and the frontier area equals the
SUM of the probed per-engine macro areas (0.041740 mm2), pinned. Memory dominates the area
story exactly as the design-guidance corpus says it should: the 32KB macro alone is ~90x the
placed 8-lane datapath. Regression: 1385 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** All three PPA axes now compose at system level from real tools: Verilator
cycles, ZigZag workload energy (calibrated), CACTI macro area — plus OpenROAD datapath
area/power on the physical path. Named residues: datapath area (OpenROAD) and memory area
(CACTI) both spell `area_mm2` and CANNOT yet appear in one objective (the deepest-covering
rule would pick one, not sum across rungs — cross-rung metric composition is a distinct
mechanism, deliberately not improvised here); the extraction wrapper is mounted for
composition campaigns only (a plain memory_size campaign with a cacti rung would still hit
the multi-memory refusal — same fix, when wanted); interconnect remains the axis composition
has never met.

## D253. Sub-22nm CACTI: characterize at a native node, scale by a published factor, cite it

**Decision.** CACTI cannot model ASAP7-class nodes and now says so honestly: the answer to
"is CACTI running ASAP7?" was NO on both sides — the D252 memory areas were 28nm planar
(the arch's own declared n28, interpolated by CACTI's ITRS models), while the OpenROAD rung
hardcodes ASAP7 at 7nm, making D252's ~90x memory-vs-datapath aside a cross-technology
comparison (corrected here: the like-for-like 7nm figure is ~15x). Three changes. (1) A
FLOOR guard in the cacti translator: below 22nm — probed for real, 0.022um runs, 0.016um and
0.007um fail outright — the refusal is typed and names the sanctioned route instead of
letting CACTI crash unparseably. (2) `flux_evaluator_cacti.scaling`: area scaling factors
vendored VERBATIM from Stillmaker & Baas 2017 (Integration VLSI J. 58, Table 4, the 7nm
row; openly hosted by the authors), with the honesty block attached to the module and to
every scaled result: these are ITRS logic-geometry factors applied to an SRAM macro
(approximate), and per Sarangi & Baas 2021 they OVERESTIMATE scaling at the newest nodes —
a scaled 7nm area is, if anything, optimistic. Nodes the table does not carry are refused,
never interpolated (verified: the vendored row's ratios reproduce the printed matrix within
its own rounding). The DeepScaleTool spreadsheet was fetched and inspected first but its
factors are computed in VBA whose exact branchwork could not be faithfully reconstructed
(my reimplementation did not reproduce the tool's own displayed values) — so the fully
printed primary source won. (3) `MemoryLevelAreaRung(scale_from_nm=)` + the
`cacti_scale_from_nm` search field (validated against the published nodes >= 22): the rung
characterizes at the native node, scales the area, downgrades the method to ANALYTIC (a
scaled simulation is a model estimate), and appends `+scaled` plus the full citation to
provenance.

**What was verified.** Unit (3): the vendored factors (32->7 = 7.8; 45->32 ratio vs the
printed 2.2), non-table refusal, and the rung asserted from a fake inner (characterized at
n32, scaled 0.078 -> 0.01, method downgraded, citation present; same-node pass-through
untouched). The old n16-parses translator test was REWRITTEN to the new contract — it pinned
arithmetic that real CACTI crashes on at runtime. Live probe: an n7 chain engine's gbuf
through the real scaled rung — 32KB = 0.006145 mm2, 4KB = 0.000853 mm2, `cacti7@real+scaled`,
citation in provenance. Regression: 1393 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** ASAP7-class system campaigns get consistent-technology memory area by
opting in (`cacti_scale_from_nm: 32`); the numbers say they are scaled, by how much, and by
whose published data. Delay/energy scaling factors exist in the same paper (its Table 5
polynomials) and are deliberately NOT vendored yet — area was the asked-for axis, and each
factor family deserves its own verification pass.

## D254. Generated ASAP7 SRAM macros: the engine and its buffer place together

**Decision.** `flux_evaluator_openroad.sram_macro.generate_sram_macro` — black-box SRAM
macros for the ASAP7 flow, the real answer to "can we generate an ASAP7 lib": ASAP7 ships no
public SRAM macros, and the standard open-flow workaround (bsg_fakeram, BSD-3, as used by
OpenROAD-flow-scripts — inspected, not vendored: internally it is CACTI-plus-scaling, which
this repo already has with citations) is a GENERATED macro. Ours emits a LEF with a real
footprint sized from the caller's area (in practice: real CACTI scaled per D253), a liberty
with area/pins/one conservative timing arc and the REQUIRED provenance sentence embedded as
a comment ("a macro whose numbers cannot say where they came from is exactly the
unlabeled-model artifact this repo refuses to produce"), and a Verilog black-box stub.
`run_ppa_flow(macros=[...])` threads them through both tools: yosys reads the stubs so
instances survive synthesis; OpenROAD reads the macro LEF/liberty and places the block with
Hier-RTLMP before standard-cell placement.

Two real-tool lessons, both measured: this OpenROAD has no `macro_placement` command
(Hier-RTLMP's `rtl_macro_placer` replaced it), and MPL-0005 rejects macro pins that are not
on the track grid — the generator now puts every pin rect centered on M4's real
OFFSET+n*PITCH (0.003 + n*0.048, wire width 0.024, read from the vendored tech LEF), with a
unit test asserting the on-grid property for every generated pin.

**What was verified.** Unit (5): geometry/interface math (4KB x 64b -> depth 512, 9 address
bits, 853 um2 at the D253-scaled area), non-power-of-two refusal, every pin on the M4 grid,
too-short-for-its-pins refusal, provenance embedded. Live (real Yosys + OpenROAD on ASAP7):
an 8-lane int8 MAC datapath instantiating its generated 4KB buffer places as ONE design —
reported area 1260 um2 = macro 853 + datapath ~407 (matching D225's 401 um2 8-lane pin
within placer noise), positive slack at 2ns with the conservative macro timing. The D246
meta-test caught the new openroad-gated file missing from the physical CI job — the guard
working as designed — and the file is now in the job's list. Regression: 1393 passed, 22
skipped.

**Implications.** Engine area can now mean datapath PLUS buffer in one placed number from
one flow at one technology — dissolving D252's cross-rung area residue for designs that
route memory through the macro path. The named next step is campaign wiring: an
openroad-rung variant whose per-engine RTL instantiates the engine's own gbuf macro
(generated from its searched size via D253), making the system frontier's area a single
placed total. Timing in the macro liberty is placement-grade by construction and says so;
routed-flow interaction with macro OBS geometry is untested.

---

## D255. The scaling checked: correct arithmetic, physically impossible density, and a bitcell floor

**Decision.** The D253 scaling was audited on request, in three steps. (1) **Arithmetic**:
raw CACTI@32nm (4KB = 0.006656 mm2, 32KB = 0.047928 mm2) divided by the vendored 7.8 factor
reproduces the reported 7nm values exactly — the mechanism computes what it claims. (2)
**Independent physical cross-check**: converting to area-per-bit and comparing against the
published TSMC N7 high-density 6T bitcell (0.027 um2, WikiChip Fuse 2019; Samsung 7nm
0.030 um2 corroborates the scale) showed the 32KB scaled macro at 0.0234 um2/bit — DENSER
than a periphery-free bitcell array, which is physically impossible — and the 4KB at 0.0260,
marginally below the bitcell. Against a realistic macro (bitcell / 60-75% array efficiency,
~0.036-0.045 um2/bit) the scaled values were ~1.5-1.9x optimistic. This QUANTIFIES the
caveat D253 declared qualitatively: logic-geometry factors over-scale SRAM, whose scaling
famously lags logic below 22nm. (3) **The fix is a physical invariant, not a fudge**:
`scale_area_mm2` gained a bits-aware BITCELL FLOOR — the scaled macro area is clamped to
`bits x published bitcell area` where a verified anchor exists (only 7nm today; nodes
without an anchor never clamp — no guessed constants), and the provenance note says when
the clamp engaged and cites the anchor. The composed rung passes the level's bits. Floored
results: 4KB = 884.7 um2, 32KB = 7077.9 um2 — both at exactly bitcell density, i.e. still
the OPTIMISTIC edge (100% array efficiency), now stated as a bounded lower bound instead of
an impossible number.

**What was verified.** The audit chain above, each number from a real run or a cited
publication; unit (1 more): clamp value + citation in the note, above-floor pass-through,
no-anchor-no-clamp; the D254 live flow test re-pinned to the floored macro (884.7 um2;
combined placement 1292 um2) and re-run green. Regression: 1394 passed, 22 skipped.

**Implications.** Scaled 7nm SRAM areas are now bounded-optimistic with the bound cited: the
true value lies between the floor (bitcell density) and ~1.7x it (realistic array
efficiency). A caller needing tighter numbers needs a real 7nm macro compiler, which is
exactly what does not publicly exist for ASAP7 — the honest end of this road. The
array-efficiency band itself (60-75%) is folklore-grade and deliberately NOT encoded
anywhere numbers flow; it appears only here as context.

---

## D256. "Can CACTI support ASAP7?" — patching its tech tables is rejected; its own efficiency report is adopted

**Decision.** The user's question — add or use CACTI's tech-parameter files to support ASAP7
— was investigated to a decision, not a shrug. Findings: (1) our CACTI is HP's cacti 7,
cloned and built from source by the adapter, so patching its compiled-in technology tables
IS mechanically possible — and is REJECTED on physics grounds: those tables feed planar-CMOS
analytical equations, and substituting 7nm FinFET parameters into planar equations is
exactly the method the literature built FinCACTI to replace (Shafaei et al. 2014, Best
Paper, IEEE ISVLSI — TCAD-calibrated FinFET modifications to CACTI's equations, later
updated against ASAP7 in published work). (2) FinCACTI/PCACTI itself is UNOBTAINABLE through
official channels today — both USC hosts (sportlab and atrak download pages) are dead; the
vendoring route is blocked on availability, recorded for revisit. (3) What CACTI CAN
